bugs.title: STP references to stale interfaces remain when the port group changes
bugs.symptoms: When you change an existing port group, e.g., from one 100G to 4 25G, STP still reports the old interfaces when you issue 'show stp' from the CLI. Additionally, the new interface does not display in the CLI.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when making changes to the port group mode, e.g., from one 100G to 4 25G mode.
bugs.impact: -- The old interfaces still display when running 'show stp' from the CLI. -- The new interface does not display when running 'show stp' from the CLI. -- You must manually remove the old interfaces and add the new interface via the CLI.
bugs.workaround: You must manually remove the old interfaces and add the new interface using the CLI.

bugs.title: On system controller failover, tenant mgmt IP's may be unreachable for several minutes.
bugs.symptoms: During a system controller failover, tenant management IP's may be unreachable for several minutes. Once the ARP entry for the tenants IP times out in the upstream router, it will be re-populated with the correct MAC after the failover and begin working again.
bugs.conditions: This occurs during a system controller failover due to the ARP entries not being updated for the tenants.
bugs.impact: The tenant management IP may be unreachable for several minutes after a system controller failover. Once the upstream ARP entry has timed out, the tenant management IP will be reachable again.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround, and once the upstream ARP entry has timed out, the tenant management IP will be reachable again.
bugs.fix: The tenant orchestration layer will now cause Gratuitous ARPs to be sent for the tenant management IPs when a system controller failover happens. The restores tenant management IP connectivity quickly after a system controller failover.

bugs.title: VLAN name change is not allowed once a tenant is launched
bugs.symptoms: When you change the VLAN name on a rseries (R2x00 or R4x00) Appliance, the BIG-IP tenant does not honor the name change.
bugs.conditions: -- One or more tenants are running on a rSeries (R4x00 or R2x00) platform. -- A VLAN name is changed for a VLAN that is in use by a running tenant.
bugs.impact: Changing the VLAN name after a tenant is launched and reassigning that VLAN removes the interface in TMM.
bugs.workaround: Set the VLAN name to the initial name that the tenant used when it was launched. Or, if you need to change the name of the VLAN, delete the tenant and redeploy.

bugs.title: Link stats misrepresentation on interfaces in Autonegotiate mode when link goes down
bugs.symptoms: When an interface is configured for autonegotiation and then this link goes down, the port-speed and duplex-mode attributes are not cleared and are still displayed.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the interface is configured for autonegotiation mode, has port-speed and duplex-mode populated from a prior active connection, and the link subsequently goes down
bugs.impact: Users might misinterpret the current state of the interface.
bugs.workaround: To accurately determine the link status, users should rely on the state oper-status field.

bugs.title: TLS Extended Master Secret support
bugs.symptoms: TLS Extended Master Secret may not be negotiated on some versions.
bugs.conditions: NA
bugs.impact: TLS Extended Master Secret is unavailable.
bugs.workaround: No
bugs.fix: Updated versions include TLS Extended Master Secret support.

bugs.title: Null bytes or non-ascii characters are present in velos.log
bugs.symptoms: Null bytes are created in the log files.
bugs.conditions: Abrupt restarts may cause this issue.
bugs.impact: Grep considers the log file as a binary file.
bugs.workaround: Use ‘-a’ option in grep command.

bugs.title: Port-profile changes when tenants are in the deployed state
bugs.symptoms: Port-profile changes are not being blocked when tenants are in the deployed state.
bugs.conditions: Changing port-profile on a system with a tenant in the running-state is deployed.
bugs.impact: Tenants may not come up after the system reboots.
bugs.workaround: For each tenant in the deployed state, move the tenant running state to provisioned and back to deployed. Then the tenant will then come up and function properly.

bugs.title: Error message is not displayed when user configures more than 3 DNS servers in ConfD CLI or webUI
bugs.symptoms: When user tries to configure more than 3 DNS server entries in F5OS-A using command "system dns servers server" or from webUI, no error message is displayed. System allows only 3 DNS servers, but user will be allowed to configure more than 3.
bugs.conditions: Configure DNS server in F5OS-A using ConfD CLI or webUI.
bugs.impact: No impact. Even though user configures more than 3, system will take only 3 entries.
bugs.workaround: NA

bugs.title: tmstat-merged logs only applicable to chassis no longer appear in appliance logs
bugs.symptoms: In prior versions, tmstat-merged logs on appliance had references to slot and cluster-IP, which only apply to chassis.
bugs.impact: Extra log messages that do not apply to appliances were found in the logs.
bugs.fix: Log messages only applying to the chassis no longer appear in the appliance tmstat-merged logs.

bugs.title: Unable to configure or disable both cipher suites and TLS/SSL protocols on the management interface in F5OS.
bugs.symptoms: Administrators are unable specify allowed cipher suites/TLS protocol versions for the F5OS management interface (HTTPS). The configuration options for cipher suites and TLS versions are not exposed
bugs.conditions: 1. Applies to F5OS management interface (HTTPS access) 2. Occurs when attempting to configure TLS settings for the httpd service via ConfD CLI.
bugs.impact: 1. Cipher suites cannot be disabled or restricted. 2. Cannot enforce TLS protocol version restrictions for management access.
bugs.fix: Issues is Fixed.

bugs.title: Missing/defective DIMM not reported sufficiently to end user
bugs.symptoms: If a memory DIMM is missing or defective, the system does not report the situation sufficiently to the user through the "show system health" API.
bugs.conditions: A memory DIMM becomes missing or defective.
bugs.impact: The platform is operating at less than the shipped memory configuration, which could impact the number of tenants deployed on a system.
bugs.workaround: Refer to the AOM PEL log for details of the missing and/or defective DIMM.

bugs.title: ISO file not copied during clean install from USB DVD/CD-ROM device
bugs.symptoms: ISO file is not copied over to /var/import/staging during a clean install with DVD devices.
bugs.conditions: Clean install with DVD devices.
bugs.impact: ISO file not copied to /var/import/staging and importing any other image will cause problems with further upgrades or downgrades.
bugs.workaround: Explicitly copy the ISO file which ever used for clean installation to the device to the location /var/import/staging.

bugs.title: F5OS Does Not Support Configuring Intermediate CA with Server Certificate
bugs.symptoms: With Apache 2.4.6, SSLCertificateFile does not support having an intermediate CA with the server certificate
bugs.conditions: -- Configure '/system/aaa/tls/config/certificate' with intermediate CA and server certificate -- Configure CA-bundle (root CA) -- Enable verify-client -- Try to log in via browser with p12 or Curl with the client certificate. -- Login fails due to SSLCertificateFile not accepting both the intermediate CA and the server certificate.
bugs.impact: The customer is unable to configure the server certificate correctly with the intermediate CA
bugs.fix: With F5OS 200, the Apache version was updated to 2.4.8, which allowed SSLCertificateFile to have both the intermediate CA and the server certificate

bugs.title: IPV6 packets are fragmented on F5 r2K/r4K platforms.
bugs.symptoms: IPv6 packets are fragmented on F5 r2K/r4K platforms, which causes a slight performance degrade.
bugs.conditions: Fragmentation is seen for IPv6 packets.
bugs.impact: Performance is degraded when passing IPv6 traffic. There is not any functionality impact because of this issue other than the performance impact.

bugs.title: ConfD CLI not prompting user to confirm the LDAP bind password
bugs.symptoms: On ConfD CLI, the system is not prompting the user to confirm the given LDAP bind password to make sure the entered password is correct.
bugs.conditions: Setting LDAP bind password in ConfD-CLI using R2R4/R5R10 appliances.
bugs.impact: The issue does not impact the functionality of setting the LDAP bind password. When the user sets up the LDAP bind password, they need to be careful when entering to make sure the password is correct.
bugs.workaround: The workaround is to use the webUI to set up the LDAP bind password.

bugs.title: Missing rpm-ostree status output in QkView diagnostic data
bugs.symptoms: "rpm-ostree status" output is missing from QkView file.
bugs.conditions: When QkView data is collected from the F5OS device.
bugs.impact: "rpm-ostree status" output is missing from qkview file.
bugs.workaround: Manually run command "rpm-ostree status" on the system.
bugs.fix: The QkView collection has been updated to include the output of the rpm-ostree status command.

bugs.title: Show tenants displays trust-mode parameter on R5K/10K/12K
bugs.symptoms: The output of "show tenants" displays the trust-mode parameter on R5k/10k/12k appliance platforms. This parameter is not applicable on these platforms.
bugs.conditions: Displays only on R5K/10K/12K
bugs.impact: No functional impact.
bugs.fix: The trust-mode parameter will not be displayed on the unsupported platforms.

bugs.title: On rSeries FIPS system live upgrade, cavium_n3fips (liquidsec_pf_vf driver) may fail to come into operational state
bugs.symptoms: After a reboot of the system in live upgrade, tenants that were running earlier might not change to a running state. This is due to the HSM board driver stuck in SAFE_STATE instead of OPERATIONAL_STATE. In some cases, the driver changes to an operational state after some amount of time (approximately 10 minutes). But this time might vary upon detection of reset/link failure in the hardware. In some other systems, the driver becomes stuck in SAFE_STATE indefinitely.
bugs.conditions: Live upgrade/reboot of the rSeries FIPS system with F5OS-A. You may observe the below logs in dmesg- [ 964.105021] liquidsec_pf_vf_driver 0000:ca:00.0: We might have a link issue... resetting [ 964.113688] liquidsec_pf_vf_driver 0000:ca:00.0: RESETTING FIRMWARE... CAUTION
bugs.impact: Running tenants goes to pending state when this issue occurs in a live upgrade.
bugs.workaround: Check contents of cavium_n3fips file as shown below. [appliance]# cat /proc/cavium_n3fips/driver_state HSM 0:OPERATIONAL_STATE If the driver changes to an operational state, perform "docker restart fips-support-pod" to help in recovering. But if the driver state is still "HSM 0:SAFE_STATE", you may need to perform a power cycle reboot (but this will not guarantee recovery).

bugs.title: Automatic LOP recovery failure when stuck in bootloader mode.
bugs.symptoms: System controllers may have significant loss of functionality such as: - System Inventory displays nothing. - System controller 1 is in Faulted state. - No Slot info in Partition default. - Lost connection to Controller Floating IP. - Admin account login becomes impossible.
bugs.conditions: Faulty fantray or interrupted LOP firmware update may cause bootloader mode.
bugs.impact: System controller malfunction.
bugs.workaround: If caused by a faulty fantray, it should be removed or replaced to prevent the LOP from going into bootloader mode again. A power cycle can be used to restart the LOP and get it out of bootloader mode.
bugs.fix: If a system controller's LOP is in bootloader mode during booting, the automatic firmware update process will recover it.

bugs.title: VELOS system controller fails to PXE boot when network-range-type is RFC1918
bugs.symptoms: If the network-range-type is set to RFC1918, a VELOS system controller will fail to PXE boot from its peer system controller, reporting an error message "Unable to locate configuration file".
bugs.conditions: - The Internal Chassis Networking range (network-range-type) is set to RFC1918 (the default is RFC6598).
bugs.impact: Unable to PXE boot the system controller.
bugs.workaround: Log into the peer controller (the one NOT being PXE booted) as root, and navigate to the /var/images/pxelinux.cfg directory. In the directory, locate the file whose name is six hex characters ("0a", followed by two digits, followed by "07"), and rename the file to uppercase. For example: [root@controller-1(VELOS):Active ~]# cd /var/images/pxelinux.cfg/ [root@controller-1(VELOS):Active pxelinux.cfg]# ls -l 0a* -rwxr--r--. 2 root root 352 Oct 7 15:14 0ae107 [root@controller-1(VELOS):Active pxelinux.cfg]# mv 0ae107 0AE107 [root@controller-1(VELOS):Active pxelinux.cfg]#

bugs.title: TPM status may not reporting during PXE install
bugs.symptoms: The tpm-integrity-status parameter may incorrectly be displayed as "Unavailable" when running the ‘show components component platform command’.
bugs.conditions: When performing a PXE install downgrade, SIRR DB does not persist across OS updates. This leads to mismatch SIRR and BIOS version; SIRR DB may not have the info about the newer BIOS version, causing inconsistencies in TPM validation.
bugs.impact: This may impacting TPM integrity validation.
bugs.workaround: Contact F5 support for further assistance and more details.

bugs.title: No error when DNS server is configured with port other than 53
bugs.symptoms: F5OS allows to configure DNS port other than 53 although it is not being used by DNS resolvers.
bugs.conditions: Configuring DNS port other than 53.
bugs.impact: No Functional impact.
bugs.fix: F5OS will not allow to configure DNS port other than 53. Along with this, F5OS also restricts number of DNS servers count to 3.

bugs.title: WebUI limitation when enabling LLDP on multiple interfaces
bugs.symptoms: LLDP must be enabled individually on each interface on the webUI.
bugs.conditions: Occurs when a user attempts to enable LLDP on multiple interfaces simultaneously.
bugs.impact: No functional impact. However, enabling LLDP interface-by-interface can be time-consuming.
bugs.workaround: Enable LLDP individually on each required interface.
bugs.fix: With the updated design, users can enable or disable LLDP on multiple interfaces simultaneously.

bugs.title: LLDP is allowed to configure on interfaces when virtual wire is enabled
bugs.symptoms: LLDP is allowed to configure on interfaces although virtual wire is enabled.
bugs.conditions: 1) Enable virtual wire on interface. 2) Attach interfaces to a lag. 3) Enabled LLDP on the interfaces.
bugs.impact: When virtual wire is enabled, BIG-IP will function in transparent mode and is not expected to see interfaces on either side. With this issue, F5 interfaces will be visible when LLDP is enabled.
bugs.workaround: Do not configure LLDP on the interfaces when virtual wire is enabled.

bugs.title: Adding support for TLSv1.3
bugs.symptoms: No support for TLSv1.3
bugs.conditions: No support for TLSv1.3
bugs.impact: Security concern due ot lack of compatibility to enable TLSv1.3
bugs.fix: Add the capability to configure TLSV1.3 as well as TLSv1.2 in F5OS

bugs.title: SSH cryptographic algorithm update
bugs.symptoms: SSH algorithms not following best practices.
bugs.impact: Unexpected impact.
bugs.fix: SSH algorithms now following best practices.
bugs.behavior: Deprecated SSH ciphers are not accepted by the SSH service.

bugs.title: Log levels adjusted for tmstat rsync messages about non-critical partial transfers
bugs.symptoms: The rsync failures are logged as ERROR level events (priority="Err") even for non-critical partial transfers. The following return codes have been moved to INFO level logs: rc=23: Partial transfer due to error rc=24: Partial transfer due to vanished source files rc=25: The --max-delete limit stopped deletions
bugs.impact: This creates excessive alarm noise in environments where sporadic partial transfers are benign and expected.
bugs.fix: This issue is fixed.

bugs.title: VELOS/rSeries does not have infield diagnostic capability
bugs.symptoms: VELOS/rSeries does not have infield diagnostic capability
bugs.conditions: NA
bugs.impact: Users cannot run on demand diagnostics
bugs.workaround: NA
bugs.fix: Added a new feature capability for performing in-field diagnostics

bugs.title: Multiple CVEs in SQLite package
Malformed JSON Output for DNS Server State Queries in ConfD CLI
bugs.symptoms: The display JSON option on the CLI interface displays badly formatted JSON output for the API "show system dns servers server state address"
bugs.conditions: Always when the display JSON option is used on the CLI
bugs.impact: No functional impact

bugs.title: BIG-IP tenants created before F5OS-A 1.3.0 may be allocated a smaller disk than required
bugs.symptoms: If the BIG-IP tenant is created before F5OS-A 1.3.0 with default storage size, the displayed size values in "show tenants tenant" are not correct. They will be displayed as "0".
bugs.conditions: Happens when the BIG-IP tenant is created before F5OS-A 1.3.0 with default storage size and upgrades to F5OS-A 1.5.1 (or a later version).
bugs.impact: No effect on BIG-IP tenant's functionality.
bugs.workaround: From F5OS-A 1.4.0, the user does not need to adjust the size unless the user needs a bigger size. The right/minimum size will be auto-allocated when the state is changed.

bugs.title: DMA Agent crash after SEP file mapping error
bugs.symptoms: When DMA Agent is unable to map the SEP block for a newly deployed tenant it may crash during shutdown.
bugs.conditions: Insufficient resources to deploy the tenant.
bugs.impact: The crash occurs on shutdown, it has no impact.

bugs.title: F5-PLATFORM-STATS-MIB::diskPercentageUsed not available.
bugs.symptoms: The diskPercentageUsed OID is not available. snmpwalks/getnext of diskUtilizationStatsTable will not return diskPercentageUsed. snmpget of diskPercentageUsed will fail with a no Such instance error. snmptable of F5-PLATFORM-STATS-MIB:diskUtilizationStatsTable shows a question mark (?) for diskPercentageUsed.
bugs.conditions: Snmpget of diskPercentageUsed
bugs.impact: The disk percentage used statistic is not available via SNMP.
bugs.fix: Support for disk percentage used statistic is added via SNMP.

bugs.title: Some nuisance messages are sent to the platform log after every authentication configuration change
bugs.symptoms: Messages similar to the following may be added to the platform log after every authentication configuration change: 2023-08-03T09:43:49.150901+00:00 appliance-1 authd[8]: priority="Info" version=1.0 msgid=0x3901000000000149 msg="System's IPv6 management address isn't configured.". 2023-08-03T09:43:49.157934+00:00 appliance-1 authd[8]: priority="Info" version=1.0 msgid=0x3901000000000092 msg="LDAP server:" server="ldap://ldapserver.example.com:389". 2023-08-03T09:43:49.157951+00:00 appliance-1 authd[8]: priority="Info" version=1.0 msgid=0x3901000000000096 msg="LDAP SSL:" ssl="off".
bugs.conditions: The user makes a change in system aaa authentication.
bugs.impact: There are nuisance messages in the platform log.
bugs.fix: Nuisance messages will be printed only when relevant (LDAP configuration changes, for example).

bugs.title: Tenants on rSeries system will not deploy, stuck in "Starting" state, with status "Not ready: containers with unready status: [compute]"
bugs.symptoms: Tenants fail to start. - F5OS reports the tenant status as "Starting" - F5OS reports the tenant instance status as "Not ready: containers with unready status: [compute]"
bugs.conditions: - rSeries appliance - DNS search domain for system is configured with an uppercase letter in a domain, e.g.: r5900# show system dns state search system dns state search [ Example.com ]
bugs.impact: Tenants will not start.
bugs.workaround: Modify the DNS search domain list so that all entries contain only lowercase letters. On an r2000 or r4000 series appliance, reboot the system. On an r5000 or r10000 series appliance, either reboot the system or set the tenant to a "provisioned" state and then back to "deployed".

bugs.title: Help string mismatching between GUI and CLI for port 8888
bugs.symptoms: In allowed IP configuration there is help string mismatched between CLI and GUI.
bugs.conditions: Check help for allowed ip in CLI and GUI
bugs.impact: Online help for port 8888 is inconsistently referred to as either "RESTCONF" or "tcp/udp (8888)".
bugs.fix: Help string is consistent between CLI and GUI for port 8888 in allowed-ip configuration.

bugs.title: Remove unused nslcd.service file
bugs.symptoms: 'systemctl status nslcd' shows that nslcd is inactive when it is in fact active
bugs.conditions: This issue is usually seen while troubleshooting LDAP auth on the system. The unused nslcd.service file gives the false impression that nslcd is not running.
bugs.impact: Leaving the unused nslcd.service file intact has resulted in several unnecessary escalations because this file gives the false impression that nslcd service is not running, when in fact nslcd runs inside a container
bugs.workaround: Remove unused nslcd.service file from F5OS.
bugs.fix: Removed unused nslcd.service file from F5OS

bugs.title: Tcpdump performed with an interface filter on VELOS or rSeries will show broadcast traffic from all interfaces
bugs.symptoms: When performing a tcpdump in VELOS or an rSeries appliance, a traffic capture limited to a specific interface will show broadcast traffic hitting other interfaces.
bugs.conditions: - VELOS platform or r5000 / r10000 / r12000 series appliance - Running a packet capture on a specific interface (e.g. 1/1.0 or 1.0)
bugs.impact: This can cause confusion or impede troubleshooting when unexpected broadcast traffic is seen in a capture such as ARP or Miscabling Protocol traffic.
bugs.fix: This issue is now corrected.

bugs.title: Documentation Added for VCC Terminal Server
bugs.symptoms: Previous documentation failed to clearly explain the purposes of vcc-terminal-server.default and vcc-terminal-server.main, their differences, and the expected system impact if either service is not running.
bugs.fix: Documentation was added to the Vcc-Terminal-Server README to describe vcc-terminal-server.default and vcc-terminal-server.main, including their purpose, differences, and system impact if either service is not running.

bugs.title: VELOS Tenant console utility virtctl is missing from default shell path.
bugs.symptoms: The virtctl utility for accessing tenants consoles is not in default shell path.
bugs.conditions: Applies to versions prior to VELOS v2.0 where virtctl is not in default shell path.
bugs.impact: Pre VELOS v2.0, use /usr/share/omd/kubevirt/virtctl.
bugs.workaround: Prior to VELOS v2.0, use /usr/share/omd/kubevirt/virtctl VELOS 2.0 and greater virtctl exists in default path /usr/local/bin.
bugs.fix: VELOS v2.0 and later version virtctl exists in default path /usr/local/bin.

bugs.title: VM events are not captured inside the log file
bugs.symptoms: The VM logs seen on kubernetes events will not be recorded in the log file. The log file k3s_events is helpful in identifying the life cycle of the VM.
bugs.conditions: K3s events related to BIG-IP VM are not captured in k3s_events log.
bugs.impact: No functional impact.
bugs.fix: Capturing the events in the log may help in debugging.

bugs.title: R2000/R4000 silent reboot
bugs.symptoms: R2xxx/R4xxx system experiences a silent reboot. This is caused by a compatibility issue between the system and the solid-state storage device.
bugs.conditions: NVME fails to initialize after multiple reboots. (1) The following matching signature is found in the system event log: Ex: MCA Error-Reporting Registers Capture. Bank: 6 Core: 0 STATUS Register: 0x0419 Value: 0xb980000000000e0b MCA Error-Reporting Registers Capture. Bank: 6 Core: 0 MISC Register: 0x041b Value: 0x0000000000180000 (2) The NVME SSD installed in the system is a 480GB Micron NVME SSD, model 7450_MTFDKBA480TFR . ex: Model: Micron_7450_MTFDKBA480TFR
bugs.impact: 1.System will reboot by its own 2.System is unresponsive
bugs.workaround: Follow the workaround steps described in K000151762: rSeries 2000/4000 systems with NVME SSD may fail to initialize after multiple reboots, available at https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000151762
bugs.fix: This issue is fixed in the BIOS version 1.00.160 and later.

bugs.title: OpenShift cluster failure due to disk exhaustion from oversized log file's
bugs.symptoms: When log files in system grown several gigabytes(GB) and exhaust the disk space, resulting in OpenShift cluster failures.
bugs.conditions: When log rotation is configured on a daily basis and a log flood occurs in the system.
bugs.impact: The log file size can increase by several gigabytes during a flood event, potentially exhausting available disk space.
bugs.fix: The log rotation job configured to run hourly instead of daily to prevent log files from growing excessively large. This will ensure timely rotation and manage file sizes more effectively.

bugs.title: Unable to launch tenant, as VF interface is getting incorrect name while attaching to tenant.
bugs.symptoms: On r2x00/r4x00 related systems, tenant launch fails with an error in ConfD tenant status leaf: "[default/virt-launcher-bip1-1-9sblf:sriov-net3-bip1]: error adding container to network "sriov-net3-bip1": failed to set up pod interface "net7" from the device "x557_4": failed to set netlink MAC address to 00:94:a1:db:bd:0c: resource temporarily unavailable" Linux network manager udev rules and sriov cni try to access the VF and change the interface name of VF. During this process, VFs fail and unable to retrieve. Thus, resource temporarily unavailable error occurs.
bugs.conditions: On r4x00 or r2x00 based systems: 1. In kubectl get pods -A output, the tenant pod goes into Init:0/1 state. default virt-launcher-bip1-1-t6rkh 0/1 Init:0/1 0 36s 2. And in kubectl events, "resource temporarily unavailable" occurs on one of the VFs. 3. In /sys/class/net folder unable to see the below VF interfaces. Instead, some interfaces point to ensp* names which are wrong. Actual result should be as follows: [root@appliance-1 ~]# ls /sys/class/net apigw-dummy-1 lcd sfp_7 sfp_p6v0503 veth0c09f23b veth6cec172f vethea3619d5 x557_p1v1100 x557_p3v1902 br_appliancenet lcd-intf sfp_8 sfp_p7v0900 veth2765115 veth80370796 vetheccdd5fb x557_p1v1101 x557_p3v1903 cni0 lo sfp_p5v0100 sfp_p7v0901 veth3f32fd86 veth82a8440b vethf4081a48 x557_p1v1103 x557_p4v1d00 default-intf mgmt sfp_p5v0101 sfp_p7v0903 veth4ab82fc6 veth8cda0b4d x557_1 x557_p2v1500 x557_p4v1d01 docker0 mgmt0-system sfp_p5v0102 sfp_p8v0d01 veth50d18b0 veth9e8b2e8c x557_2 x557_p2v1502 x557_p4v1d02 dummy0 sfp_5 sfp_p6v0500 sfp_p8v0d02 veth5fe12ffd vethac6590f8 x557_3 x557_p2v1503 flannel.1 sfp_6 sfp_p6v0502 sfp_p8v0d03 veth64783052 vethb688f03e x557_4 x557_p3v1901
bugs.impact: Tenant launch is unsuccessful and unable to connect to the tenant console or tenants' management connection.
bugs.workaround: 1. Move tenants to configured state 2. Remove ice, iavf drivers using the following commands, a. "rmmod /lib/modules/3.10.0-1160.71.1.F5.el7_8.x86_64/updates/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/ice/ice.ko" b. "rmmod /lib/modules/3.10.0-1160.71.1.F5.el7_8.x86_64/updates/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/iavf/iavf.ko" 4. Load ice and iavf drivers using the following commands a. "insmod /lib/modules/3.10.0-1160.71.1.F5.1.el7_8.x86_64/updates/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/ice/ice.ko" b. "insmod /lib/modules/3.10.0-1160.71.1.F5.1.el7_8.x86_64/updates/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/iavf/iavf.ko" 5. Run config_ice_vfs.sh script present in /usr/omd/scripts/ folder using - "sh /usr/omd/scripts/config_ice_vfs.sh" 6. Wait until script is completed and VFs are created correctly. 6. Move tenants to running state and check the running state of tenant, after some time.

bugs.title: Failed to register/deregister logs observed when tenants are deleted
bugs.symptoms: Deploy two BIG-IP Next tenants and one BIG-IP tenant. After deleting the running tenants in the system, we can see error logs flooding. There are multiple register and deregister failed error logs observed. This is because when a tenant is deleted in ConfD, it is deregistered automatically, but when a tenant is deleted in ConfD, the pod persists, and is still trying to make calls to api-svc-gateway. bugs.title: Platform-deployment script logs are now captured in both its dedicated log file and the systemd journal
bugs.symptoms: The platform-deployment script used bare echo statements for all output, meaning log messages were not persisted to a dedicated log file and were not captured in the systemd journal. This made it difficult to troubleshoot platform service deployment issues (e.g., container startup failures, registry setup, OS rebase errors) after the fact, as the output was only visible in the service status and could be lost on rotation or reboot.
bugs.conditions: Any F5OS-A or F5OS-C system running the platform-services-deployment service during upgrade/downgrade, reboot, or service start/stop operations.
bugs.impact: Reduced observability during platform service deployment. Operators had limited ability to diagnose historical deployment failures, Docker Compose errors, or registry setup issues because log messages were transient and not written to a persistent, searchable location.
bugs.workaround: Prior to this fix, operators could manually inspect systemctl status platform-services-deployment.service -l for recent output, but historical logs were not reliably available.
bugs.fix: Added structured logging to the platform-deployment script. All output is now timestamped and written to a dedicated log file (/var/log/platform-deployment.log) with logrotate support, and simultaneously forwarded to the systemd journal via StandardOutput=journal on the service unit. This enables operators to use both journalctl -u platform-services-deployment and the persistent log file for troubleshooting platform service deployment issues

bugs.workaround: The user should wait a few minutes after issuing the BIG-IP Next tenant 'delete' command for the tenant to be deleted properly before proceeding with system interrupt operations (rebooting/upgrading/power cycling/changing port modes/licensing/network switching). Command to check tenant is deleted: kubectl get pods -A The above command lists all Kubernetes pods; ensure no pods are starting with the tenant name.

bugs.title: VELOS management LAG may bridge traffic between management interfaces during LACP negotiation
bugs.symptoms: When the management interfaces of VELOS system controllers are configured in a LACP LAG, the VELOS system may incorrectly forward some ethernet frames ingressing one management interface out the other management interface. This behavior occurs during the period between when an interface links up and when the system completes LACP negotiation and adds the interface to the LAG. This can result in management switches incorrectly learning non-VELOS MAC addresses as being present on the VELOS management LAG interface.
bugs.conditions: - VELOS system - Management interfaces configured in LACP LAG
bugs.impact: VELOS management interfaces incorrectly forward non-VELOS frames from one management interface out the other, causing upstream switches to learn non-VELOS MAC addresses as being present on the VELOS management LAG interface.
bugs.workaround: Configure the upstream switch to be an LACP lag first, then configure the VELOS system MGMT interfaces to use an LACP lag.

bugs.title: Debug logging may not capture all relevant messages due to systemd journal log throttling
bugs.symptoms: When enabling very verbose logging on an F5OS system, some log messages may not be logged due to systemd journal log throttling. When this occurs, a messages such as the following will be present: Jan 01 00:42:47 appliance-1 journal: Suppressed 42047 messages from /system.slice/docker.service
bugs.conditions: - F5OS system - Enabling debug logging, e.g. enable debug logging for LDAP authentication
bugs.impact: Log messages required to debug a problem are not captured in the system logs.
bugs.workaround: For LDAP debug logging: 1. Log into the system via SSH as root 2. Stop the system-managed 'nslcd' daemon by removing its control file: rm /etc/auth-config/nslcd For a VELOS partition, log into the system controller where the partition is active, and use: rm /var/F5/partition<partition ID>/auth-config/nslcd 3. Wait a few seconds (for the system to notice the file deletion and stop the running nslcd instance). 4. Start nslcd manually and pass "-d" (or "-dd" or "-ddd" or other parameters, as desired). For a VELOS partition, the container name will be "partition<partition ID>_name-service-ldap, rather than "name-service-ldap". docker exec -it name-service-ldap /usr/sbin/nslcd -d | gawk '{ print strftime("[%FT%T%z]"), $0 }' | tee /var/tmp/nslcd-debug.log The system will kill this nslcd process any time an administrator make configuration changes to authentication settings (including changing a role's "remote-gid" mapping). At that point, the administrator will need to re-do these steps again to restart debug logging. 5. When debugging is complete, stop the foreground nslcd process with Ctrl-C. Re-enable the system-managed instance by recreating the control file removed in step 2: touch /etc/auth-config/nslcd For a VELOS partition: touch /var/F5/partition<partition_ID>/auth-config/nslcd

bugs.title: When configuring SNMPv3 users, require passwords be set when corresponding auth/privacy protocol are specified
bugs.symptoms: A backup taken on version 1.8.x, where SNMP v3 users were set up without a privacy/auth password, fails to restore on version 2.0 because the newer version requires a privacy password to be present.
bugs.conditions: The issue occurs when an SNMP v3 user is configured with a auth/privacy protocol but without a auth/privacy password on version 1.8.x, and the backup of that configuration is restored after upgrading to version 2.0.
bugs.impact: The backup restore fails, leaving the system unable to recover its previous configuration after an upgrade to version 2.0. This forces the user to manually reconfigure all settings from scratch, resulting in potential downtime and loss of the original configuration.
bugs.workaround: Before upgrading to version 2.0, ensure that all SNMP v3 users configured with a privacy protocol also have a privacy password set. This will make the backup compatible with version 2.0's validation requirements and allow the restore to complete successfully.

bugs.symptoms: When the port mode is mismatched on a Front Panel QSFP port, it can cause port interface flapping on other ports.
bugs.conditions: A port mode mismatch, such as a 100GE optic installed when the port is configured for 40GE operating mode. This did not occur on earlier versions so it might be detected after you upgrade to an affected version.
bugs.impact: The status on other interfaces may incorrectly show ‘down’ when the interface is ‘up’.
bugs.workaround: Do not operate in a mismatched mode.
bugs.fix: Updated FPGA firmware is required for the fix.

bugs.title: Rate limit XBAR to sum of speeds of used interfaces
bugs.symptoms: Dropped packets in Gearbox. (tmctl -d blade gbx_stat)
bugs.conditions: - F5 r5000, r10000, or r12000-series appliance - Passing traffic when the sum of the speeds of enabled and used interfaces is less than 100G.
bugs.impact: Dropped packets.
bugs.fix: Rate limit XBAR to avoid dropping packets in Gearbox when using interfaces with speeds less than 100G.

bugs.title: A blade may fail to join the Kubernetes cluster if another blade is offline.
bugs.symptoms: In pre F5OS-C v2.0 software version, if a blade is offline in the Kubernetes cluster and a new blade tries to join the Kubernetes cluster, the addition of the new blade to Kubernetes cluster will fail.
bugs.conditions: This can happen when an existing blade in the Kubernetes cluster is offline, or in a failed state.
bugs.impact: New blades will not be able to be added to the Kubernetes cluster, until the offline blade is either recovered or removed from the Kubernetes cluster.
bugs.workaround: The workaround is to bring the failed blade back online in the cluster, or to remove the failed blade from the cluster. Once this done the new blade will be able to join the cluster.
bugs.fix: With the upgrade to K3S in v2.0.0 and newer F5OS-C releases, it is no longer required to have all blades online in the cluster to add a new blade.

bugs.title: Partition RESTCONF may return an incomplete response for f5-cluster:cluster/nodes/node
bugs.symptoms: When querying f5-cluster:cluster/nodes/node in a partition, it succeeds for 1000 calls, but then starts returning an incomplete response.
bugs.conditions: This only happens on chassis with at least one empty slot. Each time that cluster/nodes/node/<blade>/state/tenant-memory is requested on an empty slot, an internal queue will hold on to that request. When the queue is full, requests will stop working.
bugs.impact: After the symptom starts, cluster/nodes/node cannot be queried successfully until partition services are restarted.
bugs.workaround: Modify queries to avoid requesting tenant-memory on empty slots. For example, do not use the top-level cluster/nodes/node, but instead use cluster/nodes/node/blade-1.
bugs.fix: Fixed platform-stats-bridge to no longer query blades that are not present or ready.

bugs.title: Unable to add rSeries device IP to 'known-hosts' file
bugs.symptoms: Trying to add a rSeries device's IP to a 'known-hosts' file using the CLI command 'file known-hosts known-host' fails.
bugs.conditions: If the remote host is running F5OS-A-1.8.0, then adding that device's IP to 'known-hosts' file using the CLI command 'file known-hosts known-host' fails.
bugs.impact: File export/import to remote rSeries device from a local rSeries device using secure mode will fail.
bugs.workaround: File export/import to remote rSeries device from a local rSeries device can be done using other supported protocol such as https.

bugs.title: LCD UI contains missing data or report incorrect OS version after an OS downgrade
bugs.symptoms: When the OS on a system is downgraded (For example, from F5OS-A 1.7.0 to F5OS-A 1.5.2), the LCD may no longer report the system’s hostname and management IP address. It may also continue to report the OS version prior to the downgrade.
bugs.conditions: When a rSeries appliance OS has been downgraded (For example, from F5OS-A 1.7.0 to F5OS-A 1.5.2).
bugs.impact: No functional impact. The hostname, management IP address, and OS version are correctly reported by ConfD or through the GUI.
bugs.workaround: When the OS is downgraded on a system, the LCD UI does not automatically revert to the version provided by the downgraded OS. As a result, some LCD UI features may no longer be available after the downgrade. To force the LCD UI to be downgraded, follow these steps: 1) Log in to the system as a root user. 2) At the Linux prompt, issue the following command: `docker exec -it platform-fwu psf call PUT:firmware/lcd/ui updatePolicy=different`. 3) Wait 60-90 seconds for the LCD UI update to complete. 4) At the Linux prompt, issue the following command: `docker exec -it platform-hal psf call POST:lcd/reboot waitForBootup=true`. 5) Wait 60-90 seconds for the LCD to complete a reboot. A clean install in the lower version of F5OS-A, for example, 1.5.2, may also restore the functionality of the new lcd-ui firmware.

bugs.title: Setting LDAP search 'base' after 'ldap-group' is already configured for a role affects the role mapping
bugs.symptoms: If you have set up a 'ldap-group' for a specific role on F5OS, but you did not configure the 'base' for the LDAP search until after it is committed, the role mapping will not appear in ldap-gid-map.txt.
bugs.conditions: 1. Define a 'ldap-group' mapping for a role in F5OS. For example: appliance-1(config-role-admin)# system aaa authentication roles role admin config ldap-group cn=my_group appliance-1(config-role-admin)# commit Commit complete. 2. Configure the LDAP search ‘base’ path *after* step #1. For example: appliance-1(config)# system aaa authentication ldap base ou=Group,dc=local appliance-1(config)# commit Commit complete.
bugs.impact: Role mapping is not stored in ldap-gid-map.txt, so users with that mapping will be unable to access the system.
bugs.workaround: Remove the configuration for 'ldap-group' for the role and then re-configure it after the 'base' has been configured.

bugs.title: BX520 tcpdump throughput improvement
bugs.symptoms: The BX520 blades have more throughput than the BX110, but the tcpdump utility cannot keep up with the amount of tcpdump traffic on the BX520 blade.
bugs.conditions: BX520 tcpdump throughput is quite low compared to BX110 blades, about half of BX110 when it should be double to 3x that of BX110 since BX520 has 4x throughput as BX110.
bugs.impact: Slower tcpdump from dropping packets when using system diagnostic tcpdump in the confD cli.
bugs.fix: Now the line-dma-agent is servicing the DMs on NSO/TAM fast enough for the TCPDUMP higher-throughput traffic on BX520.

bugs.title: When telemetry exporter is not reachable, logs to enable send_queue or retry will be printed in platform.log
bugs.symptoms: When telemetry exporter is not reachable, logs to enable send_queue or retry will be printed in platform.log.
bugs.conditions: Logs will be printed only when configured telemetry exporter is not reachable.
bugs.impact: No functional impact.
bugs.workaround: Ensure the exporter is reachable.

bugs.title: AOM Network configuration silently fails if duplicate IP address is used
bugs.symptoms: When setting the IP address in AOM to an IP address already in use in the network, the configuration silently fails.
bugs.conditions: -- Configuring SSH AOM network settings -- Setting the IP address to an address already in use
bugs.impact: The AOM network configuration fails without alerting the user.

bugs.title: F5OS displays an incorrect error if the admin tries to set a password before committing a new user
bugs.symptoms: F5OS reports that a password was rejected and displays the configured password policy if the admin tries to set a new user’s password before the new user has been added to the system.
bugs.conditions: The admin tries to set a password for a user that has just been configured but not yet committed.
bugs.impact: The administrator could mistakenly think that the selected password is inadequate. But the actual problem is that the user has not been committed to the system yet.
bugs.workaround: When creating a new user, admins must commit the new user before setting a user’s password.

bugs.title: Resource-admin is unable to perform SCP.
bugs.symptoms: Resource-admin is unable to perform SCP.
bugs.conditions: When trying to use SCP with resource-admin for the available virtual paths.
bugs.impact: Resource-admin cannot perform SCP file transfers.
bugs.workaround: Though SCP fails, the file upload/download API works for file upload/downloads.
bugs.fix: Permissions for resource-admin to perform the SCP file transfer were added.

bugs.title: 100G-LR and 100G-LR4 (Innolight and Coherent) optics can fail to link
bugs.symptoms: The 100G-LR and 100G-LR4 optics can fail to link on bringup.
bugs.conditions: No known special conditions. This issue can happen when the link is initially brought up.
bugs.impact: The link is down and can't be used. The link needs to be reset. Reboot or reload the FPGA to re-initialize the front panel link.
bugs.workaround: A fix for this issue is in F5OS-C-1.8.1 EHF2 and newer. The fix for this issue is also included in F5OS-C-2.0.0.
bugs.fix: Data was being transmitted before the optic had finished its power-up. Fix was to modify the SDK to check optic interrupts and wait until all interrupts are clear before proceeding with RX initialization.

bugs.title: Timestamps in PEL/SEL Output Align with Timezone
bugs.symptoms: In Platform Event Log (r10k/r5k) and System Event Logs (r4k/r2k) there was a difference in how the timestamps were reported. In r4k/r2k appliances, a time zone suffix was added causing confusion with when events occurred.
bugs.conditions: On F5OS appliance running 1.8 or lower the output from the different platforms is is different. Output format for r10k/r5k: [root@appliance-1:Active] ~ # docker exec platform-hal psf call GET:lop/pel direction | event | sequence | sequenceNext | severity | severityId | slotID | slotId | source | timestamp -------------+----------------------------------------------------+----------+--------------+----------+------------+--------+--------+--------+---------------------- Na | ASW_3 action: fan step 3 | 52239 | 52240 | Info | 6 | 255 | 255 | AOM | 11/05/2024 01:00:20 Output format for r4k/2k: [root@appliance-1:Waiting for cluster service] config # docker exec platform-hal psf call GET:bmc/sel evMRev | event | eventData | eventDir | eventType | nextRecord | recordNumber | recordType | sensorNumber | sensorType | severity | sourceId | timestamp ---------+--------------------------------------+------------------------+------------+-----------------+------------+--------------+------------+--------------+-----------------------+----------+----------+-------------------------------- 4 | | [0xf7 0x1 0x1 ] | Asserted | Sensor-specific | 4 | 3 | 0x2 | #b | System Boot Initiated | Info | BMC | 2024-10-15 16:05:36 +0000 UTC
bugs.impact: There is no functional impact to this difference.
bugs.fix: After upgrading to F5OS 2.0 or later, the output for PEL and SEL timestamps will be the same.

bugs.title: Remote User First Login Failure
bugs.symptoms: The first time a remote user attempts to log in to a system, the access is denied despite providing the correct credentials. This is true for both TACACS and RADIUS remote users.
bugs.conditions: This always happens. A way to simulate the first login is to delete the file /etc/libnss-udr/passwd.
bugs.impact: The first login fails. Subsequent remote login attempts succeed with proper credentials.
bugs.workaround: Attempt remote login again.
bugs.fix: The user can now log in with proper credentials on the first attempt. Note that the fix involves having the following version of OpenSSH (or newer): # rpm -q openssh openssh-7.4p1-21.F5.6.2.7.el7.x86_64

bugs.title: [F5OS Changes] vlan members fails to populate inside the tenant if vlans attached to interface before deploying the tenant if VLANs spanning multiple interfaces are configured
bugs.symptoms: You can tag the same VLAN to multiple interfaces on r2K/r4K platforms, but when you attach VLANs to interfaces before deploying the tenant, the VLAN members will not be populated in the tenant. On BIG-IP, running 'tmsh list net vlan' will not show any tagged VLANs from F5OS.
bugs.conditions: -- rSeries r2000 and r4000-series platforms -- Tagged VLAN spanning multiple interfaces -- VLANs attached to the interfaces before deploying a BIG-IP tenant
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP tenant will not show the expected VLANs.
bugs.workaround: In F5OS, remove and re-attach the vlans to the interfaces. Example: appliance-1(config)# no interfaces interface 1.0 ethernet switched-vlan config appliance-1(config)# no interfaces interface 7.0 ethernet switched-vlan config appliance-1(config)# commit Commit complete. appliance-1(config)# interfaces interface 1.0 ethernet switched-vlan config trunk-vlans [ 1001 3006 ] appliance-1(config-interface-1.0)# interfaces interface 7.0 ethernet switched-vlan config trunk-vlans [ 1001 3006 ] appliance-1(config-interface-8.0)# commit Commit complete. appliance-1(config-interface-8.0)#

bugs.title: No active instance of ConfD after failover
bugs.symptoms: Unable to configure VELOS system, ConfD CLI commands fail.
bugs.conditions: Rarely, after failover newly active system controller silently transitions to none.
bugs.impact: Unable to configure VELOS system, ConfD CLI commands fail.
bugs.workaround: Reboot chassis.
bugs.fix: In releases with this fix in place, after failover there will be always be an Active instance of ConfD.

bugs.title: Timestamp is missing from logfile /var/log_controller/reprogram_chassis_network
bugs.symptoms: There is no timestamp for the logs related to RFC network changes
bugs.conditions: When network RFC changes happens logs are getting log in /var/log_controller/reprogram_chassis_network but the timestamp is not included.
bugs.impact: Unable to determine exactly when the log occurred.

bugs.title: F5OS-C system update logs now include timestamps
bugs.symptoms: System-update logs on F5OS-C do not have timestamps.
bugs.conditions: Running the partition-update process and viewing /var/log_controller/partition-update.
bugs.impact: The lack of timestamps in system-update logs could result in inefficient troubleshooting processes.
bugs.fix: Timestamps are logged in the system-update logs for all operations.

bugs.title: Partition may raise alarms if there are duplicate MAC address assignments
bugs.symptoms: On a VELOS chassis, if a partition is using MAC addresses that the system controller does not have in the chassis wide MAC database then, the partition will raise alarms.
bugs.conditions: If the system controller's MAC address database has been corrupted then, it may lose track of what addresses the partition owns. This knowledge article outlines how this can occur: https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000139293
bugs.impact: This can cause problems with traffic due to duplicate MAC assignments.
bugs.workaround: Alarms are raised to alert the user that duplicate MACs may be present in the partition. Partition configuration may need to change to eliminate duplicates.
bugs.fix: Refer to article https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000139293

bugs.title: New Alarms Introduced for Chassis-Wide MAC Pool Issues
bugs.symptoms: When there are chassis-wide MAC pool issues, e.g., a partition using MACs the controller did not know about, the user has little data to identify the issues, except for show system mac-allocation and show system chassis-macs. See 1576241 for details
bugs.conditions: Various chassis-wide MAC pool issues include partitions using the same MAC, controller partition MACs being the actual partition MAC pools, etc. See 1576241 for details
bugs.impact: Lack of new means of detecting the MAC issues prolongs the finding of the problems. See 1576241 for details
bugs.workaround: Since this is an improvement bug, there is no mitigation
bugs.fix: This improvement would allow users to collect more data that facilitates detecting and troubleshooting MAC issues

bugs.title: New Command Added for Configuration Changes and system controller Database Rationalization
bugs.symptoms: The new command is intended for cases when the MACs cannot be recovered by the vcc-partition-agent to the network-manager through the normal handshaking communication
bugs.conditions: The new command is intended for cases when the MACs cannot be recovered by the vcc-partition-agent to the network-manager through the normal handshaking communication
bugs.impact: Depending on the condition, configuration updates and standard failover/recovery procedures may be required. A new command is available to help reassign affected MAC allocations and align system records.
bugs.fix: Introduced a new command to simplify MAC reassignments and align system records.

bugs.title: Partition Network Manager is crashing when turning up.
bugs.symptoms: Upon Partition turn up, the Network Manager component crashes.
bugs.conditions: The Partition is turning up. This can happen due to partition creation, partition enable, or controller reboot.
bugs.impact: No impact. The Network Manager will successfully start after a retry.

bugs.title: Support for case-insensitive LDAP username lookup
bugs.symptoms: Previously, username lookup for LDAP-authenticated users was always case-sensitive.
bugs.conditions: Third-party authentication is configured with LDAP or Active Directory; user(s) in question reside in LDAP directory.
bugs.impact: Username lookups for authentication/authorization against LDAP directory were always conducted in a case-sensitive fashion, even for directories where case-insensitive was the default for the organization (e.g. Windows AD). Case-insensitive default is considered a safer security posture. It prevents username masking and cache injection when multiple users that only differ by case, with differing authorization privileges, exist in the same directory.
bugs.workaround: Always use correct case for case-sensitive searches.
bugs.fix: A new option was added which allows the admin to enable case-insensitive searches for LDAP username lookups. Note that case-sensitive remains the default for security reasons.

bugs.title: EPVA related dma-agent crash
bugs.symptoms: A dma-agent seg_fault occurs when there is a conflict between special EPVA allow-list entries.
bugs.conditions: A conflict between two entries on the allow-list triggers a code path in the dma-agent and resulting in a seg_fault.
bugs.impact: Traffic loss as the dma-agent needs to be restarted by its watchdog/start up script. Tenants need to re-register with the datapath.
bugs.fix: This issue has been fixed by setting a THREAD local variable in the epva_tbl_mgmt thread, preventing a seg_fault when the edge case method is triggered.

bugs.title: Observing "Failed to send restarting msg to VF" errors during reboot
bugs.symptoms: This error “Failed to send restarting msg to VF” appears during reboot and causes a delay in reboot.
bugs.conditions: When two or more BIG-IP tenants are deployed.
bugs.impact: Delay in reboot time.

bugs.title: F5OS Tenant Throughput (bits/packets) and TMM CPU usage higher than expected until VLAN is added or removed
bugs.symptoms: Higher CPU usage and throughput from the tenant than expected. Traffic being directed to a single blade in a multi-blade system.
bugs.conditions: Repeated deletes/adds of a VLAN from/to a tenant. After approximately 130 deletes, the issue occurs.
bugs.impact: Traffic imbalance, higher than normal CPU usage.
bugs.workaround: Re-add the recently deleted VLAN to the tenant.
bugs.fix: Properly clean up internal storage when a VLAN is deleted from a tenant.

bugs.title: SEL does not contain entries without a timestamp
bugs.symptoms: Certain SEL entries, mainly those without timestamps, are not being added to /var/log/platform/sel. This affects the entries that come before and after them also.
bugs.conditions: Anytime r2000 and r4000 systems encounter any event that would lead to a non-timestamped entry, like a CPU MCE.
bugs.impact: This makes diagnosing certain system issues more difficult, since there is less accessible information to those working on the issue. If F5 Support detects missing entries in /var/log/platform/sel you may be asked to run additional commands in order to diagnose potential issues.
bugs.fix: Non-timestamped entries are now logged in /var/log/platform/sel.

bugs.title: GUI fails to modify interfaces on F5OS-C
bugs.symptoms: Interface-related operations from the GUI fail.
bugs.conditions: -- Interface-related operations like LAG creation or deletion. -- F5OS build prior to 1.8.0-15246
bugs.impact: You are unable to perform interface operations from the GUI
bugs.fix: GUI is able to modify the interfaces on F5OS-C

bugs.title: Next Tenant Management interface is turned down/unreachable
bugs.symptoms: A BIG-IP Next Tenant Management Interface remains down.
bugs.conditions: -- VELOS or rSeries is the host -- The maximum number BIG-IP tenants are deployed -- Some tenants are deleted -- Some BIG-IP Next tenants are simultaneously deployed This can cause the new tenant to have the same MAC address as the tenant that is still shutting down, and the interface will not be marked up.
bugs.impact: 1. BIG-IP Next tenant's management interface will remain down. 2. Tenant will be unreachable.
bugs.workaround: 1. Move the affected tenant from Configured to Deployed 2. Rebooting the system Also fixes the as it will Delete and create the interface again.

bugs.title: Interface state enabled value stale due to timeout to reach confd
bugs.symptoms: When trying to modify the interface admin status to disabled across five different interfaces on five blades in a VELOS partition in a single commit message, the CLI operation to update the state interface enabled field fails with an error "system call failed". "Failed to write 68 bytes to ConfD: Connection timed out".
bugs.conditions: This can occur when a failover of chassis-controller and partition occurs, right before the interface enabled field changes.
bugs.impact: Stale value for interface/state/enabled field.
bugs.workaround: Enable and re-disable the interfaces.
bugs.fix: With the fix, the interface/state/enabled field will reflect accurately the configuration admin status of the interface.

bugs.title: Monitor rSeries ATSE to BE2 links and Raise Alarms in the Event of Failures
bugs.symptoms: Monitor rSeries ATSE to BE2 links and Raise Alarms in the Event of Failures
bugs.conditions: F5 rSeries r5000, r10000, or r12000-series appliance. This update is not applicable to r2000 or r4000-series appliances.
bugs.impact: In cases where errors are detected between the ATSE and BE2 links, alarms and events will be reported.
bugs.fix: Monitor ATSE to BE2 links and raise alarms and report events when errors are detected.

bugs.title: BE2 GCI interface training failures during runtime results in failure to process networking traffic
bugs.symptoms: On particular rSeries appliances, one or more symptoms could occur during normal operation: -- High availability stops working -- Inbound traffic stops -- Platform.log contains 'DM Tx Action ring hung' This is similar to the symptoms in https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID1580489.html, except that this can be triggered during system operation.
bugs.conditions: -- rSeries r5000, r10000, or r12000-series appliance This issue does not affect r2000 or r4000-series appliances.
bugs.impact: The system stops delivering traffic from front-panel ports to the host, although egress traffic may continue to work. If a LACP LAG is configured, ports will be unable to join the LAG.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround for this issue. If an appliance has already locked up, rebooting it might restore network connectivity. If your system is running F5OS-A version 1.5.x, F5OS-A-1.5.2-29198.R5R10.EHF-4.iso is an Engineering Hot Fix (EHF) that contains a software fix, and is available at https://my.f5.com/manage/s/downloads?productFamily=F5OS&productLine=F5OS_Appliance_Software&version=1.5.2&container=1.5.2-EHF You can also upgrade to F5OS-A 1.8.0.
bugs.fix: New FPGA bitstreams stabilize the interface between the ATSE and BE2 chip.

bugs.title: Seeing error logs in messages file for offline vcpus when lower end license is installed
bugs.symptoms: You see a flood of logs in /var/log/messages: appliance-1.chassis.local k3s: W0616 12:57:50.066828 35509 sysinfo.go:394] Cannot read core id for /sys/devices/system/node/node0/cpu18, core_id file does not exist, err: open /sys/devices/system/node/node0/cpu18/topology/core_id: no such file or directory
bugs.conditions: This occurs after applying a r10600 license that activates a different number of CPUs than the system has.
bugs.impact: Log flood of error logs for offline vcpus in /var/log/messages file

bugs.title: iHealth client can occasionally throw a core file
bugs.symptoms: The iHealth client, accessible with the command line, system diagnostics ihealth can be used for uploading QKView files to the iHealth service. If this client loses connection to the system database for any reason, it may throw a core file, in the host system's /var/shared/core directory.
bugs.conditions: System has been up for a long time, and there is a problem with the ConfD database causing the iHealth client to disconnect.
bugs.impact: A core file may be thrown. The iHealth client will restart if this happens, so functionality is not affected.
bugs.workaround: Retry the ihealth client operation.
bugs.fix: The iHealth client will only access the ConfD database when it needs to query information, and not maintain an open connection.

bugs.title: F5OS API tokens invalidated after a minute of inactivity
bugs.symptoms: F5OS API (restconf) tokens expire after approximately a minute of inactivity, regardless of the configured token lifetime. In the audit log, the token is rejected with an error of: ERROR: Token is not active: <username><session ID>
bugs.conditions: - Using the F5OS API - Wait more than a minute between API requests
bugs.impact: API tokens are invalidated prematurely and cannot be renewed, and the user must request new tokens.

bugs.title: BAY ID of RAID drivers are displayed as 0,1
bugs.symptoms: BAY ID of RAID drivers are displayed as 0,1 which are not consistent with the actual hardware ID
bugs.conditions: Running 'show system raid'
bugs.impact: ID shown for RAID drivers is 0,1 instead of 1,2 respectively. No other functional impact.

bugs.title: F5OS - BIG-IP Tenant does not display VELOS Chassis slot serial number
bugs.symptoms: F5OS BIG-IP Tenant does not display the serial number for the slot ("Host Board Serial") under "System Information"
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP tenant is running on a chassis, and command "tmsh show sys hardware" is run from the tenant
bugs.impact: The slot serial number is not immediately visible to the user
bugs.workaround: For CLI, login to the partition and run command "show components component state serial-no". For GUI, login to the active controller, then go to System Settings -> System Inventory. The blade serial number will be shown.
bugs.fix: F5OS was updated to provide the blade serial number to the tenant for display. The tenant was updated to populate the blade serial number into "show sys hardware" command output, so it is now visible to the user. This fix requires a version 17.5 tenant.

bugs.title: Tenant status is not accurate when the F5OS upgrade is in progress
bugs.symptoms: The “show tenants” data is not updated properly when the firmware upgrade is in progress.
bugs.conditions: During upgrade, if “show system install status” shows in progress, the data is not updated as k3s is not turned up completely.
bugs.impact: No functional impact. Users should get accurate data once the firmware installation is complete. You can refer to “show tenants” data post system upgrade is completed.
bugs.workaround: Wait until the upgrade activity is completed.
bugs.fix: Once appliance upgrade activity is completed, the status will be reflected with the actual tenant status.

bugs.title: Incorrect PSU mismatch indication for two Murata MW2100 PSUs operating at different AC input voltages
bugs.symptoms: If two Murata MW2100 AC PSUs are installed in the system and one is operating with an AC input at or above 100V and the second is operating with an AC input below 100V, then an incorrect PSU mismatch condition may occur. Use the F5OS command "show components" to view voltage details for the PSUs.
bugs.conditions: - r10000 or r12000-series appliance - Two Murata MW2100 AC PSUs, one with an AC input at or above 100V and the other with an AC input below 100V.
bugs.impact: An incorrect "PSU mismatch" condition may occur.
bugs.workaround: Ensure both Murata MW2100 AC PSUs have input voltage at or above 100V or below 100V.
bugs.fix: There is no PSU mismatch for two MW2100 PSUs that are operating at different AC input voltages.

bugs.title: F5OS unable to transmit frames out to external interface, even though link is reported as UP
bugs.symptoms: Intermittently, one of the external links on the appliance reports a link 'UP' status. However, the system will receive ingress frames on the interface, but no frames will egress the interface. - An F5OS packet capture will show frames being sent on that link, but they will not egress the interface. - If the port is a member of an LACP LAG, the LAG status will be reported as LACP_DOWN / OUT_SYNC, and lacpd may log messages similar to the following repeatedly: lacpd[13]: priority="Info" version=1.0 msgid=0x3401000000000088 msg="Mux_disable_colldist" port_state="Intf=5.0 partnerDefaulted:1 rxState:3 selected:0 txState:0 actorChurn:0 partnerChurn:1 muxState:0 periodicTxState:1 actorState:10000111 partnerState:01000111". - The interface 'out' counters will not increment. - The tmctl 'gbx_stat' counters will show incrementing egress packet counters ('egr_pkt_cnt'). - Platform.log may report the transmit direction for the interface MAC as being disabled, although this can occur even if the interface is working properly: fpgamgr[15]: priority="Info" version=1.0 msgid=0x309000000000016 msg="Configured Interface MAC." INTERFACE="10.0" Tx="Disabled" Rx="Enabled".
bugs.conditions: -- r5000, r10000, or r12000-series appliance. -- The first time an interface links up after a system reboot.
bugs.impact: After a link comes up, the system is unable to transmit frames.
bugs.workaround: This issue is intermittent, and should not occur after rebooting the appliance. Use the following procedure if the rebooting does not resolve the issue. === Collecting data to determine which interface is in an unexpected state. On an r5000: for i in nw_{0..9}; do echo $i; docker exec system_fpga fpgatool -c "mac enable asw $i"; echo; done On an r10000 or r12000: for j in asw nso; do for i in nw_{0..9}; do echo $j $i; docker exec system_fpga fpgatool -c "mac enable $j $i"; echo; done; done For example: nw_7 target is up on 127.0.0.1:1060 TX Enable state: 0 ===> (!!!) RX Enable state: 1 === To map the output of one of those to a named interface, see `tmctl gbx_cfg` r5000: interface_name link chip -------------- -------------- ---- 1.0 f5sw_link_nw_0 asw 2.0 f5sw_link_nw_1 asw 3.0 f5sw_link_nw_2 asw 4.0 f5sw_link_nw_3 asw 5.0 f5sw_link_nw_4 asw 6.0 f5sw_link_nw_5 asw 7.0 f5sw_link_nw_6 asw 8.0 f5sw_link_nw_7 asw 9.0 f5sw_link_nw_8 asw 10.0 f5sw_link_nw_9 asw r10000/r12000: interface_name link chip -------------- -------------- ---- 1.0 f5sw_link_nw_0 nso 2.0 f5sw_link_nw_1 nso 3.0 f5sw_link_nw_2 nso 4.0 f5sw_link_nw_3 nso 5.0 f5sw_link_nw_4 nso 6.0 f5sw_link_nw_5 nso 7.0 f5sw_link_nw_6 nso 8.0 f5sw_link_nw_7 nso 9.0 f5sw_link_nw_8 nso 10.0 f5sw_link_nw_9 nso 11.0 f5sw_link_nw_0 asw 12.0 f5sw_link_nw_1 asw 13.0 f5sw_link_nw_2 asw 14.0 f5sw_link_nw_3 asw 15.0 f5sw_link_nw_4 asw 16.0 f5sw_link_nw_5 asw 17.0 f5sw_link_nw_6 asw 18.0 f5sw_link_nw_7 asw 19.0 f5sw_link_nw_8 asw 20.0 f5sw_link_nw_9 asw (Note that interfaces 1-10 are on *different chips* when comparing an r5000 and r10000/r12000.) === Run the following command to manually enable the affected interface docker exec system_fpga fpgatool -c "mac enable asw <INTFERACE> 1 1" For example, the following command will enable interface 8.0 on r5000 docker exec system_fpga fpgatool -c "mac enable asw nw_7 1 1" === Wait for 10 second and check the state again. docker exec system_fpga fpgatool -c "mac enable asw <INTERFACE>" === Assuming both RX and TX were enabled in the last step, check the LACP LAG status.

bugs.title: F5OS-A/F5OS-C support for SNMPv3 using Auth 'SHA256' and Encryption 'AES192, AES256'.
bugs.symptoms: F5OS does not support auth SHA256 and private aes192, aes256 for snmpv3 user as Secure 256-bits ciphers are mandated for security policy.
bugs.conditions: No Specific conditions.
bugs.impact: Certain ciphers are not allowed with SNMP.

bugs.title: Multus may not be installed after new blade is inserted
bugs.symptoms: Newly inserted blade is added to cluster correctly but it will not be operational for tenant use since multus is not installed.
bugs.conditions: After new blade is installed, there is a race condition on detecting new blade and installation of multus fails.
bugs.impact: Unable to deploy working tenants on this node.
bugs.workaround: Run oc delete node <blade-x> on the console to remove the blade. The blade installs correctly after removal.

bugs.title: Improved logging to identify the cause of unexpected system reboots
bugs.symptoms: When platform-mgr triggers a system reboot, no log message is generated to explain the reason for the reboot. This makes it difficult to diagnose why an unexpected or unintended reboot occurred.
bugs.conditions: A change in the number of online CPU cores vs. licensed cores A change in CPU frequency Failure to read an internal settings file
bugs.impact: Without sufficient logging, it becomes difficult to determine the root cause of a platform-mgr-initiated reboot from system logs alone.

bugs.title: i40e driver not loaded error
bugs.symptoms: A blade is not responsive, and the platform deployment log reports "ERROR: Module i40e is not currently loaded"
bugs.conditions: Install the 1.7.1-C iso.
bugs.impact: Network interfaces are not detected or initialized properly.
bugs.workaround: # Load the i40e driver module modprobe i40e # Verify it's loaded lsmod | grep i40e
bugs.fix: The i40e driver now loads earlier in bootup.

bugs.title: SysDescr value returns empty string under SNMPwalk, after performing backup/restore configuration
bugs.symptoms: System config backup/restore resets the system database to default. Due to this, the sysDescr in SNMP will also reset to default.
bugs.conditions: This occurs after performing F5OS system config backup and restore.
bugs.impact: The sysDescr in SNMPwalk displays the default value.
bugs.workaround: Restart the snmpd docker service.
bugs.fix: The SNMP sysDescr is updated to the correct value after F5OS system config backup and restore operation.

bugs.title: Show services command shows stale entries for deleted tenants
bugs.symptoms: After deploying many tenants (100+) in the configured state and then rapidly deleting them, the 'show tenants' command will show deleted tenants.
bugs.conditions: -- Deleting a large list of tenants via a script that does not wait in between deletion commands.
bugs.impact: The show tenants command shows stale entries.
bugs.workaround: Add a sleep of 3 seconds after each commit when deleting a tenant.

bugs.title: Unable to search events using a keyword.
bugs.symptoms: You are unable to search log events via a keyword.
bugs.conditions: -- F5OS GUI -- Searching for certain events in the logs
bugs.impact: You are unable to search for and locate specific events, particularly when the event list is extensive.
bugs.workaround: You can view and filter the events on the CLI: show system events | include "<keyword>"
bugs.fix: A search bar has been added to the events data table, allowing users to easily find specific events using keywords.

bugs.title: GUI login fails with a crash in system_manager.external-authenticator
bugs.symptoms: The curl request or GUI login fails with core in system_manager.external-authenticator component. This is caused due to the corrupted primary key.
bugs.conditions: External curl request or GUI login.
bugs.impact: External curl request including GUI login fails.
bugs.workaround: 1. You can regenerate the primary key using this command: # system aaa primary-key set passphrase <value> Try to login GUI and see if the crash appearing or not. 2. If the issue still persists, it requires clean install.

bugs.title: A large amount of SPVA DoS allow list entries can overload DMA-Agent causing a tenant to fail to pass traffic
bugs.symptoms: If the DMA-Agent receives a high volume of SPVA allow list entries at once, it may become overwhelmed and stop working. As a result, no traffic will be able to exit the tenant. This can be identified by observing the DMA-Agent using 100% of the cpu.
bugs.conditions: This is usually seen in configurations where there are many virtual servers configured with a dos profile that contains an IP-based allow list. The problem does not arise when VIPs are added individually, but it often happens after TMM is restarted following a tenant reboot.
bugs.impact: Affected tenants will fail to pass any traffic on the data-plane. The TMSTAT sep_stats.tx_send_drops3 will be incremented. This issue could also effect other tenants hosted on the same F5OS hypervisor.
bugs.workaround: Perform the following on the tenant: tmsh modify sys db dos.forceswdos value true tmsh save sys conf To recover the DMA-Agent in F5OS, set the tenant state to “configured” and then set it back to “deployed.
bugs.fix: The DMA-Agent now handles a high volume of SPVA allow list entries.

bugs.title: LACP status shows UP in BIG-IP tenant even if its down on F5OS.
bugs.symptoms: LACP Trunk is UP in BIG-IP tenant even when it’s DOWN on F5OS.
bugs.conditions: Condition 1: 1. Setup a rSeries or VELOS system. 2. Configure LACP LAG with interfaces operationally down. 3. Make sure LACP Trunk is DOWN on F5OS. 4. Upgrade the software. 5. Launch a BIG-IP tenant. 6. Check LACP trunk status inside tenant. Condition 2: 1. Setup a rSeries or VELOS system. 2. Configure STATIC LAG with interfaces operationally down. 3. Ensure STATIC Trunk is DOWN on F5OS. 4. Launch a BIG-IP tenant. 5. Check the Trunk status inside the tenant. It will be DOWN. 6. Convert LAG type to LACP 7. Check the Trunk status inside the tenant. It will be UP even though it is down on F5OS.
bugs.impact: LACP Trunk members are shown as working members even though they are DOWN.
bugs.workaround: Check the interface config. If the admin is disabled, enable it.
bugs.fix: The status of LACP members is read whenever an LACP member is added as an operational member.

bugs.title: License installation is not working with HTTPS Proxy server

bugs.title: Reset counter functionality not working properly on rSeries platforms

bugs.impact: The system may be completely inoperative, or the system may be running with different OS versions, which could lead to unknown problems.

bugs.title: OpenShift namespace can get stuck in terminating if resources are still in use.

This causes the namespace created in Openshift for the F5OS partition to get stuck in the terminating state. If a new partition is created that tries to re-use this partition ID, the new namespace representing the new partition will fail to start until the old namespace is cleaned up.

bugs.impact: If the namespace gets stuck in terminating and new partition is created using the same partition-id, services for that partition will NOT be able to start and tenants in that partition will NOT be able to start.

bugs.title: VLAN groups or VLAN group members may be deleted on F5OS tenant
bugs.symptoms: If using VLAN groups on a tenant running on an rSeries appliance or VELOS chassis, the system may delete the VLAN group or VLAN group members unexpectedly. This will happen when configuration changes to the tenant are made in F5OS or if the interface members of the VLAN change state (i.e. link down) - If the VLAN groups are in a non-common partition, any members of the VLAN group will be removed, but the VLAN group will remain. - If the VLAN groups are in common partition, but are not referenced by higher-level objects, the VLAN group will be removed. - If the VLAN groups are in common partition and are referenced by higher-level objects, the system will not delete the VLAN group, but will log messages similar to the following: err mcpd[9181]: 01070623:3: The vlangroup (/Common/otters-vlangroup) is referenced by one or more virtual servers. err chmand[4691]: 012a0003:3: hal_mcp_process_error: result_code=0x1070623 for result_operation=eom result_type=eom
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP tenant running on rSeries appliance or VELOS chassis - VLAN group configured in tenant, and not using virtual wire
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted due to removal of VLAN group objects or VLAN group members.
bugs.workaround: To avoid this problem, define an unused VLAN group in the common partition and assign it to the VLAN list for a virtual server. tmsh create net vlan-group /Common/unused-vg tmsh create ltm virtual /Common/unused-virtual vlans-enabled vlans add { unused-vg } description "Workaround for ID1623325" tmsh save sys config Note the use of "vlans-enabled" and adding the empty VLAN group to the virtual server's VLAN list. This means that the BIG-IP system will never actually process traffic via this virtual server, as it would only accept traffic to the virtual server that arrives over the VLAN group, but the VLAN group will never receive any actual traffic. As a result of implementing this workaround, when the tenant processes any configuration updates from F5OS, the tenant will log error messages similar to the following: err mcpd[10720]: 01070623:3: The vlangroup (/Common/unused-vg) is referenced by one or more virtual servers. err chmand[6781]: 012a0003:3: hal_mcp_process_error: result_code=0x1070623 for result_operation=eom result_type=eom
