bugs.conditions: This issue arises when an “Inaccessible Memory” incident occurs, resulting in OMD generating redundant alerts “openshiftCertsExpWithinNinetyDays” for the same event, which is causing confusion and unnecessary noise in alert tracking systems.
bugs.impact: False-positive or duplicate alerts for OMD.
bugs.workaround: To verify and troubleshoot the issue, you can: 1. Use the confD command 'show cluster cluster-status' to check the cluster's current status. 2. Analyze the openshift.log/velos.log file for any errors or abnormalities related to the incident or cluster health.
bugs.fix: The issue has been addressed by implementing enhanced logic in OMD alert generation to eliminate duplicate alerts resulting from overlapping OID/alert IDs. The system now ensures each alert is uniquely identified and mapped to its respective event, preventing redundancy during “Inaccessible Memory” incidents. All configurations have been updated to maintain integrity and consistency.

bugs.title: PAM faillock data is deleted on restart, allowing users to log in immediately
bugs.symptoms: The administrator can set up the max-login-failures (Number of unsuccessful login attempts allowed before lockout) to a non-zero number. Also, the unlock-timeout can be increased from the default value of 60 seconds. Once the number of failed login attempts is reached, then the user must wait the alotted unlock-timeout period before being allowed to login with the correct credentials. The number of login-failures for each user is currently reset to zero upon a system reboot.
bugs.conditions: Rebooting simply eliminates the tally count of login failures for all users.
bugs.impact: The max-login-failures setting is set back to zero if the system is rebooted.
bugs.fix: With this fix, rebooting does not reset the tally count for login failures. This can be verified by viewing the state of the user: show system aaa authentication users user <user> state which will not go to zero after a reboot.

bugs.title: Error when creating a server-group name with an embedded space
bugs.symptoms: An error log inside 'platform.log' for the rSeries systems or 'velos.log' in the VELOS systems when you configure a server-group name with an embedded space. In velos.log on F5OS-C or platform.log on F5OS-A: appliance-1 authd[8]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x3901000000000109 msg="Failed to set element in cdb." path="/system/aaa/server-groups/server-group" error="Bad key "my server group" (wrong number of identifiers) at: /system/aaa/server-groups/server-group" errno="Exec format error".
bugs.conditions: Creating a server-group name with an embedded space. Example: my server group
bugs.impact: The configuration change will not take an effect.
bugs.workaround: Remove all spaces from the server-group name. For example, if the server-group name with a space was 'my server group', you can rename it into 'my_server_group' and re-configure the rest of the values. appliance-1(config)# system aaa server-groups server-group my_server_group config name my_server_group appliance-1(config)#commit
bugs.fix: Avoid embedded spaces when you create server-group names.

bugs.title: Inconsistent timezone indication in system command output
bugs.symptoms: - The command "show system aaa primary-key state" displays date/time without explicitly indicating the timezone.
bugs.conditions: Observed when running the command "show system aaa primary-key state".
bugs.impact: - Confusion or misinterpretation of timestamps by users. - Lack of clarity on the date/time's timezone.
bugs.workaround: The date/time displayed is UTC, even though it does not display a timezone.

bugs.title: SwitchD core file observed after live upgrade
bugs.symptoms: Users may observe core files being generated on both controllers after a system live upgrade.
bugs.conditions: The occurrence of the core is non-deterministic, but it can happen after the live upgrade.
bugs.impact: When this issue occurs, the SwitchD process generates a core file on the controller.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the controllers after observing SwitchD core file on the controller.
bugs.fix: This issue has been resolved to ensure proper process initialization during SwitchD initialization.

bugs.title: ConfD HA Status does not match bash prompt
bugs.symptoms: When accessing the confd-cli it may report a different ha-state than that of the bash prompt. For example you may see: syscon-2-standby# [root@controller-2:Active ~]#
bugs.conditions: No specific conditions, the issue roots from Vcc-HA using blocking socket I/O that hangs when attempting to program ccsync state. When it hangs, Vcc-HA will hang forever and active/standby state of ccysnc will not be programmed correctly.
bugs.impact: Ccsync isn't programmed correctly images and other resources managed by ccsync will not be correctly synced between controllers.
bugs.workaround: Perform docker restart vcc-ha on both controllers.
bugs.fix: Updated vcc-ha to use non-blocking socket I/O to insure it cannot get hung when trying to program ccsync. It will instead exit and retry if the timeout is hit.

bugs.title: Multiple docker containers can get assigned the same bridge IP during rolling upgrade
bugs.symptoms: Multiple containers can get the same bridge IP during a rolling upgrade or docker restart [root@controller-2 ~]# docker inspect controller-services-registry-2502 | grep IPAddress "SecondaryIPAddresses": null, "IPAddress": "100.64.0.2", "IPAddress": "100.64.0.2", [root@controller-2 ~]# docker inspect partition-services-registry-2202 | grep IPAddress "SecondaryIPAddresses": null, "IPAddress": "100.64.0.2", "IPAddress": "100.64.0.2", There's a race in IP address allocation in Docker.
bugs.conditions: When multiple containers start at the same time.
bugs.impact: This causes one of the two containers to answer requests depending on which container last refreshed the arp cache. The other container does not work properly.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the system.
bugs.fix: Docker address allocator uses bit map to manage IP address pool but it's not thread safe. Now, set/unset bitmap operations are protected by a lock.

bugs.title: Active Directory LDAP integration without uidNumber/gidNumber does not work after system reboot
bugs.symptoms: After an rSeries appliance reboot, Active Directory LDAP authentication configured with "Unix Attributes" set to false does not work and users from Active Directory are unable to authenticate with the F5OS system. There will be messages similar to the following logged in platform.log shortly after the reboot: authd[8]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x3901000000000101 msg="LDAP API error during : -" oper="SASL bind" code=-1 msg="Can't contact LDAP server". authd[8]: priority="Warn" version=1.0 msgid=0x3901000000000098 msg="Unable to retrieve domain Sid for supplied servers and domains; server will be treated as if it has unix attributes present.".
bugs.conditions: - F5OS device configured with Active Directory LDAP authentication, and the "Unix Attributes" setting configured as false. - System reboots
bugs.impact: LDAP remote authentication does not work.
bugs.workaround: To workaround this issue on an rSeries appliance, create a cron task to restart the system_user_manager and authentication-mgr docker containers after a system reboot: 1. Log into the system as root and create /etc/cron.d/ldap-post-reboot with these contents (not including the '==='): === # Workaround for post-reboot issue with LDAP auth (ID1782925) # # In the the first five minutes after the system reboots, assume the first # instance of the following log message that we see is a result of the management # port lack of connectivity when the docker containers start up, and restart both # system_user_manager and authentication-mgr once. # # authd[8]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x3901000000000101 msg="LDAP API error during : -" oper="SASL bind" code=-1 msg="Can't contact LDAP server". @reboot root timeout 5m sh -c 'tail -n0 -F /var/F5/system/log/platform.log | grep -a -m1 authd.*0x3901000000000101 && sleep 20s && echo Restarting authd and user-manager && docker restart system_user_manager authentication-mgr' || echo "Timed out" === This mitigation may fail under some corner cases, e.g. potentially after an upgrade or if something goes wrong with the platform services such that they don't start up within the first five minutes after system boot. In those circumstances, log into the system as root and restart the system_user_manager and authentication-mgr containers: docker restart system_user_manager authentication-mgr

bugs.title: ATSE Datapath lockup causes blade to report unhealthy and stop passing traffic
bugs.symptoms: This failure looks like an RQM lockup. An RQM lockup can show up as a DMA receive failure or a DMA transmit failure. Receive failure because the receive queue will not accept HBM memory writes. Transmit failure because loopback health check packets will back up and flow control the transmit data-path. - A partition's tenants may be unreachable while another partition is unaffected. - System health output (show system health) will report something similar to "blade-X overall-health = Unhealthy/Critical; other blades/controllers healthy." - A partition's blade will log its velos.log file occurrence(s) of ATSE register dumps and "ring hung", for example: <timestamp> ACTIVE dma-agent[13]: nodename=blade-1(p2) priority="Alert" version=1.0 msgid=0x4201000000000130 msg="Health monitor detected DM Tx Action ring hung." ATSE=0 DM=2 OQS=2. <timestamp> ACTIVE dma-agent[13]: nodename=blade-1(p2) priority="Info" version=1.0 msgid=0x4201000000000137 msg="Health monitor DM register dump complete." FILE="agent-dump-1764975200.txt".
bugs.conditions: No known conditions. This typically happens on initialization, but has been seen at runtime.
bugs.impact: This causes a data-path lock-up and traffic will not be passed by the affected blade.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the affected blade. A fix for this issue is available in F5OS-C 1.8.2-28324.EHF-1, which is available for download on MyF5: https://my.f5.com/manage/s/downloads?productFamily=F5OS&productLine=F5OS+Platform+Software+for+VELOS&version=1.8.2&container=1.8.2-EHF
bugs.fix: HBM calibration has been fixed.

bugs.title: ATSE Datapath lockup on HBM calibration issue
bugs.symptoms: Datapath lockup in the ATSE FPGA. Can be seen at startup with no traffic received at the host, or some time after startup with packet framing errors. This can also show up as a transmit packet path lockup because health check loopback packets can back up into the transmit datapath and block it.
bugs.conditions: No known conditions.
bugs.impact: The impact is no packets can get from the network to host for processing.
bugs.workaround: The datapath lockup requires a reload of the ATSE FPGA. Reload typically done by rebooting the system. This issue has been fixed in ATSE bitfiles v72.5.8.00 and v72.41.8.0 and all newer bitfiles.
bugs.fix: The issue is an FPGA memory reset procedure. The HBM memory inside the ATSE FPGA has a very specific bringup procedure. There was an issue with the initial implementation of that procedure.

bugs.title: Bash history file containing "PRIVATE KEY" may block qkview
bugs.symptoms: Qkview file generation gets stuck at zero percent complete: # system diagnostics qkview status result {"Busy":true,"Percent":0,"Status":"collecting","Message":"Collecting Data","Filename":"controller1.qkview.tar.gz"} Subsequent attempts to generate a qkview fail with the result "Qkview capture can not be initiated. Another Qkview capture is already in progress"
bugs.conditions: -- Generating qkview -- The bash history file is large and contains the text "PRIVATE KEY"
bugs.impact: Qkview files are not able to be collected
bugs.workaround: 1. Run system diagnostics qkview cancel 2. mv ~/.bash_history ~/.bash_history.bak 3. Re-run qkview
bugs.fix: TBD

bugs.title: Controller prompt stuck "Waiting for firmware status"
bugs.symptoms: The command line system prompt perpetually says "Waiting for firmware status" on both controllers.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when a user has issued the command to reset the confd database (reset-default-config) without rebooting the controllers.
bugs.impact: Message will stay until controllers are rebooted.
bugs.workaround: Reboot both controllers.

bugs.title: Tenant deployed with Max Memory available on system results in Resource allocation failed - Node is up but Platform services not responding
bugs.symptoms: Tenant fails to come to running state when deployed with max memory on system.
bugs.conditions: Tenant is deployed with max-available memory on the blade in prior releases of F5OS-C 1.8.1 version.
bugs.impact: Tenant fails to come to running state.
bugs.workaround: Since the max memory available for tenants on blade is corrected in F5OS-C-1.8.1, the tenant memory should be configured accordingly. Step 1. Move failed tenant to configured state and adjust the memory to the new max-available memory of the tenant. Step 2. Move the tenant back to the deployed state.
bugs.fix: Max memory available on system for tenant deployment has been corrected with right value.

bugs.title: Management port not bouncing on failover on VELOS CX410 chassis
bugs.symptoms: When a failover occurs on VELOS CX410 chassis, the management link won't be updated, resulting in loss off connectivity for 300s or other to which remote switch has set as it's timeout for the mac address table.
bugs.conditions: Failover occurs on VELOS CX410.
bugs.impact: Loss of management connectivity for 300s or other to which remote switch has set as it's timeout of the mac address table.
bugs.workaround: Wait for remote switch to timeout and clear it's mac address table.
bugs.fix: With this fix in place the VELOS CX410 chassis will now bounce it's management link on failover immediately clearing the remote mac address table on the switch.

bugs.title: It's possible to add a l2 listener fdb without error
bugs.symptoms: You are able to manually add a l2 listener entry type fdb from the CLI but this should not be allowed.
bugs.conditions: The fdb command is used from the cli defining the entry-type field as L2-LISTENER.
bugs.impact: Fdbs with the entry-type L2-LISTENER should be only added by the system.
bugs.workaround: Do not add fdbs with the entry-type field set to L2-LISTENER.
bugs.fix: It is impossible now to add a l2 listener fdb.

bugs.title: Unable to launch tenant, VF interface is missing under "ip link show"
bugs.symptoms: On r2x00/r4x00 related systems, tenant launch fails with an error in ConfD tenant status leaf: "error adding container to network "sriov-net3-bip1": failed to set up pod interface "net7" from the device "x557_4": failed to set netlink MAC address to <mac>: resource temporarily unavailable" or "SRIOV-CNI failed to load netconf: LoadConf(): the VF 0000:ec:01.3 does not have a interface name or a dpdk driver" Linux network manager udev rules and sriov cni try to access the VF and change the interface name of VF. During this process, VFs fail and unable to retrieve. Thus, resource temporarily unavailable error occurs.
bugs.conditions: On r4x00 or r2x00 based systems: 1. In kubectl get pods -A output, the tenant pod goes into Init:0/1 state. default virt-launcher-bip1-1-t6rkh 0/1 Init:0/1 0 36s 2. And in kubectl events, "resource temporarily unavailable" occurs on one of the VFs. 3. In /sys/class/net folder unable to see the below VF interfaces. Instead, some interfaces point to ensp* names which are wrong.
bugs.impact: Tenant launch is unsuccessful and unable to connect to the tenant console or tenants' management connection.
bugs.workaround: 1. Set all tenants to the Configured state. 2. Reboot the appliance. 3. Once the system is up, change one tenant’s state to Deployed at a time, allowing a gap of 3–5 minutes before moving to the next tenant. 4. Repeat this process until all tenants are deployed.

bugs.title: Question mark for wName, fw-version-sirr in snmpwalk ouput
bugs.symptoms: snmpwalk and snmptable were returning data that did not match the ConfD CLI output for F5-PLATFORM-STATS-MIB::fwUpdateStatus.
bugs.conditions: Whenever there is a config change from the confd cli related to F5-PLATFORM-STATS-MIB::fwUpdateStatus table.
bugs.impact: Ambiguity about the information for fwUpdateStatus table.
bugs.workaround: Fixed backend issue for snmp handler for fwUpdateStatus table.
bugs.fix: No mismatch between the CLI output and snmpwalk, snmpget for the fwUpdateStatus table.

bugs.title: In rare instances, LACPD may crash when creating a new aggregation interface.
bugs.symptoms: LACPD produces a core dump and restarts.
bugs.conditions: Adding a new interface with type ieee8023adLag: interfaces interface myinterface config type ieee8023adLag Other unknown variables may increase the likelihood of a crash occurring.
bugs.impact: Any interfaces managed by LACP may briefly stop processing traffic as LACPD restarts. The new ieee8023adLag interface will be functional after LACPD restarts.
bugs.fix: LACPD will no longer crash when a user creates a new interface of type ieee8023adLag.

bugs.title: SNMP bulk queries for LAGs on VELOS might return incomplete information
bugs.symptoms: SNMP queries for interface statistics for a LAG might return incomplete information
bugs.conditions: - VELOS partition - Querying SNMP for LAGs - The LAG contains multiple members - The SNMP client is issuing bulk SNMP queries - The SNMP client queries for the first member of the LAG, skips another member of the LAG, and then queries information for the LAG
bugs.impact: The SNMP statistics reported by the VELOS system could possibly return incomplete information (failing to include statistics from one or more of the members of the LAG).
bugs.fix: The system will now correctly report SNMP statistics for LAGs.

bugs.title: VQF VOQ entries missing for the functional blades in the show fpga-tables output
bugs.symptoms: Blade 13 is in faulty state due to a different issue related to memory DIMMs. For the show FPGA tables command there is output for VOQs corresponding to blades 1 and 11. And in the vqf_voq_stat table output, the remaining VOQ stat requests starting from 13 do not return data although the tmstat table for some other blades are intact.
bugs.conditions: One of the intermediate blades from the list of show components is faulty and leads to skipping of processing the vqf voq stat requests for rest of the blades that are properly functional.
bugs.impact: Improper output for the 'show fpga-tables vqf_voq_stat' command.
bugs.fix: Added a code change to get the stats completion for rest of the functional blades when one of the blades is faulty.

bugs.title: If 'ldap-group is configured for a role but LDAP search fails, users with the default GID for the role can still get those privileges
bugs.symptoms: When an 'ldap-group' mapping is configured for a F5OS role, and the mapping fails (because the filter is invalid or the LDAP query of remote groups fails for some other reason), the default mapping for the role (or, what is configured in 'remote-gid' for the role) is still used. For example, if you were attempting to map the F5OS role 'admin' (default GID 9000) to an LDAP group 'CN=my-ldapgroup', and the LDAP search for that group failed (because the provided filter was invalid, the group does not exist, etc.), users with GID 9000 would still be able to authenticate and login with 'admin' privileges.
bugs.conditions: 1. LDAP authentication is enabled. 2. A role mapping is applied via the 'ldap-group' configuration for a F5OS role. 3. The provided 'ldap-group' filter is invalid or another unexpected issue is encountered when querying the LDAP server.
bugs.impact: Users can login with privileges in excess of what one might expect given the system configuration.
bugs.workaround: If the LDAP group/users have Posix attributes ('gidNumber'), it is possible to map the F5OS role using this GID number by specifying it in the 'remote-gid' configuration under the role. If this is not feasible, it is possible to directly validate the 'ldap-group' mapping was successful by inspecting this file from a bash shell: [root@appliance-1(test):Active] ~ # cat /etc/ldap-gid-map.txt 1108:=9000 If there is an entry that has the default GID for the role on the right-hand side of ':=' in this file, it means the mapping was applied successfully and users with the default or 'remote-gid' GID will not be able to obtain the role permissions. If such an entry is missing, you will need to fix the 'ldap-group' filter so an LDAP query of the group can be successful.
bugs.fix: If a configured 'ldap-group' mapping fails, deny all role-based access for the mapped role until it is fixed or de-configured.

bugs.title: IPMI 0xC0 "Node Busy" PEL/SEL related messages
bugs.symptoms: IPMI commands are failing with a "Node Busy" error because the BMC cannot complete the request.
bugs.conditions: Intermittent race conditions occur when BMC executes IPMI commands.
bugs.impact: On "Node Busy." failure IPMI commands will now retry up to 5 times.
bugs.fix: After upgrading to F5OS 2.0 or later, IPMI commands will now retry up to five times if the BMC is busy, rather than failing with the "Node Busy" error message.

bugs.title: Component fpgamgr in restart loop with segmentation fault after failed FPGA firmware update
bugs.symptoms: Component fpgamgr experiences segmentation fault after failed FPGA firmware update and persists in a reboot loop. The CLI command "show cluster nodes node state platform fpga-state" indicates that FPGA_STATE persists in FPGA_INIT and never reaches the state FPGA_RDY.
bugs.conditions: FPGA firmware update fails and one or more of the FPGA devices does not show up on the PCI bus. This causes a FPGA SDK segmentation fault upon the fpgamgr component startup, and perpetual reboot loop so long as the FPGA issue persists.
bugs.impact: A failure in the FPGA firmware update process results in one or more FPGA devices not being detected on the PCI bus. This, in turn, causes a segmentation fault in the FPGA SDK upon the startup of the fpgamgr component, leading to a continuous reboot cycle until the FPGA issue is resolved.
bugs.workaround: None. Perpetual reboot loops after trying to load FPGA firmware that do not recover typically indicates a hardware error and requires an RMA.
bugs.fix: One of the BARs fails to initialize when the PCIE speed does not load at the intended Generation. This issue was causing a segmentation fault in the SDK, but it has now been resolved by having the SDK notify the fpgamgr of the missing BAR instead. While the device may still fail to load, the fpgamgr will no longer experience a crashing loop as a result.

bugs.title: LDAP Authentication Succeeds for Invalid LDAP Group Due to Server-Side Group Change
bugs.symptoms: F5OS gets the GID value from the server only at commit time on ConfD. Thus, if the GID value changes on the server side, the client (F5OS) has no way of knowing the new GID value. This has resulted in an issue where a user is logging in as a different role.
bugs.conditions: -- Configure LDAP server configuration -- Enable LDAP authentication -- Configure ldap-group -- Log in as an LDAP user that's mapped with the ldap-group configuration -- Change the GID value on the server-side for the user logged in on the above step -- Log in as an LDAP user, and the new GID is not reflected
bugs.impact: - A user with a lower privileged role can be granted an elevated privileged role (security concern) and vice versa
bugs.workaround: If there is any modification on the server-side, recommit LDAP configuration on ConfDCLI so that any of the new information such as GID is been reflected on F5OS system.
bugs.fix: Integrated a polling system for the LDAP server to query periodically to have updated LDAP-group information.

bugs.title: F5OS-A webUI HTTP responses are unexpectedly gzip-compressed
bugs.symptoms:
Accessing random URLs via the F5OS-A webUI (e.g., https:///xyz) returns a gzip-compressed response similar to the following: ``` HTTP/1.1 200 OK Date: Wed, 29 Jan 2025 14:56:13 GMT Server: Apache Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=63072000; includeSubdomains; Last-Modified: Tue, 06 Aug 2024 05:56:33 GMT ETag: "168-61efd74a82640" Accept-Ranges: bytes Content-Length: 360 Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; upgrade-insecure-requests; frame-ancestors 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; connect-src 'self'; font-src 'self'; frame-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; manifest-src 'self'; media-src 'self'; worker-src 'none'; X-XSS-Protection: 1; mode=block Cache-Control: no-cache, must-revalidate Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8 Content-Encoding: gzip <-- Note
```
bugs.conditions: Accessing random URLs via the F5OS-A webUI.
bugs.impact: All responses are compressed, which might trigger a false positives from scanners probing for web-accessible backup files. For example: https://<management IP>/backup.tar.gz Responses are compressed even if a client supplies an 'Accept-Encoding: identity' header. No impact should be observed when accessing URLs from a modern browser with JavaScript enabled. Requests to random URLs will be redirected to the login page. Compression still occurs but improves network performance.
bugs.fix: Fixed this issue in v2.0.0

bugs.title: Restoring a backup with an SNMP user on a system with a different SNMP Engine ID will duplicate the SNMP user
bugs.symptoms: If you restore a backup containing an SNMP user, but the SNMP user’s SNMP Engine ID does not match the current system, a new SNMP user will be created with the same name and the current system’s SNMP Engine ID. However, this is only seen when the database is later backed up.
bugs.conditions: -- Restoring a database backup that contains an SNMP user. -- Doing the restore on a system with a different SNMP Engine ID.
bugs.impact: Two SNMP users with the same name (but different SNMP Engine IDs) are saved to subsequent backups. SNMP will not work.
bugs.workaround: Reconfigure the SNMP user authentication and privacy passwords after restoring the backup. SNMP will work after configuring passwords.
bugs.fix: When backup is restored on a system with a different EngineID, SNMP might not work for SNMP users. However, it can be mitigated by reconfiguring the SNMP user authentication and privacy passwords after restoring the backup.

bugs.title: DDM system alarms triggered when interface is disabled
bugs.symptoms: Running 'show system alarms' reports "Portgroup <N> ERROR Lanes: 1 Transmitter power low alarm"
bugs.conditions: Disabling an interface locally
bugs.impact: Transmitter power low and transmitter bias low alarms occur.
bugs.workaround: To clear the alarms, workaround provided in article K000150155 can be followed.

bugs.title: Fpgamgr failing to clear alarms when unplugging and replugging SFPs combined with disabling/enabling interfaces
bugs.symptoms: Fpgamgr fails to clear the {transmit,receive} {power,bias} {low high} alarms, even though the values are within tolerance.
bugs.conditions: -- Unplugging and replugging SFPs -- Disabling/enabling interfaces at the same time
bugs.impact: The {transmit,receive} {power,bias} {low high} alarms do not clear.

bugs.title: Interfaces do not come up after upgrade
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading, interfaces using unsupported third-party optics will not be marked online.
bugs.conditions: -- Unsupported third-party optics are installed -- An upgrade is performed
bugs.impact: Unsupported third-party optics are not detected and the interface does not come online
bugs.workaround: Use only supported optics. For more information see K000140617: Verify the right optics module to install on your F5OS system https://my.f5.com/s/article/K000140617

bugs.title: Arrow keys do not work in the GRUB edit screen of the console
bugs.symptoms: The arrow keys do not work as expected in the GRUB edit screen in the console.
bugs.conditions: -- Connected via console. -- In the GRUB edit screen. -- Attempting to use arrow keys on the keyboard.
bugs.impact: Unable to select a GRUB image.
bugs.workaround: If connected via SSH, ctrl-p and ctrl-n can be used for up (previous) and down (next). ctrl-b and ctrl-f can be used for left (back) and right (forward). And ctrl-h can be used to delete a character left to the cursor when backspace key does not work. In addition, the grub.cfg file can be modified to make the arrow keys work. Change: serial --speed=115200 terminal_input serial console terminal_output serial console to terminal_input console terminal_output console
bugs.fix: Remove serial port configurations from grub.cfg. Our BIOS supports serial port console emulation that conflicts to the serial port config.

bugs.title: Daemons that handle ZMQ messages may crash under certain conditions.
Orchestration Agent process may core
F5OS chassis switchd core dump
bugs.symptoms: The switchd process experiences crashes that generate core dumps.
bugs.conditions: These crashes are typically observed during certain interface queries or other operations involving statistics updates.
bugs.impact: The switchd process crashes and generates core files. Temporary service disruptions may occur for functionalities reliant on the switchd process.
bugs.fix: This issue has been fixed, ensuring switchd includes proper handling for TMSTAT query.

bugs.title: After a controller failover, sometimes CPU stats not getting displayed in the GUI
bugs.symptoms: After a controller failover, sometimes CPU stats nare not displayed in the GUI.
bugs.conditions: A controller failover occurs
bugs.impact: CPU stats not displayed in the GUI after a controller failover.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue that prevented CPU stats from displaying after a failover.

bugs.title: Timeout for the Ansible playbook during cluster install cannot be retried.
bugs.symptoms: If there are other issues on the chassis that cause the ansible playbooks to run slowly during Kubernetes cluster install, the playbook cannot be retried correctly if it reaches timeout.
bugs.conditions: This can occur, if there are other issues on the chassis that cause the ansible playbooks to run slowly, such as DNS or remote auth issues when a Kubernetes cluster rebuild is executed.
bugs.impact: The Kubernetes cluster install may fail repeatedly because it will not correctly recognize the timeout, and raise the amount of time it will wait.
bugs.workaround: Mitigation is resolve the issue(s) causing the playbooks to run slowly. This may involving removing bad DNS servers or remote auth servers that may be causing the slow down.
bugs.fix: The orchestration-manager code has been updated to correctly recognize the timeout error, and handle it correctly.

bugs.title: Zero is not allowed as Prefix Length for allowed IPs
bugs.symptoms: It is not possible to save a prefix length with a value of ‘0’.
bugs.conditions: Prefix Length value is configured to '0'.
bugs.impact: Allowed IPs cannot be created with prefix value '0'.
bugs.workaround: Works from CLI.
bugs.fix: Fixed to accept '0' as prefix length value.

bugs.title: Tenant may not come to Running state after quick movement of slots between partitions
bugs.symptoms: After quick movement of a slot between different partitions, it is possible that tenants on that slot will not come back to the Running state.
bugs.conditions: This situation can occur if nodes are moved from current partition to another partition and then back to original partition.
bugs.impact: Tenant may not come to Running state.
bugs.workaround: Toggle the running-state of the tenant from deployed to configured and then back to deployed.

bugs.title: BX520 Port LED solidly illuminated indicating link up while system software reports link down.
bugs.symptoms: The BX520 Port LED may be solidly illuminated indicating link up while system software reports link down. This is typically a transient condition during initial port bringup. If it persists, it could be an indication of a problem with the fiber or at the link partner.
bugs.conditions: The BX520 Port LED is illuminated solid when the associated port has achieved RX alignment. The system software indicates port status UP when the BX520 port has achieved RX Alignment AND the link partner has also signaled it has achieved RX Alignment through the 802.3 Remote Fault Indicator protocol. It is expected that there may be transient cases of this during port bringup. If it persists, it can be an indication that the BX520 was able to achieve RX alignment but the link partner was not.
bugs.impact: Differences in Link status as reported by HW LED and SW Status can cause confusion.

bugs.title: Partition 'cluster reboot all' can be excessively slow
bugs.symptoms: The 'cluster reboot' command does detect if a blade is present in the chassis before attempting to reboot it. It takes 5 to 10 seconds to issue the reboot, regardless of whether the blade exists, and this operation is performed sequentially across all blades assigned to the partition.
bugs.conditions: Empty/unused chassis slots assigned to a partition.
bugs.impact: The 'cluster reboot all' command can take several minutes to complete and report status.
bugs.workaround: Using the chassis CLI or UI, assign empty/unused blade slots to partition 'none'.

bugs.title: LDAP Remote user may show as a different user after logging in to the system
bugs.symptoms: LDAP Remote user may show as a different user after logging in to the system and using the 'who' command.
bugs.conditions: LDAP auth is not configured at the time the local user is created, then LDAP auth is configured.
bugs.impact: If LDAP auth is not configured at the time the local user is created, the account could potentially end up with the same local user's UIDs. However, the permissions will not be be determined by the UIDs, therefore the account is required to have the correct permissions.

bugs.title: LDAP authentication certificate text greater than 8 KB may cause issues
bugs.symptoms: Configuring TLS certificates or keys or CA certificates for LDAP authentication that are larger than 8 KiB does not work, and results in LDAP authentication configuration changes no longer taking effect; LDAP authentication continues with the previous configuration. Log messages such as the following in velos.log or platform.log: authd[11]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x3901000000000001 msg="cdb_get failed" ret=-1 confd_errno=21 fmt="/system/aaa/authentication/ldap/tls_cacert".
bugs.conditions: - Configuring LDAP authentication on F5OS - Attempting to configure certificate or key material that is 8 KiB in size or larger, e.g. a large set of CA certificates.
bugs.impact: LDAP authentication does not work and attempts to make further configuration changes (i.e. changing the LDAP servers used for authentication) will not take effect until the issue with the certificates are addressed.
bugs.fix: TLS CA certificates and certificate and key buffers have been expanded from 8 KiB to 64 KiB.

bugs.title: Intermittent traffic failures with tenant when round-robin DAG is enabled on a VLAN
bugs.symptoms: Intermittent traffic failures for traffic in a tenant on VLANs with round-robin DAG enabled. In particular, this can manifest as monitor traffic intermittently failing (pool members flapping).
bugs.conditions: - Tenant running BIG-IP v17.1.2 or above - VLAN is configured for round-robin DAG (RRDAG) in the tenant ("dag-round-robin enabled") - Host is one of the following platforms: -- r5000, r10000, or r12000-series appliance -- VELOS - Host is running F5OS-A 1.8.0 or above (rSeries appliance) or F5OS-C 1.8.0 or above (VELOS chassis)
bugs.impact: Intermittent traffic disruption. This often manifests as ICMP monitors intermittently failing, but will also impact virtual server traffic and other protocols (e.g. UDP and TCP).

bugs.title: Cmp_dest may give incorrect results on rSeries.
bugs.symptoms: Cmd_dest may give incorrect results when run on an rSeries appliance.
bugs.conditions: Cmp_dest command is run on an rSeries appliance.
bugs.impact: Has no impact on platform behavior, but may affect analysis of port distribution.
bugs.fix: Fixed cmp_dest when run on an rSeries appliance.

bugs.title: Error log does not contain all needed information.
bugs.symptoms: An "Interface data differ" log is logged by l2-agent, but all of the compared fields in the log message are identical.
bugs.conditions: L2-agent logs an error message that the interface data differs.
bugs.impact: The lack of some data such as interface type and slot ID in the log entry makes troubleshooting more complex.
bugs.workaround: Save the backup configuration file, and inspect the file for hidden fields. For example, search for pgindex under the interface entry.
bugs.fix: With this change, the log ERROR will display all required data.

bugs.title: Update ConfD CLI Help Text for SANs Input
bugs.symptoms: In the ConfD CLI, the help text for SANs located at `/system/aaa/tls/create-csr/sans` and `/system/aaa/tls/create-self-signed-cert/san` does not specify the required format.
bugs.conditions: User display help text for SAN field (/system/aaa/tls/create-csr/sans, /system/aaa/tls/create-self-signed-cert/san)
bugs.impact: Due to the absence of a format specification for help text in the SAN field, the user was unable to set the values correctly.
bugs.fix: Please update the display example for SAN fields to eliminate any ambiguity regarding the SAN field.

bugs.title: F5OS webUI: Remove mandatory requirement for e-mail in CSR creation
bugs.symptoms: When generating a Certificate Signing Request (CSR) via the F5OS webUI, the e-mail address field is incorrectly marked as mandatory.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to create a CSR using the F5OS webUI.
bugs.impact: Users cannot generate a CSR through the webUI without providing an e-mail address, even though the field should be optional.
bugs.workaround: To generate a Certificate Signing Request (CSR) without including an e-mail address, use the F5OS ConfD CLI instead of the webUI.
bugs.fix: The F5OS web UI has been updated to correctly treat the e-mail address field as optional during Certificate Signing Request (CSR) generation. Users can now successfully generate a CSR without providing an e-mail address.

bugs.title: F5OS LLDP details page cannot display information about neighbors with matching port IDs
bugs.symptoms: On the LLDP Details page in the F5OS GUI, clicking on a neighbor row expands to show information about the neighbor system. If the F5OS system is connected to the same interface on multiple peer switches, the F5OS GUI will always show neighbor information for the first matching interface. For example: F5OS interface 3.0 => switch 1 xe-0/0/38 F5OS interface 4.0 => switch 2 xe-0/0/38 The F5OS system is connected to port xe-0/0/38 on two different switches, and attempting to use the F5OS GUI to view neighbor information for the neighbor on interface 4.0 will show the information from interface 3.0.
bugs.conditions: F5OS system with LLDP enabled. Multiple interfaces on the F5OS system connected to the same port ID on distinct switches.
bugs.impact: Unable to use the GUI to view neighbor information about some LLDP
bugs.workaround: Use the CLI or API to retrieve information about LLDP neighbors. For example, log into the CLI as an admin user and run "show lldp interfaces interface neighbor"
bugs.fix: The issue is fixed in new look and feel, now preview pane shows correct data even of the ids are same for two neighbours.

bugs.title: Missing internal interface pgindex field causes l2-agent to restart
bugs.symptoms: Upon upgrade from 1.1 -> 1.6 -> 1.8, l2-agent on blade will exit due to interface data mismatch. This mismatch happens because the pgindex hidden leaf is missing from cdb, but the l2-agent on blade expects it.
bugs.conditions: Chain upgraded from 1.1 -> 1.6 -> 1.8. Version 1.8 is the version where l2-agent added more logic to check interface data inconsistency.
bugs.impact: Dataplane is not functioning.
bugs.workaround: Work around is to delete the blades from the partition and re-add them. This will require user to reconfigure interface data (vlans, lag members).
bugs.fix: With this fix, the upgrade into 1.8 will work as expected, and l2-agent on the blade will find matching interface data.

bugs.title: Standby tenant is unreachable after F5OS partition upgrade to 1.7.x or higher.
bugs.symptoms: - The `tmsh show net arp` may show arps with an unknown status. - The confd CLI `show dag-states` command shows dag tables consisting of only zeros.
bugs.conditions: * Multi-slot tenant in a device group * Connection mirroring enabled * Upgrade F5OS partition from 1.6.x to 1.7.x or greater
bugs.impact: Standby tenant is inaccessible.
bugs.fix: This issue has been fixed in F5OS partition upgrades to 1.7.x or higher.

bugs.title: Version option is not need when creating Certificate Signing Request
bugs.symptoms: GUI is showing a version field that you can fill in when creating a Certificate Signing Request. But this option is not required.
bugs.conditions: Creating a Certificate Signing Request via the GUI.
bugs.impact: The option is not needed, the field value is ignored.
bugs.fix: The field is removed now from the Certificate Signing Request form.

bugs.title: Version option is not required when creating Certificate Signing Request via CLI
bugs.symptoms: CLI contains an option to specify a version field that you can fill in when creating a Certificate Signing Request. But this option is not used or required.
bugs.conditions: Creating a Certificate Signing Request via CLI.
bugs.impact: The option is not needed, the field value is ignored.
bugs.fix: The field is removed now from the Certificate Signing Request form.

bugs.title: Users unable to login after reboot with LDAP group configured
bugs.symptoms: - CLI/GUI access for all roles other than admin and root is denied - The GUI permit user authentication and then immediately terminate the session; for more information, refer to https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID1933645.html. - Repeated log messages from user-manager in platform.log / velos.log with an error of "Lost connection to ConfD" / "Socket to ConfD is closed": user-manager[17]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x6802000000000001 msg="cdb_get failed for" ATTRIBUTE="rolename" ERRNOSTR="Lost connection to ConfD" LASTERR="Socket to ConfD is closed" ERRNO=45.
bugs.conditions: - LDAP system authentication is enabled - A LDAP group is defined for a role in the system - Queries to the LDAP server take a long time, for example due to connection timeouts or LDAP referral chasing. This issue can also occur when the system is rebooted if user-manager tries to perform LDAP queries before the management network is accessible.
bugs.impact: Users with roles other than admin and root cannot login using CLI or GUI
bugs.workaround: 1. Restart the appropriate user-manager container (system_user_manager on rSeries appliances, controller-userman for VELOS system controllers, and partition<ID>_user_manager for VELOS partitions) 2. Disable LDAP system authentication or remove the LDAP group definitions, and then restart the user-manager container. This will restore connectivity for locally-defined users.
bugs.fix: Fix users unable to login after reboot with LDAP group configured

bugs.title: Inconsistency with network interface alarms
bugs.symptoms: An example of the issue: Both portgroup 3/1 and 3/2 have state ddm rx-pwr instant val-lane4 = -40.0, but only one reports an alarm. There also seems to be a discrepancy regarding the alarms and the logs The alarm log from velos.log reports an error from Portgroup 3/1: fpgamgr[13]: nodename=blade-3(p3) priority="Warn" version=1.0 msgid=0x304000000000012 msg="DDM low warning set" PORTGROUP="3/1" ALARMTYPE="receive power" LANE1=-0.029600 LANE2=-0.008900 LANE3=-0.046900 LANE4=-0.400000. But the alarm is reported for Portgroup 3/2: # show system alarms ID RESOURCE SEVERITY TEXT TIME CREATED ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 262401 Portgroup 3/2 ERROR Lanes: 4 Receiver power low alarm 2025-02-12 09:10:19.603552427 UTC
bugs.conditions: Both interfaces enabled, but disconnected (no cables inserted). Affects both VELOS and rSeries (r5000, r10000, r12000)
bugs.impact: Inconsistent alarms may be reported for only one of the Portgroups when both Portgroups have low rx-power values.

bugs.title: Optic removed while system down does not get removed from ConfD state
bugs.symptoms: The fpgamgr publishes portgroup state data to ConfD when an optic is inserted in the system. The portgroup state data is erased from ConfD when the optic is removed while the system is operational. If an optic is removed while the system is down the portgroup state data does not get erased.
bugs.conditions: Optic is removed while the system is down.
bugs.impact: Unexpected/undesired operational data appearing in ConfD output.
bugs.fix: Erased the portgroup operational data if the corresponding optic is not present.

bugs.title: VELOS partition Allowed IP rule restrictions
Stp stats (ex counters) are not reset when stp mode removed and added again.
bugs.symptoms: Stp stats (ex counters) are not reset to 0 when stp mode removed and added again. steps add STP > stp global config enabled-protocol STP > stp interfaces <> > stp stp interfaces <> remove STP > no stp stp interfaces > no stp interfaces > no stp global config add stp mode > stp global config enabled-protocol RSTP > stp interfaces <> > stp rstp interfaces <> check stp states and check "BPDU RECEIVED" > show stp old BPDU's counters are not reset to 0.
bugs.conditions: STP mode is removed and added again.
bugs.impact: No impact on functionality but you will see old BPDU's counter stats base instead of starting from 0.
bugs.workaround: There is no impact on functionality but restart of the device will reset the stats counters.

bugs.title: Memory leak in l2_agent daemon on F5OS
bugs.symptoms: - Large memory consumption by the l2_agent. - Tenant disruption on F5 rSeries appliance.
bugs.conditions: - An F5OS system with SNMP configured and a LAG (Link Aggregation Group) with more than 1 member. - SNMP monitoring in use. We can check the l2_agent memory consumption by using `top` command. Ex: Top output showed a 15GB l2_agent process: PID USER PR NI VIRT RES SHR S %CPU %MEM TIME+ COMMAND 19454 root 20 0 17.3g 14.9g 1788 S 0.0 5.9 174:04.57 /confd/bin/l2_agent -s appliance-1
bugs.impact: Eventually the system experience OOM (Out of Memory). On an F5 rSeries appliance, a tenant might experience disruptions and slowness, up to and including a TMM SIGABRT core.
bugs.fix: The l2_agent process no longer leaks memory.

bugs.title: "show system install" to be part of system-manager qkview
bugs.symptoms: Show system install was missing from qkview
bugs.conditions: Generating a qkview file
bugs.impact: This will help to diagnose issues related to firmware install

bugs.title: Port not enabling after SFP connection when previously disabled
bugs.symptoms: The port is disabled, and after connecting the optic to it, enabling the port does not bring it up automatically
bugs.conditions: When Optics connected to a disabled port
bugs.impact: Link is not coming up
bugs.workaround: Remove and reconnected the SFP after port is enabled.

bugs.title: CVE 2020-27743: pam_tacplus through 1.5.1 lacks a check for a failure of RAND_bytes()/RAND_pseudo_bytes().
bugs.symptoms: libtac in pam_tacplus through 1.5.1 lacks a check for a failure of RAND_bytes()/RAND_pseudo_bytes(). This could lead to use of a non-random/predictable session_id.
bugs.conditions: The current version pam_tacplus from version 1.6.0 doesn't have the fix as this was added in version 1.6.1 source package.
bugs.impact: This could lead to use of a non-random/predictable session_id which means an adversary could gain access.
bugs.fix: By updating the pam_tacplus source code to 1.7.0 where the vulnerability was fixed in 1.6.1, the new code does not have this issue.

bugs.title: F5OS LDAP operations from authentication-manager and user-manager do not respect timeouts or chase-referrals
bugs.symptoms: LDAP queries performed by authentication-manager and user-manager do not respect some of the LDAP configuration, in particular chase-referrals and connection and bind timeouts. LDAP queries take an extensive period of time. This can result in user-manager losing its connection to confd, resulting in the problems described in https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID1858617.html
bugs.conditions: - LDAP system authentication - authentication-manager trying to query the directory, which will occur if active_directory is enabled and unix_attributes is disabled. - user-manager trying to query the directory, which will occur if an LDAP group mapping is defined for a user role.
bugs.impact: Remotely-authenticated users will not work. Further problems may occur as described in https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID1858617.html

bugs.title: REST API for Docker Restart command fails
bugs.symptoms: The endpoint restconf/data/openconfig-system:system/f5-system-diagnostics-qkview:diagnostics/f5-system-diagnostics-docker:os-utils/f5-system-diagnostics-docker:docker/f5-system-diagnostics-docker:restart can be used (with POST) to restart some Docker containers. However it will fail with the message "restart aborted", e.g.: { "f5-system-diagnostics-docker:output": { "result": "snmpd restart aborted" } }
bugs.conditions: Attempting to restart a Docker container using the REST API.
bugs.impact: Unable to use the REST API to restart a Docker container.
bugs.workaround: Use the CLI instead: config system diagnostics os-utils docker restart node <node> service <service>

bugs.title: The network-manager container crashes when it fails to create FDB entry in database
bugs.symptoms: Network-manager container crashes.
bugs.conditions: The issue may occur when there is an upgrade/downgrade, tenant creation/deletion, or reset/restore the database.
bugs.impact: The network-manager container will restart.
bugs.fix: The network-manager will not crash when it fails to create FDB entry in database.

bugs.title: Health summary is not reported for some nodes in controller and partition ConfD
bugs.symptoms: System health summary is missing for some nodes.
bugs.conditions: It is observed when iso is upgraded to 1.8.1 branch
bugs.impact: System health summary is not reported for some nodes. It throws error while fetching summary.
bugs.fix: Updated Node tag in components properly. Since GET:health api is fixed in diag-agent, Show system health summary reports etails properly for all nodes.

bugs.title: F5OS password policy's "max-letter-repeat" description is incorrect
bugs.symptoms: In the CLI, the description for "max-letter-repeat" in the password policy ("system aaa password-policy") has an incorrect description. Currently it states that it, "Reject passwords with this many repeating lower-case letters in the password". It actually applies to any repeating consecutive characters, not just lower-case letters.
bugs.conditions: Viewing the CLI's online help for the password policy's "max-letter-repeat" setting.
bugs.impact: The incorrect description may lead to an unintended password policy.

bugs.title: Traffic over a LAG not working after upgrade from v1.6.2 to v1.8.0 or v1.8.1
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading from v1.6.2 to v1.8.0 or v1.8.1, the internal LAG programming may become faulty, resulting in incorrect configuration of interfaces within the LAG. This issue disrupts the proper flow of traffic.
bugs.conditions: Upgrade from v1.6.2 to v1.8.0 or v1.8.1
bugs.impact: Traffic over the LAG does not work correctly.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the blades hosting the members of the LAG.

bugs.title: Traffic over a LAG not working after upgrade from v1.6.2 to v1.8.0 or v1.8.1
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading from v1.6.2 to v1.8.0 or v1.8.1, the internal LAG programming may become faulty, resulting in incorrect configuration of interfaces within the LAG. This issue disrupts the proper flow of traffic.
bugs.conditions: Upgrade from v1.6.2 to v1.8.0 or v1.8.1
bugs.impact: Traffic over the LAG doesn’t work correctly.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the blades hosting the members of the LAG.

bugs.title: L2 Port motion events are not generated for certain port combinations on r10k.
bugs.symptoms: Missing port-motion events between interfaces on r10k platform can result in missing L2 entries.
bugs.impact: Missing port-motion causes missing L2 entries, resulting in excessive DLFs.
bugs.workaround: Ensure that ports used in redundancy configurations are not in the same set of affected ports listed above.
bugs.fix: Configure the L2 FDB table so port-motion is detected between the affected sets of ports.

bugs.title: Capture /etc/prompt-status part of qkview
bugs.symptoms: The /etc/prompt-status contents are not captured part of qkview
bugs.conditions: Analyzing a qkview file
bugs.impact: Not having contents of /etc/prompt-status can impede issue diagnosis.
bugs.workaround: Capture manually from the system
bugs.fix: Fixed in v2.0.0

bugs.title: High memory utilization by NetworkManager
bugs.symptoms: After a VELOS system controller, blade, or rSeries appliance has been running for several hundred days, the NetworkManager service may start leaking memory. This will eventually result in system instability including a failover between system controllers, or instability to tenants. Log messages similar to the following occurring in /var/log/messages or the systemd journal: controller-2.chassis.local NetworkManager[180091]: gsignal.c:2642: instance '0x564069a2be40' has no handler with id '34120' Prior to these log messages being generated, there is no way to tell if the issue is close to occurring.
bugs.conditions: The NetworkManager service has been running for a substantial period of time (i.e. more than 500 days).
bugs.impact: NetworkManager service utilizes high memory in the system, which leads to controller failover.
bugs.workaround: Restart NetworkManager by logging in to the appropriate device as root (system controller, blade, or appliance) and running the command "systemctl restart NetworkManager".

bugs.title: Core file generated while QkView upload in ihealth server
bugs.symptoms: Core file getting generated when QkView file is uploading in ihealth server.
bugs.conditions: QkView upload in ihealth server.
bugs.impact: QkView upload will fail.
bugs.workaround: Retry the QkView upload.
bugs.fix: Fixed the issue that caused core.

bugs.title: When attributes are added under exporters for Open Telemetry, the keys are not visible in the GUI.
bugs.symptoms: When attributes are added under exporters for Open Telemetry, the keys are not visible in the GUI. If any exporters have existing attributes and you try to edit the exporter from the GUI, the attributes get deleted.
bugs.conditions: Adding or updating attributes to an open telemetry exporter through the GUI.
bugs.impact: -- New attributes created under exporters don not have their keys visible in the GUI. -- Editing the exporter from the GUI will delete existing attributes.
bugs.workaround: Add attributes to exporters or update existing exporters via the CLI.

bugs.title: During partition software upgrade dagd process may crash and dump a core
bugs.symptoms: During partition software upgrade (or when multiple blades are restarted simultaneously), dagd process crashes and produces a core dumpump a core.
bugs.conditions: One of: -- Partition software version is upgraded. -- Multiple blades are restarted at the same time.
bugs.impact: This has no impact except for the core dump.
bugs.workaround: Prior to a partition software upgrade, manually move your tenants into provisioned running state.
bugs.fix: Fixed dagd core dump during partition software upgrade.

bugs.title: LDAP role mappings may not update after LDAP configuration changes.
bugs.symptoms: User role mappings may become outdated or incorrect after changes to LDAP configuration settings.
bugs.conditions: Occurs when LDAP settings are modified after roles are already configured, such as changes to bind credentials, server groups, unix-attributes, authentication method, or other LDAP options.
bugs.impact: Users may receive incorrect roles or experience authorization issues until role mappings are refreshed.
bugs.workaround: Reconfigure or refresh LDAP role mappings after making LDAP configuration changes. appliance-1(config)# system aaa authentication roles role <role> config ldap-group <ldap-group>
bugs.fix: Improved LDAP change detection and remapping logic so role mappings are automatically updated when LDAP configuration settings change.

bugs.title: Egress traffic is being dropped by upstream switch following a reboot of rSeries.
bugs.symptoms: Intermittently observed egress packets sent from the rSeries device through a specific port are discarded by the adjacent device.
bugs.conditions: - r5000, r10000, or r12000-series appliance - Intermittently occurs when a link is brought up during boot, for instance after multiple reboot attempts.
bugs.impact: Traffic on the affected port is completely dropped when the system comes up after a reboot. This includes the failure of all Layer 2 (L2) protocols, such as LACP, STP, and LLDP, along with tenant traffic.
bugs.workaround: An additional reboot helps to recover the system.

bugs.title: "Failed to write to cdb" and "Unable to set STP VLAN state" error logs are seen with MSTP configuration deletion via CLI
bugs.symptoms: Stpd and FPGA error logs are observed while doing MSTP configuration. In platform.log: stpd[1]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x6102000000000018 msg="Failed to write to cdb" FIELD="MST Instance mst-id" ERRNO=8 ERRNOSTR="badly formatted or nonexistent path". stpd[1]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x6102000000000018 msg="Failed to write to cdb" FIELD="MST Instance designated-root-address" ERRNO=8 ERRNOSTR="badly formatted or nonexistent path". stpd[1]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x6102000000000018 msg="Failed to write to cdb" FIELD="WriteTenantOperMSTInstance failed" ERRNO=0 ERRNOSTR="Unknown error".
bugs.conditions: 1. Create VLANs. 2. Attach VLANs to the interfaces. 3. Enable MSTP using webUI. Select Network Settings > STP configuration and select MSTP. 4. Create an instance(1) and attach a VLAN to it (created VLANs). 5. Add the interfaces to instance 1. 6. Delete mstp instance. 7. You will observe errors under platform.log.
bugs.impact: There is no impact on MSTP behavior and convergence.
bugs.fix: The fix added to change the deletion logic so that STP state is only reset on interfaces belonging to the MST instance.

bugs.title: "system diagnostics net-utils tcpdump" Tab Completion Does Not Show Option Descriptions
bugs.symptoms: When using the system diagnostics net-utils tcpdump command and pressing Tab for completion, the CLI only lists the available keywords and flags, but does not display any descriptive information for those options.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when a user runs: appliance-1# system diagnostics net-utils tcpdump <Tab> on the appliance CLI to view available tcpdump options under net-utils
bugs.impact: Users only see a list of possible completions (such as --timeout, -c, -w, bpf, count, filter, outfile) with no description of what each option does. This makes the interface less user-friendly, forces users to rely on external documentation or prior knowledge, and can slow down troubleshooting or diagnostics activities.
bugs.fix: After the fix, when the user enters: system diagnostics net-utils tcpdump <Tab> The CLI will display both possible completions and brief descriptions for each option, similar to the behavior of the system diagnostic tcpdump command. This provides inline guidance on tcpdump parameters, improving usability and reducing the need to reference external documentation.

bugs.title: Resolved Tcpdump Issue of Capturing Packets Indefinitely with Count Set to 0
bugs.symptoms: Tcpdump does not stop capturing packets when the packet count is set to zero; instead, it continues running indefinitely until it is manually interrupted.
bugs.conditions: This issue arises when tcpdump is initiated with the packet count parameter set to zero or a value that equates to zero. This leads to the capture process running indefinitely without a natural termination condition.
bugs.impact: Prolonged or unintended packet captures can lead to increased resource usage (CPU, memory, and disk), potential log or storage exhaustion, and operational overhead, as administrators must manually detect and stop the capture process.
bugs.fix: Updated tcpdump behavior so that when the packet count is configured as zero, it is handled correctly and no longer causes the capture to run indefinitely. Tcpdump now terminates as expected based on the configured capture limits, preventing unintended long‑running captures and excessive resource usage.

bugs.title: Unable to capture tcpdump packets if the mgmt interfaces are aggregated
bugs.symptoms: Tcpdump on the management port will not be executed if the management ports are part of a LAG (Link Aggregation Group). Logs report 'mgmt port in lagError': # system diagnostics net-utils tcpdump tcpdump: unsupported configuration: mgmt port in lagError: application error
bugs.conditions: -- Running tcpdump on the management port -- The management ports are in lags.
bugs.impact: Fail to running tcpdump on management port on F5OS-C if management ports are in lags.

bugs.title: GUI immediately logs user off with "User Session Terminated" error and "validator" process cores
bugs.symptoms: After logging into the device, the GUI immediately reports "User Session Terminated. You will be logged out of the application." Core files generated from the "validator" process in the confd container (system_manager, vcc-confd, or partition<X>_manager).
bugs.conditions: Trying to login to the GUI, and the "limited" group is missing from /etc/group. The "limited" group is an internal role that should always be defined and cannot be deleted by a user. The most likely reason for it to be missing is https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID1858617.html
bugs.impact: Users are not able to access the GUI.
bugs.workaround: Apply a workaround for https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID1858617.html
bugs.fix: Even if the "limited" group goes missing, users should still be able to access the GUI.

bugs.title: Interface remain down in F5OS after removing and reinserting SFP modules
bugs.symptoms: After SFPs are removed and reinserted in a VELOS blade, the interface will remain down in F5OS until the blade is rebooted. The peer switch may report the interfaces as having a link.
bugs.conditions: - VELOS chassis running F5OS-C 1.8.0 - SFPs in blade are removed and reinserted.
bugs.impact: F5OS interfaces remain reported as operationally down until the blade is rebooted.
bugs.workaround: After SFP modules are removed and reinserted on a blade, reboot the blade.

bugs.title: SNMP PSU stats display incorrect measurement units
bugs.symptoms: SNMP PSU statistics output shows the numerical reading, followed by an incorrect measurement unit (milli-<unit>) instead of whole units. mV -> (V)olts mW -> (W)atts mA -> (A)mps
bugs.conditions: SNMP polling for PSU Statistics.
bugs.impact: Cosmetic only. Numerical values are correct but annotation includes 'm'before the unit of measure. "psu-1" = INTEGER: 9.671 mA. "psu-1" = INTEGER: 206.000 mV "psu-1" = INTEGER: 1872.000 mW The measurements are in whole units: (A)mps, (V)olts or (W)atts.

bugs.title: Infrequent and uneven traffic to front panel LAGs can lead to premature aging of L2 events
bugs.symptoms: For front panel LAGs on rSeries which span FPGAs (1.0/11.0, 2.0/12.0, etc) infrequent traffic which is not evenly distributed across the LAG members can lead to premature aging of L2 entries.
bugs.conditions: - r10000 or r12000-series appliance - LAG members spanning FPGAs and minimal incoming traffic on the LAG can cause premature aging of L2 entries when the traffic isn't evenly distributed among LAG members.
bugs.impact: Missing L2 entries can cause excessive DLFs until the MAC address is re-learned.
bugs.workaround: Re-configure the LAG members such that they connect to the same FPGA (1.0/2.0, 11.0/12.0). Interfaces 1.0 through 10.0 are on one FPGA, and interfaces 11.0 through 20.0 are on the other FPGA.
bugs.fix: Ensure L2 age events are handled for all LAG members.

bugs.title: Logging doest work properly if wrong tls is configured for remote log servers
bugs.symptoms: Logging is halted qkview generation fails
bugs.conditions: -- F5OS configured for remote log server authentication for secure log forwarding. -- TLS settings are missing or incorrect
bugs.impact: F5OS logging will be stopped.
bugs.workaround: Fix the wrong or missed tls configuration for remote logging servers.
bugs.fix: The log forwarding actions should be fine tuned so that F5OS logging continues to work even in case of wrong tls is configured.

bugs.title: DOC: EtherLike-MIB file need to be updated for unsupported OID
bugs.symptoms: Document update with F5OS supported OIDs in the EtherLike-MIB
bugs.conditions: Its a documentation bug.
bugs.impact: No functional impact.
bugs.workaround: NA
bugs.fix: Updated KB article (https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000151374)

bugs.title: Failed to Verify CA with basicConstraints.CA Set to False
bugs.symptoms: Client Certificate verification and client certificate authentication fail if the CA's basicConstraints.CA is set to false. This is due to the upgrade of the Apache version from 1.0. x to 1.1.1 in the F5OS-200 release
bugs.conditions: -- Set ca-bundle with basicConstraints.CA set to false in F5OS -- Enable client certificate verification or/and/or client certificate authentication -- Try to log in using certificates
bugs.impact: The user who uses CA with basicConstraint.CA=FALSE will no longer be to use cert-based auth after 200 version.
bugs.workaround: Generate CA with basicConstraints.CA=True when upgrading to 200.

bugs.title: Partitions can leave stale tenant pods when controller configuration reset to default is issued
bugs.symptoms: Partition tenants that are configured with slots greater than max-nodes can fail to come back when resetting the controller configuration and restoring it back via save configuration for controller and partition.
bugs.conditions: Occurs typically when - Partition with ID 1 - Tenant uses virtual slots that do not match the physical slot. - Controller reset-to-default is issued
bugs.impact: Stale tenant pods for partition 1 tenants will still show after restoring the controller configuration and partition configuration, but the impacted tenants may not came back up fully (multinodes case).
bugs.workaround: - Bring partition tenants down if planning to do controller configuration reset-to-default. or - Manually delete default partition 1 after reset-to-default before restoring the save controller configuration. This should take care of removing everything associated to the namespace before the config-restore happens. Partitions with ID different than 1 should clear the namespace automatically, since they don't get recreated as part of reset-to-default.
bugs.fix: Startup stale cleanup logic has been adjusted to manage multinode and virtual slots tenants appropriately.

bugs.title: Unable to launch tenant, as VF interface missing under "ip link show" across reboots
bugs.symptoms: On r2x00/r4x00 related systems, tenant launch fails with an error in ConfD tenant status leaf: "error adding container to network "sriov-net3-bip1": failed to set up pod interface "net7" from the device "x557_4": failed to set netlink MAC address to <mac>: resource temporarily unavailable" or "SRIOV-CNI failed to load netconf: LoadConf(): the VF 0000:ec:01.3 does not have a interface name or a dpdk driver" Linux network manager udev rules and sriov cni try to access the VF and change the interface name of VF. During this process, VFs fail and unable to retrieve. Thus, resource temporarily unavailable error occurs.
bugs.conditions: On r4x00 or r2x00 based systems: 1. In kubectl get pods -A output, the tenant pod goes into Init:0/1 state. default virt-launcher-bip1-1-t6rkh 0/1 Init:0/1 0 36s 2. And in kubectl events, "resource temporarily unavailable" occurs on one of the VFs. 3. In /sys/class/net folder unable to see the below VF interfaces. Instead, some interfaces point to ensp* names which are wrong. 4. Under "ip link show <pf>" you may see the missing VFs. (Example: ip link show x557_1)
bugs.impact: Tenant launch is unsuccessful and unable to connect to the tenant console or tenants' management connection.
bugs.workaround: 1. Set all tenants to the Configured state. 2. Reboot the appliance. 3. Once the system is up, change one tenant’s state to Deployed at a time, allowing a gap of 3–5 minutes before moving to the next tenant. 4. Repeat this process until all tenants are deployed.

bugs.title: QKView creation status does not update automatically in the GUI.
bugs.symptoms: When generating a QKView via the web UI, the progress status remains at "Collecting - 0% completed" and does not update automatically.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using the GUI to generate a system diagnostics report (QKView). The status updates only if the user manually refreshes the page or switches windows.
bugs.impact: Users cannot track the real-time progress of QKView creation through the GUI. The display may incorrectly suggest the process is stalled at 0%.
bugs.workaround: Manually refresh the browser page or navigate to a different GUI screen and back to update the status.
bugs.fix: The GUI now correctly reflects the real-time progress of QKView generation without requiring a manual page refresh.

bugs.title: Rpm -q does not list all installed packages in hal-services
bugs.symptoms: Hal-services containers copied /lib/libzmq.so.5, instead of installing the libzmq rpm, which led to issues when building a sysroot for debugging core files.
bugs.conditions: NA
bugs.impact: Caused issues while debugging core files.
bugs.workaround: NA
bugs.fix: Rpm -q lists all installed packages in hal-services

bugs.title: Qkview-collect crashes while collecting a QKView
bugs.symptoms: Qkview-collect may crash when collecting a QKView.
bugs.conditions: This happens intermittently when collecting a QKView.
bugs.impact: Unable to collect a QKView.

bugs.title: TCPDUMP on Management Port Fails to Exit Gracefully After Restart
bugs.symptoms: When a network capture (tcpdump) is running on the management interface and the underlying diagnostic service is restarted, the tcpdump session does not terminate gracefully. Instead of exiting with a clear status and packet summary, the command ends with an “application communication failure” message, providing no proper indication that the diagnostic service was restarted.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when a tcpdump capture is running on the management interface and the underlying diagnostic service responsible for tcpdump is restarted while the capture is still in progress.
bugs.impact: The tcpdump session terminates with an “application communication failure” instead of a clear, informative message and packet summary. This can mislead administrators into suspecting a network or application issue, complicate troubleshooting, and require them to rerun captures to obtain complete diagnostic data.
bugs.fix: When a tcpdump capture is running on the management interface and the underlying diagnostic service is restarted, the tcpdump session now terminates gracefully. The command exits with a clear, informative message indicating that the diagnostic service was restarted and provides the expected packet summary, instead of reporting an “application communication failure.”

bugs.title: Deployment fails to start after downgrading from a USB-installed version 2.0.0-2690 to 1.8.0-9682
bugs.symptoms: Unable to access the system when we downgrade from 2.x bare metal to 1.x version because of VDO backward compatibility issue.
bugs.conditions: 1. Do baremetal installation of 2.x version 2. Downgrade to 1.x version 3. Check the system (VDO.service)
bugs.impact: Unable to access the system.
bugs.fix: This issue is fixed in F5OS v2.0. Replaced VDO with lvm.

bugs.title: When setting "Apply Policy on Setting Passwords for User Accounts" to false, trying to change user password fails and triggers application timeout
bugs.symptoms: - The GUI reports a Server Error 'application timeout' when attempting to change a user's password. - Attempting to load the "Users & Roles" page fails with the error "Failure for data/openconfig-system:system/aaa/authentication/f5-system-aaa:roles/role API. The server or an underlying service is unreachable."
bugs.conditions: - F5OS system - The local password policy "Apply Policy on Setting Passwords for User Accounts" option (referred to as "apply-to-root" in the CLI and API) is set to "false". The default for this option is "true". - Attempt to change a user's password.
bugs.impact: The user manager daemon is temporarily unresponsive. It should recover after approximately five minutes. Attempts to change user's password does not take effect and authentication fails when using the new password.
bugs.workaround: Set the "Apply Policy on Setting Passwords for User Accounts" / "apply-to-root" option to "true".

bugs.title: Tenant file system stats fail to clear after deleting a tenant
bugs.symptoms: When running "show components component state file-systems", a row of file system data will appear for a previously deleted tenant.
bugs.conditions: A tenant is deleted.
bugs.impact: This is cosmetic only. It is stale data captured before the tenant was deleted.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the system to clear the stale data.

bugs.title: SSH configuration file on the active controller can be corrupted
bugs.symptoms: It is possible that the SSH configuration file on the active controller can become corrupted.
bugs.conditions: The SSH configuration file is not protected correctly from the multi-threaded orchestration-manager process.
bugs.impact: Host names that do not correspond to the correct IP addresses are observed.
bugs.workaround: The corrupted configuration file required to be fixed manually.
bugs.fix: This issue is fixed.

bugs.title: Tcpdump performance improvement
bugs.symptoms: There were a lot of drop logged for tcpdump when under large amount of traffic.
bugs.conditions: Send large amount of traffic.
bugs.impact: Tcpdump is capturing less than 1% of the traffic
bugs.fix: Performance of tcpdump is improved by restructuring tcpdumpd-master. The system no longer returns EAGAIN errors during high-volume traffic captures, resulting in more reliable packet capture

bugs.title: Removed unsupported traps from F5OS-APPLIANCE-ALERT-NOTIF-MIB
bugs.symptoms: The F5OS-APPLIANCE-ALERT-NOTIF-MIB mib was contained trap OIDs which are not supported by appliance platform. Those trap OIDs are removed from the MIB.
bugs.conditions: F5OS-APPLIANCE-ALERT-NOTIF-MIB.txt MIB file.
bugs.impact: OIDs exist for elements that do not apply to rSeries such as blade-hardware-fault and boot-time-integrity-status.
bugs.fix: The F5OS-APPLIANCE-ALERT-NOTIF-MIB mib contained trap OIDs which are not supported by appliance platform. Those trap OIDs are removed from the MIB.

bugs.title: High CPU or increased translation errors following upgrade or restart when DAG distribution changes
bugs.symptoms: Dagv2 tables are randomized and may change when a tmm is restarted. This can result in a change of traffic distribution, which in some cases may lead to traffic disruption. The specific condition when this option was introduced is using a CGNAT pool that is not large enough.
bugs.conditions: - tmm is restarted (or chassis rebooted)
bugs.impact: - dag distribution changes which may cause a traffic disruption.
bugs.workaround: You can restart tmm until the distribution is good, which can be checked using tools like cmp_dest.
bugs.fix: ID 1966941 added two DB variables to control dagv2 behavior - sdag.runtime.hashtable sdag.runtime.mirror.hashtable. This adds F5OS-side support to this solution.

bugs.title: "Show cluster" may incorrectly log a system controller as not present
bugs.symptoms: When running "show cluster", it may show a message like this, even though a system controller is present: Controller 2 is NOT present. A service incorrectly reads that a system controller is not present, but correctly reads it as present immediately after.
bugs.conditions: This happens very rarely. There are no specific conditions that will cause this issue.
bugs.impact: This only causes a message to be logged and does not affect the stability of the chassis.

bugs.title: On system startup, DIMM faults are reported even when no actual hardware issue exists.
bugs.symptoms: On system startup, DIMM faults are reported even though no actual hardware issue is present.
bugs.conditions: On startup, the system may falsely detect DIMM faults due to incorrect fault criteria.
bugs.impact: Customers may see false DIMM fault alerts
bugs.fix: Corrected the DIMM fault detection logic to prevent false alarms during system startup.

bugs.title: Confd.smp memory consumption spikes high with snmpEnableAuthenTraps enabled
bugs.symptoms: When config-restore is performed on a RMA system, with the configuration of SNMPv3 users and targets and snmpEnableAuthenTraps enabled, observed confd.smp process memory spikes increase and causes OOM after system reboot.
bugs.conditions: Restoring the configuration onto an RMA replacement system.
bugs.impact: Confd's RSS memory begins to grow rapidly and causes restart of ConfD process.
bugs.workaround: The available workarounds, 1. After performing config-restore on a RMA system, disable snmpEnableAuthenTraps 2. Reset all SNMPv3 users and passwords right after performing config-restore.
bugs.fix: Disabling snmpEnableAuthenTraps when the engine-id of the database backup and the system engine-id. This will prevent confd.smp process memory hike in case of any sudden reboot of the system. User can reconfigure the snmpEnableAuthenTraps after reseting the SNMPv3 users authentication and privacy password.

bugs.title: iHealth upload is failing with error "certificate signed by unknown authority"
bugs.symptoms: When attempting to use the QKView upload feature, the upload may fail with the message "certificate signed by unknown authority". This is due to a recent Entrust certificate authority shutdown resulted inconsistency between F5OS and iHealth.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to upload a qkview file to iHealth after 30 June 2025.
bugs.impact: Unable to upload QKView files to iHealth with a single click.
bugs.workaround: You can use the File Export feature to download QKView files, and then log into iHealth and upload the files via the iHealth page. You can find the QKView files in the GUI at System Settings > File Utilities, then choose "diags/shared" as the base directory, then select "qkview".
bugs.fix: Certificate authorities used by the iHealth upload feature in F5OS will be updated.

bugs.title: Can't upgrade F5OS-C 1.8.x FIPS-licensed chassis to F5OS 2.x
bugs.symptoms: On F5OS-C-1.8.0 and 1.8.1, the "check-version-fips" and "set-version-fips" commands fail with a compatibility check failure.
bugs.conditions: Upgrade chassis from 1.8.0 or 1.8.1 to 2.0 or later w/ FIPS licensed.
bugs.impact: Cannot upgrade to F5OS 2.x
bugs.fix: Upgrade compatibility check succeeds.

bugs.title: BIG-IP Tenant's VM will be patched/relaunched everytime after system reboot/upgrade/failover/TPOB restart
