bugs.symptoms: After upgrading from F5OS v1.6.1/1.7.0 to v1.8.x, tenant VMs were being unnecessarily patched and recreated, VM patches also not being properly applied.
bugs.conditions: - System upgraded from F5OS-C v1.6.1 or v1.7.0 to v1.8.x. - System reboot, failover, or TPOB restart occurs.
bugs.impact: Tenant VMs were being unnecessarily patched and relaunched after every reboot.
bugs.workaround: None. Recommended to upgrade to F5OS-C v1.8.3 which includes this fix.
bugs.fix: These changes prevent unnecessary VM patching and recreation after system upgrades, reboots, or TPOB restarts while ensuring legitimate patches are properly applied.

bugs.title: RADIUS remote authentication specifying IPv6 server addresses does not work
bugs.symptoms: F5OS does not send RADIUS Access-Request messages to a server specified as an IPv6 address. No messages are transmitted at all. When attempting authentication against SSH, log messages similar to the following are in /var/log/secure: sshd[30736]: pam_radius_auth: Failed looking up IP address for RADIUS server [2001:db8::1] (errcode=9)
bugs.conditions: F5OS remote authentication configured with a server defined by IPv6 address.
bugs.impact: F5OS remote authentication does not work.
bugs.workaround: Reference the RADIUS server by DNS hostname rather than IP address. Important: The DNS hostname should only only resolve to IPv6 addresses, and not also be associated with an IPv4 address; for more information, refer to ID1975245: https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID1975245.html

bugs.title: Logging from PAM modules only seen for SSH authentication, and not GUI/API authentication
bugs.symptoms: Logging from PAM modules (e.g. pam_unix, pam_radius_auth, or pam_unix) is only captured in system logs when a user attempts to authenticate via SSH; no such logging occurs when authenticating via the F5OS GUI or API.
bugs.conditions: - F5OS system - Attempting to troubleshoot issues related to authentication
bugs.impact: PAM module log messages are not logged anywhere. The system does generate authentication success/failure messages that are captured in the audit.log, e.g.: audit-service[12]: priority="Notice" version=1.0 msgid=0x1f03000000000012 msg="User authentication failed" reason="Invalid login attempt, user-id/password is incorrect" failcount=8 user="otters".
bugs.workaround: When troubleshooting authentication issues, attempt to log in via SSH. PAM modules will generate log messages that are captured in /var/log/secure and the systemd journal.

bugs.title: Empty CPU allocation after downgrading F5OS-A
bugs.symptoms: Empty CPU allocation returned by confd for running tenant after downgrading F5OS-A from 1.8.0 to any lower versions. # show tenants -- snip --- state vcpu-cores-per-node 8 state reserved-cpus "" <<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<< Empty cpus state memory 24576 -- snip -- NODE CPUS ------------ 1 - <<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<< No CPU allocation
bugs.conditions: Downgrade F5OS-A from 1.8.2/1.8.0 to any lower versions.
bugs.impact: GUI Dashboard displays "Data Unavailable No Running Tenants Listed" within CPU tab
bugs.workaround: Rebooting the system after a downgrade will restore CPU allocation. If reboot does not work, change the tenant state to Configured/provisioned and then change it back to deployed.

bugs.title: Unable to change F5OS primary key with LDAP TLS client cert+key set
bugs.symptoms: Attempting to set the system's primary key ("system aaa primary-key set") aborts and fails. System log shows: authd[8]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x7b01000000000075 msg="OpenSSL Keys and Certificates must start with -----BEGIN ...".
bugs.conditions: -- LDAP TLS certificate and key are configured.
bugs.impact: Unable to change primary key on device.
bugs.workaround: 1. Make sure you know the unencrypted value of the LDAP TLS cert and key. 2. Remove the LDAP TLS cert and key values 3. Rotate the system primary key 4. Re-configure the LDAP TLS cert and key values.

bugs.title: OPT-0056 QSFPO Rev 1C showing as "40G/100GBASE-FR" in "show portgroup" output
bugs.symptoms: OPT-0056 QSFPs have 100G media speed. The Rev 1A shows this when running "show portgroups", but the Rev 1C versions show "40G/100GBASE-FR".
bugs.conditions: -- OPT-0056 Rev 1C QSFP installed in the system. -- Running "show portgroups" on the CLI.
bugs.impact: Misinformation.

bugs.title: WebUi does not display warning about Zeroization during FIPS license installation or removal
bugs.symptoms: When adding or removing a FIPS license through the webUI, no notification is provided to alert that this action will initiate zeroization and results in the deletion of all partitions and the primary key.
bugs.conditions: This occurs during the installation or removal of a FIPS license using the webUI.
bugs.impact: The absence of this warning can lead to unintentional data loss.
bugs.workaround: The CLI provides a warning during this operation. Additionally, the Admin Guide documents this behaviour and its implications.
bugs.fix: A warning message is added in the webUI which alerts you that installing or removing a FIPS license will initiate zeroization, including deletion of all partitions and the primary key.

bugs.title: Module Communication Error Persists After Component Removal
bugs.symptoms: The module communication error does not clear when the component is removed
bugs.conditions: A module communication error has occurred, and the component has been removed
bugs.impact: This resulted in situations where the module communication error status remained uncleared even after the component was removed.
bugs.workaround: Restart the diag-agent using the command below docker restart diag-agent
bugs.fix: Fixed Communication Error not clearing after component removal

bugs.title: Config backup and restore is failing after downgrading from 2.0 to lower versions
bugs.symptoms: When restoring a configuration from backup, the restore action fails with an error: Error: response 'Failed.' confd_load: 662: maapi_apply_trans_flags(sock, tid, 0, aflags) failed: external error (19): /oc-sys:system/f5-security-ciphers:security/ services/service{httpd}/config/ssl-ciphersuite: Invalid openssl cipher received: TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
bugs.conditions: -- Config backup is taken after downgrading from 2.0. -- The backup file is used to restore the configuration.
bugs.impact: Config restore fails due to unsupported ciphers present.
bugs.workaround: There are three possible workarounds: -- The issue will not be seen if rollback is applied before downgrading from 2.0 -- Issue will not be seen if config-backup is taken before upgrading to 2.0 from lower versions and then config-restore is applied after downgrading to lower versions. -- If config-backup is not taken before upgrading to 2.0, then after downgrading to lower versions, execute "no system security services service httpd" before taking config-backup.

bugs.title: VOQ IMM watchdog does not resolve
bugs.symptoms: VOQs do not sync after an IMM watchdog. Backplane traffic may be disrupted.
bugs.conditions: IMM VOQ watchdog occurs.
bugs.impact: Backplane traffic may be disrupted.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the affected blade.

bugs.title: OTel telemetry data for a system controller or blade stopped after its reboot
bugs.symptoms: If a system controller is rebooted or a blade is rebooted or removed and inserted back, OTel telemetry data is stopped for it.
bugs.conditions: System controller or blade reboot, blade removed and inserted back.
bugs.impact: OTel telemetry data is stopped after a blade or system controller reboot.
bugs.workaround: Blade reboot scenario - making changes in the exporter path like disabling and enabling back, change in instrument list might help. Restartinig diag-agent on the active system controller might help. In a system controller reboot scenario - restart diag-agent on the active system controller.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue causing OTel telemetry data to stop being collected after a reboot.

bugs.title: No egress traffic from front-panel interface for port 1/2.1 in 4x100G mode on CX1610/BX520 blades
bugs.symptoms: Symptom is no traffic from front-panel interface for port 1/2.1 in 4x100G mode.
bugs.conditions: CX1610/BX520 blade front panel ports have to be configured in 4x100G mode.
bugs.impact: Loss of traffic routed to front panel.
bugs.workaround: This has been fixed with a TAM bitfile update in F5OS-C-1.8.1 EHF2 and newer. This issue is fixed in TAM FPGA bitfile version 73.80.18.66 and newer.
bugs.fix: FPGA logic fix in TAM FPGA bitfile version 73.80.18.66 (or newer).

bugs.title: VLAN cannot be deleted after removing all tenant and interface references
bugs.symptoms: If a box experiences hitting Bug ID 1759761, sometimes the workaround for that bug does not always work. The currently published workaround for that bug is: "The [vlan] deletion operation can be retried, or wait a moment after unassigning the VLAN before deleting it." However, in some cases the vlan delete will always fail because the vlan-listener for the tenant is never removed. Which means every attempt to delete the vlan will fail until the vlan-listener is removed, and any lingering fdb entries. You will see one or even a handful of vlan listeners that should not exist anymore.
bugs.conditions: Sometimes it will take several iterations for the vlan-listener to not be deleted in time. It's possible enabling network-manager and api-svc-gw debug logging increases the probability of hitting this bug. 1. Create and deploy a tenant 2. Copy the bash script vlan.tenant.tort.bsh to an external client 3. Modify the script to match rseries or partition mgmt ip, username, password and tenant name: ex. PARTITION_MGMT_IP=172.12.12.12 USERNAME=admin PASSWORD=admin TENANT=rdt1 4. run show vlan-listener | repeat 1 on the rSeries 5. run the script: while :;do date;bash vlan.tenant.tort.bsh 1;echo "sleeping for 10";sleep 10;done 6. As soon as the script reports it's sleeping for 10 seconds, check to see if the vlan-listener still exists from the output of #5. If its still there for 2+ seconds; kill the bash script to leave the device in that state.
bugs.impact: VLAN-listener does not get deleted, and will show disabled.
bugs.workaround: There are two delays needed, which I know is less then ideal. One for Bug ID 1759761 which is before removing the vlan entirely. and A second one for Bug ID 1983061 before removing the vlan from the tenant. And both bugs are resolved by the change for 1759761 which is fixed in F5OS v2.0.0 and is unfortunately not backportable.
bugs.fix: Fixed in version 2.0.0.

bugs.title: qat_stat process generates core.host.unknown during system upgrade or reboot
bugs.symptoms: The qat_stat process generates a core dump file (core.host.unknown) on F5OS appliance and chassis platforms. The core dump triggers alert event 327680 in the platform log: "Core dumped on appliance. process=qat_stat, location=/var/shared/core/host/core.host.unknown.xxxxx.xxxxxxxxxx.core.gz"
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs during system reboot or F5OS software upgrade operations. When the system sends a SIGTERM signal during these operations, the qat_stat process is terminated immediately without properly releasing tmstat rows and other resources, resulting in a core dump.
bugs.impact: Unexpected core.host.unknown files are generated and core-dump alerts are raised during upgrade or reboot operations. There is no impact to system functionality or traffic processing. The core files consume disk space and may cause confusion during troubleshooting.
bugs.workaround: Upgrade to F5OS version containing qat-support-pod 3.1.34 or later.
bugs.fix: Added signal handlers (SIGTERM, SIGINT, SIGHUP) to the qat_stat process to enable graceful shutdown. When a termination signal is received during upgrade or reboot, qat_stat now properly releases tmstat rows and cleans up resources before exiting, preventing core dumps. Additionally, the qat_service_manager (QAT-Support-Pod) was updated to send SIGTERM instead of SIGKILL, allowing the qat_stat process time to perform cleanup before shutdown.

bugs.title: System uptime misreported when uptime is 7 days or more
bugs.symptoms: The "show system uptime" command and uptime reported for controllers and blades in the F5OS GUI will report incorrect uptime values when it has an uptime that is 7 days or more, e.g.: [root@controller-1:Active ~]# f5sh show system uptime NAME UPTIME --------------------------------- controller-1 0d, 21h, 36m, 55s controller-2 3d, 5h, 37m, 27s [root@controller-1:Active ~]# uptime 15:41:54 up 21 days, 21:36, 1 user, load average: 6.73, 7.01, 6.56 [root@controller-1:Active ~]#
bugs.conditions: - VELOS system
bugs.impact: The "show system uptime" command output fails to include the number of weeks of uptime.
bugs.workaround: Log into the system as root and run "uptime" on the appropriate system controller or blade.

bugs.title: Add output of "show system uptime" for Qkview data
bugs.symptoms: Uptime data was missing from QKView data.
bugs.conditions: No ConfD repo changes for collecting output of uptime.
bugs.impact: No uptime data about devices for debugging and records.
bugs.workaround: Changes to ConfD repo for collecting output for uptime.
bugs.fix: Qkview will have output of "show system uptime".

bugs.title: Tenant experiences master key decrypt error after F5OS api-svc-gateway restart
bugs.symptoms: After the F5OS API service gateway (api-svc-gateway) restarts, tenants may experience SecureVault errors while attempting to decrypt the master key. The tenant will be inoperative. Logs similar to the following will be present in F5OS: api-svc-gateway[13]: nodename=blade-2(p3) priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x5803000000000011 msg="Crypto key installation failed:" ERRNOSTR="Lost connection to ConfD" LASTERR="EOF on socket to ConfD" ERRNO=45 api-svc-gateway[13]: nodename=blade-2(p3) priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x5804000000000027 msg="No unit key was found in confd for tenant" TENANT="tenant1" Logs similar to the following in the tenant: err mcpd[5803]: 010713d0:3: Symmetric Unit Key decrypt failure - decrypt failure notice mcpd[5803]: 01071029:5: Symmetric Unit Key decrypt notice mcpd[5803]: 01071027:5: Master key OpenSSL error: 4007094004:error:06065064:digital envelope routines:EVP_DecryptFinal_ex:bad decrypt:evp_enc.c:664:
bugs.conditions: Issue is observed rarely when there is a recent restart (or power-cycle) of the system (specifically after a restart of the F5OS api-svc-gateway container).
bugs.impact: Unable to access tenants. Tenant restarts.
bugs.workaround: Restart the API service gateway and ensure it does not log errors while retrieving the tenant unit keys. If the problem persists, restart the tenants. If the problem continues to persist after number of tenant restarts, deploy new tenant and load UCS.

bugs.title: Serial Console Occasionally Locks Up Immediately After Logout
bugs.symptoms: The serial console locks up and does not drop the login prompt again intermittently.
bugs.conditions: Log out of the blade serial console.
bugs.impact: Cannot log in to the serial console
bugs.workaround: Restart the serial console service $ systemctl restart serial-getty@ttyS0.service
bugs.fix: Detect the problem and auto-restart the console service.

bugs.title: PSU fault alarm triggered due to outdated system data when PSU is removed and then reinserted
bugs.symptoms: A PSU fault alarm occurs but the PSU is inserted and operational.
bugs.conditions: This is applicable only to r2000 and r4000 Series models. Issue happens only when BMC events arrive in below sequence 1.Received Output inactive event 2.Received Input lost event 3.Now PSU is removed and reinserted 4.Received Input lost event 5.Received Input active event This case, PSU Fault alarm is not getting cleared
bugs.impact: Stale PSU Fault alarm will be present
bugs.workaround: Stale alarm will get cleared through running below command docker exec -it platform-hal psf run POST:bmc/rearm-all-sensors
bugs.fix: PSU state gets properly updated when a PSU is removed and reinserted, thereby eliminating erroneous fault alarms due to outdated data.

bugs.title: Unable to get link on 25G interfaces
bugs.symptoms: The portgroup speeds on r2xx/r4xx platforms are configured with the port-profile. Possible settings are: appliance-1(config)# port-profile config mode Possible completions: 2x25G-4x10G 4x25G 8x10G When changing 2x25G-4x10G to 4x25G, interfaces are not renumbered. There was a coding error that did not detect the change and did not publish the new configuration.
bugs.conditions: Changing port-profile from 2x25G-4x10G to 4x25G.
bugs.impact: Improperly published configuration caused interfaces to not get link.
bugs.workaround: Select the 8x10 port-profile in between the changes. This renumbers interfaces and the change is properly detected. 2x25_4x10 -> 8x10 -> 4x25
bugs.fix: The code has been fixed to properly detect the configuration change.

bugs.title: F5 VELOS BX520 TAM firmware v73.80.18.66
bugs.symptoms: F5 VELOS BX520 TAM firmware v73.80.18.66
bugs.conditions: F5 VELOS BX520 Platform.
bugs.impact: Not applicable.
bugs.fix: Fixes issue with 4x100G mode. See ID1983021 for more information.

bugs.title: File download failing from log/system
bugs.symptoms: File download failing from log/system using GUI and RESTCONF both.
bugs.conditions: While trying to to download audit.log or the file from host directory from log/system, 500 internal server error will display
bugs.impact: Not able to download the log file.
bugs.workaround: Instead of download use file export utility

bugs.title: VOQs don't recover after window error on own slot
bugs.symptoms: Traffic outage after a VOQ window error occurs on a the blade's own slot. The VQF_CORE_GLOBAL_ACTIVE_BLADES_REG (0x1024) on the blade will not have the bit for itself asserted.
bugs.conditions: VOQ window error occurs on a the blade's own slot.
bugs.impact: Traffic outage.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the blade with the VOQ window error.

bugs.title: Show system version should rely on sw-mgmt, not the confd db.
bugs.symptoms: After an upgrade, 'show system version' shows the previous version until reboot
bugs.conditions: Running 'show system version' or 'show system image' shortly after an upgrade of an HA pair.
bugs.impact: Possibility of stale information
bugs.fix: Updated system-service to use baseos-socket-client-lib to get runtime data instead of cdb call.

bugs.title: System controller may not update IP range for docker0 network after changing internal chassis network range
bugs.symptoms: When using a non-default internal chassis network range, a VELOS system controller may keep using 100.64.10.0/16 for the IP range for the docker0 network.
bugs.conditions: This can occur when performing an RMA replacement, or a clean install of a controller via PXE or USB drive.
bugs.impact: Some internal containers running on the system controller will continue to be addressed in 100.64.0.0/16 (RFC6598 address space) rather than the RFC1918 space configured.
bugs.workaround: 1. Log into the system controller as root 2. Edit /etc/sysconfig/docker and update the "--bip" parameter in the OPTIONS line. This can be done automatically by running the following commands from a root shell: source /etc/sysconfig/chassis_network_active.txt prefix=${network_prefix:-"100.65"} chassis_id=${chassis_id:-1} first_octet=${network_prefix%%.*} second_octet=${network_prefix##*.} (( second_octet=second_octet - chassis_id )) sed -i.bak -E "s@--bip[ =][0-9]*＼.[0-9]*＼.@--bip=${first_octet}.${second_octet}.@g" /etc/sysconfig/docker Or all on one line: ( source /etc/sysconfig/chassis_network_active.txt; prefix=${network_prefix:-"100.65"}; chassis_id=${chassis_id:-1}; first_octet=${network_prefix%%.*}; second_octet=${network_prefix##*.}; (( second_octet=second_octet - chassis_id )); sed -i.bak -E "s@--bip[ =][0-9]*＼.[0-9]*＼.@--bip=${first_octet}.${second_octet}.@g" /etc/sysconfig/docker ) 3. Reboot the system controller.

bugs.title: TLS Extended Master Secret Extension in F5OS
bugs.symptoms: EMS (extended_master_secret) extension is not present in F5OS-A versions 1.3.x and 1.4.x and F5OS-C versions 1.3.x,1.4.x,1.5.x
bugs.conditions: Openssl 1.0.2q in the F5OS-A/C does not support EMS.
bugs.impact: F5OS-A version < 1.5.x, Does not support EMS. F5OS-C version < 1.6.x, Does not support EMS.
bugs.workaround: Upgrade to supported Openssl verison
bugs.fix: F5OS-A versions 1.5.0 and above use OpenSSL version 1.0.2zc, which includes EMS support. Any version below 1.5.0 do not. F5OS-C versions 1.6.0 and above use OpenSSL version 1.0.2zc, which includes EMS support. Any version below 1.6.0 do not.

bugs.title: A TACACS+ server secret with a newline breaks PAM configs and blocks all user logins, including root.
bugs.symptoms: When a TACACS+ server secret contains a newline character, the PAM configuration files (/etc/pam.d/password-auth and /etc/pam.d/system-auth) become corrupted. This causes PAM to report "illegal module type" and "expecting return value" errors, preventing all user authentication, including root login via SSH and console.
bugs.conditions: A TACACS+ server is configured with a secret-key value that contains a literal newline character (U+000A). This can occur either by directly submitting a secret containing a newline via the REST API or when the system's primary key is corrupted, causing the decrypted secret value to contain unexpected characters.
bugs.impact: TACACS+ authentication to the system is broken.
bugs.workaround: NA
bugs.fix: Fixed in F5 v2.0 version.

bugs.title: F5OS SCP hardening
SNMPv3 support with SHA512 authentication
bugs.symptoms: Improvement. No known functional issue.
bugs.conditions: NA
bugs.impact: improvement to support SHA512 authentication in SNMPv3
bugs.workaround: Its improvement.
bugs.fix: Added SNMPv3 SHA12 authentication protocol support.

bugs.title: System health may show a transient alert during controller firmware updates that does not clear automatically
bugs.symptoms: During or shortly after a controller firmware update, system health can display an error indicating the controller’s hardware alert handler failed to initialize. The health view may suggest a fan or power controller monitoring failure even though all components later report Healthy/Ok. The error may persist in health/status after the firmware update completes, creating the impression of a controller health problem.
bugs.conditions: Occurs when controller firmware updates, controller failover, or a restart of the diagnostics service temporarily interrupts hardware health monitoring at startup.
bugs.impact: Misleading controller health alarms may remain visible after updates complete, causing confusion and unnecessary investigation. Firmware updates themselves complete successfully.
bugs.workaround: - After the firmware update, confirm that fans/power controllers report Healthy/Ok in system health. - If an initialization error persists, restart the diagnostics service or perform a controller failover to clear the stale alert.
bugs.fix: Diagnostics alert handlers now automatically retry during transient outages and recover initial alert states once hardware monitoring becomes available. As a result, the initialization error no longer appears, and system health clears correctly after firmware updates.

bugs.title: Privilege Escalation to Admin via SSH Port Forwarding
Tcpdump may crash with "malloc(): corrupted top size" when using complex BPF filters
bugs.symptoms: Running tcpdump with complex or long BPF filter expressions may result in a crash with the error message: malloc(): corrupted top size
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when tcpdump is invoked with a filter expression containing multiple conditions or a long filter string, especially when run via the system diagnostics
bugs.impact: Packet capture operations fails and no data is collected. This may impact troubleshooting or monitoring activities that rely on tcpdump.
bugs.fix: Tcpdump has been updated to reliably support complex and long filter expressions. The utility now validates filter input to prevent errors, ensuring stable and consistent packet capture operations

bugs.title: Backplane trap exists on appliance
bugs.symptoms: "backplane" trap exists on F5OS-APPLIANCE-ALERT-NOTIF-MIB.txt on applicance, where it is not applicable.
bugs.conditions: F5OS-APPLIANCE-ALERT-NOTIF-MIB.txt MIB file.
bugs.impact: "backplane" trap exists on appliance, where it is not applicable.
bugs.fix: "backplane" trap exists on F5OS-APPLIANCE-ALERT-NOTIF-MIB.txt on applicance, where it is not applicable.

bugs.title: Platform registry failures on standby partition
bugs.symptoms: This issue can manifest in several ways, including: - Tenant deployments fail. - Partition upgrade fails. - Partition fails to join the cluster after a PXE boot. This issue is due to overridden port assignments for platform registry services on the partition's standby controller.
bugs.conditions: -- Chassis-based system. -- An active controller's port assignment replaces one on the standby controller.
bugs.impact: This issue can manifest in several ways, including: - Tenant deployment fails. - Partition upgrade fails. - Partition fails to join the cluster after a PXE boot.

bugs.title: F5OS qkview fails to collect log files due to journal logs
bugs.symptoms: When generating a host qkview on F5OS, some of the journal log files are not handled properly, resulting in the output qkview missing expected log files, and the following example error log is observed in the platform.log file: panic: runtime error: index out of range [327713] with length 128
bugs.conditions: The issue occurs when qkview is generated using the standard qkview-collect on F5OS with the software version 1.8.x and lower, and the system contains binary systemd journal files in /var/log/journal folder.
bugs.impact: -- Resulting qkview archive is incomplete and missing log files. -- Diagnostic and support efforts may be hindered due to missing data.
bugs.workaround: Edit the qkview-collect.config.yml to not collect /var/log/journal files before running qkview using the below steps and commands to collect the qkview -- Edit the file /etc/qkview-collect/qkview-collect.config.yml and add the line "- /var/log/journal" under the “excludes:" section, ensuring it follows the existing YAML syntax and indentation. -- Generate a qkview: f5sh 'system diagnostics qkview capture' -- Check the qkview status using the below command and wait for the qkview collection to complete: f5sh 'system diagnostics qkview status'
bugs.fix: Journal log files are handled properly during the qkview files collection, resulting in the successful collection of log files.

bugs.title: Management MAC address may display incorrectly in some scenarios
bugs.symptoms: The management MAC address may be shown incorrectly in CLI output.
bugs.conditions: Seen on F5OS-C in certain upgrade/downgrade scenarios.
bugs.impact: Cosmetic display issue only; no traffic or connectivity impact.

bugs.title: IPv6 NDP Neighbor Advertisements may get dropped at the VELOS platform layer when tenant transitions from Standby to Active during a failover
bugs.symptoms: -- Some IPv6 NDP Neighbor Advertisements (NA) from a tenant does not egress the VELOS platform when the tenant becomes active during failover. -- When a failover occurs, drop_pkt_cnt increases when observing the counters from the controller using the following command: for i in blade-{1,2}; do echo $i; echo '====='; ssh $i docker exec -i partition_fpga fpgatool -c ＼"nsms hdp_drop_pkt_cnt 1＼"; done
bugs.conditions: -- Tenant running on VELOS v1.8.1, v1.8.2. -- IPv6 floating self-IPs and many IPv6 floating virtual addresses are configured in VLANs on the tenant. -- Failover occurs.
bugs.impact: Upstream devices do not receive the IPv6 NDP NAs that should have indicated that the new tenant has taken over for the affected IPv6 addresses.

bugs.title: F5OS-A 1.8.0 qkview does not include "user readable" docker ps -a command output
bugs.symptoms: Qkview does not include "user readable" docker ps -a command output
bugs.conditions: While capturing host qkview
bugs.impact: The captured "docker ps" command is not user-readable in the qkview file.
bugs.workaround: Manually capture the output if necessary.
bugs.fix: Fixed in 2.1.0

bugs.title: Configuring more than one mgmt aggregation interface may cause an aggregated management port to stop working
bugs.symptoms: It is a documented restriction that only one user-defined aggregation interface is allowed to be configured in the System Controller ConfD configuration - the aggregation interface required to support management port aggregation. All subsequent user defined aggregation interfaces added to the System Controller ConfD configuration will be ignored by switchd. The management port aggregation may continue to function even after this configuration is performed since the switch trunk hardware is already programmed. However, after any event which requires reprogramming of the trunk hardware (ie. loss of trunk member or a system controller reboot), requests by LACP to update the trunk will be ignored by switchd and management connectivity will appear unreliable or completely non-existent.
bugs.conditions: Configuration of an additional System Controller aggregation interface followed by some event which requires switch hardware to be reprogrammed. Example: User upgrades the System Controller which causes the controllers to reboot.
bugs.impact: You may experience unreliable or complete loss of chassis, partition and tenant management connectivity.
bugs.workaround: - Delete all but one of the user-defined aggregation interfaces and LACP interfaces of the same name from the System Controller ConfD configuration. - Make sure that SC management ports 1/mgmt0 and 2/mgmt0 ethernet aggregation-id are configured with the name of the aggregation interface that remains. - Reboot both system controllers.
bugs.fix: Attempts to configure additional user-defined aggregation interfaces are blocked.

bugs.title: System controller configuration of cplagg interfaces should be modified
bugs.symptoms: If the lag-type of a cplagg_1.x interface is removed, System Controller/blade communications will stop working. System Controller ConfD configuration of cplagg interfaces is set up by the confd initialization XML. The configuration may be viewed but should never be modified. Modification of the CPLAGG interface configuration needs to be blocked.
bugs.conditions: System Controllers are up and running, and the confd configuration is accessible to the user.
bugs.impact: Control plane communications may be lost to the blade reachable through the modified cplagg interface.
bugs.workaround: Restore the CPLAGG configuration that existed before the modification. Perform a staged reboot of the system controllers: reboot the standby controller, after the rebooted controller comes up, make it the active controller, and reboot the new standby controller.
bugs.fix: Users are prevented from modifying the System Controller confd configuration of the CPLAGG interfaces.

bugs.title: Tenant deletion may fail when a transient internal communication timeout occurs on the system controller
bugs.symptoms: After a tenant is deleted, the tenant instance may remain running on one or more blades.
bugs.conditions: The delete request was issued, but a transient internal timeout prevented the instance from being stopped and removed, and the request was not retried.
bugs.impact: After the tenant delete is issued, the user assumes the tenant was removed but it is still present.
bugs.workaround: Toggle the tenant running-state from deployed to configured and then back to deployed.

bugs.title: BX520 blade eDAG masking issue causes redirections with ipv6-prefix-len not equal to 128.
bugs.symptoms: This issue can cause lower overall system performance because of bad disaggregation to service endpoint. Host software recognizes that packets are not at the correct endpoint and redirects the packets to the correct endpoint. The extra packet hop can cause lower overall system performance.
bugs.conditions: ipv6-prefix-len not equal to 128. ATSE v75.3.23.00 or earlier.
bugs.impact: Variable packet performance and latency impact.
bugs.workaround: Update to ATSE v75.3.25.00 or newer bitstream release for BX520 blade.
bugs.fix: Logic issue in disaggregation masking found and fixed in ATSE v75.3.25.00 bitstream release for BX520 blade.

bugs.title: F5 VELOS BX520 ATSE firmware v75.3.25.00
bugs.symptoms: F5 VELOS BX520 ATSE firmware v75.3.25.00
bugs.conditions: F5 VELOS BX520 Platform
bugs.impact: Not applicable.
bugs.fix: Fixes disaggregation issue. See ID2034661 for more information.

bugs.title: Blade interface presence/stats are getting wiped because of bad power event during system controller failover
bugs.symptoms: After inserting a blade in the chassis, the blade interface state may be wiped out on the next system controller failover. Interfaces will be shown as "NOT_PRESENT" even though the blade is present and running. default-1# show interfaces interface state oper-status NAME OPER STATUS -------------------- 1/1.0 DOWN 1/2.0 DOWN 2/1.0 NOT_PRESENT 2/2.0 NOT_PRESENT 3/1.0 DOWN 3/2.0 DOWN
bugs.conditions: Physically inserting a blade in the chassis, followed by a controller failover after the blade finishes booting.
bugs.impact: After the controller failover, the incorrect 'power off' event causes the partition software to erase the blade dataplane state, resulting in the blade dataplane being inoperative.
bugs.workaround: To avoid the issue: After inserting a blade in the chassis, cause a controller failover and then reboot the blade. To recover if the problem is encountered: Reboot the blade.
bugs.fix: Inaccurate power events are not generated during system controller failover.

bugs.title: Authentication-mgr's restart triggers Controller Switchover
bugs.symptoms: When the container is restarted using ‘docker restart authentication-mgr’, at times, controller failover occurs.
bugs.conditions: When the container is restarted using ‘docker restart authentication-mgr’, the following container events take place: · container:event:kill · container:event:die · container:event:stop · container:event:start · container:event:restart. During this process, it's container:running attribute is temporarily set to Unhealthy | Error before the container starts.
bugs.impact: When authentication-mgr's container:running attribute is set to Unhealthy, even for a very short interval, In some of the instances, the parent components(Controller)are also updated to Unhealthy, which triggers a failover.
bugs.fix: The value of parameter 'critical' for authentication-mgr is updated. This will not set the container:running attribute to Unhealthy | Error before the container starts.

bugs.title: The confd-key-migrationd logs may display incorrect error messages during migration failures
bugs.symptoms: The confd-key-migrationd logs may display incorrect or misleading error messages during migration failures.
bugs.conditions: When confd-key-migrationd encounters errors during migration, the logged error messages may not accurately reflect the actual cause.
bugs.impact: The logs don't provide enough detail to identify the underlying problem.
bugs.workaround: NA
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue that caused confd-key-migrationd to log incorrect error messages during migration failures.

bugs.title: Incorrect network namespace for system_tmstat_merged
bugs.symptoms: system_tmstat_merged is running in the host network namespace at all times
bugs.conditions: It is running in the host network namespace all the time.
bugs.impact: Isolation, Security Implications, Behaviour change
bugs.workaround: Changed the network namespace from host to service:identifier
bugs.fix: system_tmstat_merged is running in the container network namespace

bugs.title: System_host_config container's outbound DNS traffic will use stale DNS lookup entries.
bugs.symptoms: When DNS server entries are added to the appliance via ConfD, the entry is not updated in /etc/resolv.conf of the system_host_config container. Outbound traffic from system_host_config will use stale DNS entries.
bugs.conditions: A new DNS server or host-entries are added on appliances via ConfD.
bugs.impact: The new entry is not updated in the system_host_config container's /etc/resolv.conf file. This container does not generate outbound traffic so there is no functional impact.
bugs.workaround: If you need system_host_config to have the updated DNS server entries, restart the system_host_config container: docker restart system_host_config
bugs.fix: Restarting the container should update the DNS lookup entries.

bugs.title: Max DNS entries supported are three, if more are configured the extras are ignored, and even after reducing to three, the previously ignored entries are not reapplied.
bugs.symptoms: The system supports a maximum of three DNS entries. When more than three are configured, the additional entries are ignored. However, after removing the extra entries and reducing the list to three, the previously ignored entries are still not added back to the system.
bugs.conditions: Configuring more than 3 DNS entries and removing previously added entries
bugs.impact: DNS resolution failure.
bugs.workaround: Recreate DNS entries
bugs.fix: NA

bugs.title: VELOS controller cannot change primary key if there is an NTP key configured
bugs.symptoms: If an NTP key is configured, attempts to change the system's primary key will fail and log these errors: confd-key-migrationd[9]: nodename=controller-1 priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x1b01000000000010 msg="Failed to set element in cdb" path="/system/ntp/ntp-keys/ntp-key{1}/state/key-value" error="" errno="Interrupted system call". confd-key-migrationd[9]: nodename=controller-1 priority="Crit" version=1.0 msgid=0x1b01000000000002 msg="Key Migration failed, attempting to restore" stage="RESTORE_SECURE_ELEMENTS"
bugs.conditions: -- VELOS system controller running F5OS-C. -- NTP encryption key configured.
bugs.impact: Unable to change primary key.
bugs.workaround: -- Remove the NTP key from the configuration. -- Perform the key migration. -- Re-add the NTP key to the configuration.

bugs.title: Appliance_orchestration_manager process occasionally cores
bugs.symptoms: Occasionally the appliance_orchestration_manager daemon will core.
bugs.conditions: This can occur in appliance_orchestration_manager during normal operation.
bugs.impact: After core, service will restart the operation.

bugs.title: Changing LDAP configuration via the GUI results in an unexpected error
bugs.symptoms: Changing LDAP configuration on GUI errors out with the following error message - "object is not writable: /oc-sys:system/oc-sys:aaa/oc-sys:authentication/f5-aaa-ldap:ldap/f5-aaa-ldap:state"
bugs.conditions: When using a Windows Active Directory (AD) server and LDAP settings are configured with Active Directory authentication enabled (true) and Unix Attributes disabled (false).
bugs.impact: You are unable to make LDAP configuration changes via the GUI.
bugs.workaround: Make the configuration change from CLI.
bugs.fix: GUI will not modify the read-only state part of the LDAP configuration and allow user to save the LDAP configuration changes.

bugs.title: NTP CLI/webUI displays "ntp api, the server or underlying service is unreachable"
bugs.symptoms: 1. Newly configured DNS IPs are not used in tcpdump-platform-agent container. 2. show system ntp command is unresponsive.
bugs.conditions: 1. New DNS IPs are configured
bugs.impact: 1. The "ping" command is unable to use the recently configured DNS IPs 2. Timeout occurs when you execute "show system ntp".
bugs.fix: 1. Ping now correctly uses newly configured DNS servers. 2. The show system ntp command responds faster.

bugs.title: Setting the primary key on VELOS will intermittently cause a failover and primary key inconsistency
bugs.symptoms: When performing a "system aaa primary-key set" operation, sometimes the controller will fail over prior to updating the database values, resulting in an inconsistent decryption key. The set key operation remains in 'IN_PROGRESS' and does not recover.
bugs.conditions: Retry timing problem in the key retrieval logic sometimes causes the database to hang for over 30 seconds during configuration reload, resulting in the hardware watchdog expiring and causing a failover.
bugs.impact: Configuration database will not be usable, partitions will not start correctly. System must be restored from backup.
bugs.workaround: Prior to attempting to change the primary-key, ensure that a controller, partition, and tenant backups with a known primary-key are available. If the problem occurs, perform a "system database reset-to-default", reset the primary key to the previous known value corresponding to the backup and restore the backups.
bugs.fix: Setting the primary key does not cause a failover.

bugs.title: 'show cluster events' cli output is not displaying unhealthy->healthy, ordering and timestamps of events
bugs.symptoms: 'show cluster events' cli output is not showing timestamp of events(when the event occurred) and no detailed information on the healthiness(healthy/unhealthy) or severity(Info/Warning) of the event.
bugs.conditions: When user executes cli related to 'show cluster events', the output is not showing timestamp of events(when the event occurred) and no detailed information on the healthiness(healthy/unhealthy) or severity(Info/Warning) of the event.
bugs.impact: There is no functional impact but displayed events timestamp, healthiness is missed.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: The issue is fixed.

bugs.title: FCS or FEC uncorrected errors seen continuously on the system
bugs.symptoms: FCS (Frame Check Sequence) and FEC (Forward Error Correction) error statistics for chassis/blade backplane ports were incorrectly reported as unhealthy because the system interpreted raw (non-zero) counter values as errors.
bugs.conditions: Occurs when switch reports FCS or FEC errors greater than 0
bugs.impact: System will display switch port status alarms and events.

bugs.title: "show system mgmt-ip" displays all zeroes instead of actual IP address when mgmt interface is down
bugs.symptoms: On F5OS-A platforms, when the management interface is DOWN, the output of the "show system mgmt-ip" command may display all zeroes or default values for the management IP address, prefix-length, and gateway. Example output: system mgmt-ip state ipv4 system address 0.0.0.0 system mgmt-ip state ipv4 prefix-length 0 system mgmt-ip state ipv4 gateway 0.0.0.0 system mgmt-ip state ipv6 system address :: system mgmt-ip state ipv6 prefix-length 0 system mgmt-ip state ipv6 gateway :: This does not reflect the actual configured management IP, which remains correctly set and visible via show running-config system mgmt-ip.
bugs.conditions: Management interface connected to an upstream switch; interface may be administratively shut down or physically disconnected.
bugs.impact: This is a cosmetic issue in the F5OS CLI. The configuration itself is not lost or changed; it remains intact and can be viewed in the running configuration.
bugs.workaround: -- To view accurate management IP configuration when the mgmt interface is DOWN, use the following command: # show running-config system mgmt-ip -- To avoid hitting this cosmetic issue, ensure that the mgmt interface remains UP and connected to its upstream switch. -- If this issue occurs, toggling the mgmt interface UP/DOWN or rebooting may temporarily resolve it; however, it may recur if the interface goes DOWN again. An upgrade or downgrade also temporarily clears the issue.

bugs.title: OPT-0056 100G link intermittently fails to come up after reboot or hot plug insertion due to incorrect Media Side FEC programming
bugs.symptoms: An OPT-0056 100G link intermittently fails to come up after a reboot or hot plug insertion.
bugs.conditions: Having an OPT-0056 100G link and after a system reboot or hot plug inserts the optic into the system.
bugs.impact: Intermittent link issues.

bugs.title: F5OS GUI/CLI "Available Storage" displayed when creating tenants not accurate due to thin provisioning
bugs.symptoms: The "Available Storage" field in the F5OS GUI/CLI shows “0 GB” available after several tenants are deployed, even though more tenants can still be created due to thin provisioning. This behavior leads to confusion as users may mistakenly believe that no additional tenants can be deployed.
bugs.conditions: * Deploy tenants on an F5OS appliance (e.g., r5k or r10900). * Observe the "Available Storage" field in the GUI/CLI after creating multiple tenants; it may display "0 GB" despite sufficient resources for additional tenants.
bugs.impact: Misrepresentation of available storage in the GUI/CLI causes users to incorrectly interpret system limits and subsequent loss of trust in the storage metric as a reliable reference.
bugs.workaround: No current workaround exists to adjust the displayed storage value.

bugs.title: F5OS rSeries r2k/r4k BIG-IP Tenant management interface not reachable
bugs.symptoms: On F5OS rSerier r2k/r4k , in rare conditions the management interface is not reachable due to a timing and ordering issue probing network interfaces In the BIG-IP Tenant, the network interfaces eth0 or mgmt are missing
bugs.conditions: This condition is rare and when it does its usually seen on tenant first boot.
bugs.impact: Unable to reach BIG-IP Tenant management address.
bugs.workaround: Reboot tenant

bugs.title: Authentication of LDAP Remote user in AD server may fail
bugs.symptoms: LDAP Remote user authentication in F5OS may fail when the Unix attributes is set to false.
bugs.conditions: If LDAP authentication is configured with an Active Directory (AD) server, remote users will not be able to authenticate successfully on F5OS.
bugs.impact: Remote user may not be able to login to F5OS.

bugs.title: Controllers lose connectivity to blades with stale LACP members in member table
bugs.symptoms: LACP member table has stale members and controllers lose connectivity to blades.
bugs.conditions: Issue can happen when the following are performed. - Manually failover the controllers. - Power down active controller. - Reboot active controller. - Physically remove active controller from the chassis.
bugs.impact: Controllers lose connectivity to blades and stale LACP members cannot be cleaned up.
bugs.workaround: Restart cc-lacpd container on the active controller, or reboot active controller.
bugs.fix: Debug log is added to help debugging the issue. Enable cc-lacpd debug log and look for msgid=0x3301000000000050 from velos.log. This debug log prints the cache of current confD member table data.

bugs.title: TACACS GUI Authentication Failure
bugs.symptoms: When using an affected version of F5OS, TACACS users may successfully authenticate; however, the GUI session closes immediately, and any requests return a 401 error. The following error message is observed: ERROR: PAM validation failed: User role modified
bugs.conditions: -- Occurs on F5OS-A (rSeries) and F5OS-C (VELOS) platforms running version 1.8.x. -- TACACS server configuration includes a home directory attribute (F5-F5OS-HOMEDIR) with a trailing space (e.g., "/tmp ").
bugs.impact: TACACS users are unable to log into the F5OS GUI. Authentication succeeds, but authorization fails, resulting in immediate session termination and a 401 error. SSH access is unaffected.
bugs.workaround: -- Remove any trailing spaces from the F5-F5OS-HOMEDIR attribute in the TACACS server configuration. -- Ensure all TACACS attributes are formatted correctly without extra whitespace.
bugs.fix: The system handles extraneous whitespace in TACACS attributes more robustly.

bugs.title: Dagd may crash if a malicious message is sent from the tenant
Partitions created on VELOS v1.1.x will have configuration wiped during controller upgrade to VELOS v1.6.4, v1.8.1, or v1.8.2
bugs.symptoms: A partition's configuration can get wiped out and reset to default when the controller is upgraded to VELOS 1.6.4, v1.8.1, or v1.8.2.
bugs.conditions: If a partition was created while the system controller was running VELOS v1.1.x, the partition configuration volume may have been created with as an LVM "thin pool" rather than a logical volume. The problem does not occur with partitions created on VELOS 1.2.0 or later. In VELOS v1.6.4, v1.8.1, and v1.8.2, the partition startup logic incorrectly fails to recognize that these filesystem volumes are already initialized, and reinitializes them resulting in data loss. The reinitialization error is persistent, and will be repeated any time the partition instance is restarted, until the volumes are recreated without "thin provisioning".
bugs.impact: -- The partition configuration data is wiped and reset back to default.
bugs.workaround: Before upgrading to the system controllers to VELOS v1.6.4, v1.8.1, or v1.8.2, check if the partition logical volumes on either system controller are incorrectly provisioned. To do this, run the "lvs" command from a bash shell on both controllers. "Thin provisioned" volumes will have numeric entries in the "Data%" and "Meta%" columns, and will have the "t" flag in the "Attr" column In this example, partitions 1 is effected: [root@controller-1:Active log]# lvs LV VG Attr LSize Pool Origin Data% Meta% Move Log Cpy%Sync Convert partition1 partition_config twi-a-tz-- 10.00g 0.00 10.61 partition3 partition_config -wi-ao-z-- 10.00g export_chassis partition_image -wi-ao---- 256.12g partition1 partition_image twi-a-tz-- 15.00g 0.00 10.57 partition1_shared partition_image -wi-a----- 10.00g partition3 partition_image -wi-ao-z-- 15.00g partition3_shared partition_image -wi-ao---- 10.00g ... If this condition exists, do not upgrade to these versions and contact support for assistance for non-destructively converting these volumes.
bugs.fix: In VELOS v1.8.3, the partition startup logic correctly recognizes that these partition logical volumes are already initialized, and does not wipe and recreate them.

bugs.title: A partition's "show system events" no longer updates after multiple partition failovers
bugs.symptoms: After a partition is failed over more than once it will no longer list new events when running "show system events".
bugs.conditions: -- Chassis system with at least one partition. -- The partition must have failed over at least twice.
bugs.impact: New events are no longer seen when running "show system events".

bugs.title: The anaconda-ssh service fails to start during installation phase, preventing remote SSH access
bugs.symptoms: SSH access is unavailable when using the inst.sshd boot parameter to enable remote debugging or Kickstart monitoring.
bugs.conditions: To enable SSH access and troubleshoot boot issues during the bare metal installation process.
bugs.impact: Blocks remote debugging over SSH during the bare metal installation process.
bugs.workaround: Need to trobleshoot through console only.
bugs.fix: Enabled the eno1 physical port and resolved the OpenSSL and OpenSSH compatibility.

bugs.title: LLDP errors are logged when no IPv4 management address is configured
bugs.symptoms: If a partition (F5OS-C) does not have an IPv4 management address configured, errors like the following will be logged in the partition's velos.log file: lldpd[9]: nodename=blade-1(p1) priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x6001000000000015 msg="Unable to start confD session." ERROR="item does not exist" LASTERR="/oc-sys:system/state/f5-partition:mgmt-ipv4 does not exist" ERRNO=1. fpgamgr[11]: nodename=blade-5(p2) priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x302000000000005 msg="cdb_get failed for" COMPONENT="/voq-states/voq-state{1 5}" ERROR="item does not exist" LASTERR="/f5-voq:voq-states/voq-state{1 5}/voqs_enabled does not exist" ERRNO=1.
bugs.conditions: A partition's IPv4 management address is not configured. Systems with only an ip6 address will also exhibit the same messages.
bugs.impact: These logs are benign and can be ignored.
bugs.workaround: To prevent these logs, configure an IPv4 management IP address.

bugs.title: F5OS not able to handle changes to LDAP tls_reqcert configuration
bugs.symptoms: Changes to an LDAP server's tls_reqcert configuration are not handled by F5OS, resulting in authentication-manager and user-manager communication failures with the LDAP server
bugs.conditions: - LDAP system authentication configured to authenticate against an Active Directory Server - Under the system Authentication Settings configuration in the Common LDAP Configuration section, "Authenticate with Active Directory" set to True and "Unix Attributes" set to False - LDAP group filters specified for one or more roles - The LDAP server's tls_reqcert configuration is modified while F5OS is actively running.
bugs.impact: Changes to the LDAP server's tls_reqcert setting will cause communication failures with the LDAP server.
bugs.workaround: Restart authentication manager and user manager after making configuration changes to the tls_reqcert configuration option.

bugs.title: Authentication failures not logged at default level in authentication-mgr and user-manager
bugs.symptoms: When LDAP authentication fails due to TLS certificate validation errors (e.g., "unable to get local issuer certificate"), these failures are not captured in the default log level of authentication-mgr or user-manager. As a result, administrators must enable debug logging to obtain useful diagnostic information about the failure.
bugs.conditions: Running F5OS-C 1.8.1 (VELOS platform) or lower version. LDAP authentication is configured for the system.
bugs.impact: - Administrators are unable to diagnose LDAP/TLS authentication failures using standard logs. - Additional troubleshooting steps (enabling debug logging) are required to obtain error details. - Increases time to resolution and may delay identification of root cause for authentication issues.
bugs.workaround: Enable debug logging for authentication-mgr and user-manager to capture detailed error messages related to LDAP/TLS failures.
bugs.fix: Future versions will improve logging so that LDAP/TLS authentication failures (such as certificate validation errors) are captured at the default log level, eliminating the need to enable debug logging for basic troubleshooting.

bugs.title: init_etile: Cable check failed
bugs.symptoms: F5 rSeries Appliances may experience issues with port bringup when using an OPT-0036 in 4x10G bifurcated (breakout) mode. The system log will show an “init_etile: Cable check failed” message for one or more of the bifurcated ports. The system will not be able to establish a link on the port and the port status will remain down.
bugs.conditions: rSeries Appliance using an OPT-0036 in 4x10G breakout mode running F5OS-A-1.8.3 or earlier.
bugs.impact: Port remains down.
bugs.workaround: None. Requires F5OS update.
bugs.fix: Fixed in F5OS-A-1.8.3-25023-EHF-6 and later.

bugs.title: PSU inventory data shows "Not Available" on F5OS-A
bugs.symptoms: After PSU power test, F5OS reports PSU serial/part number as "Not Available" and shows empty state. Platform-hal logs "wrong common header format version: 0" and "wrong zero checksum 255 != 254" errors. PSU functions normally but inventory data unavailable.
bugs.conditions: Occurs after PSU power test/reseat PSU FRU EEPROM corrupted Failed to read the Seriel number.
bugs.impact: Incorrect PSU inventory display.

bugs.title: Packets destined to the Kubernetes API server may leave the rSeries appliance's management port on platform services shutdown
bugs.symptoms: Some packets destined to the internal Kubernetes API server may leave the system's management port towards the configured management gateway for up to 10 seconds during platform services shutdown or reboot. These packets will be destined to an IP address in the internal network range on TCP port 6443, by default 100.64.0.0/12 (RFC6598).
bugs.conditions: Platform services are shutting down, typically during a system reboot.
bugs.impact: There is no known impact to system operation. Packets will no longer leave the management port once platform services start up again, which happens automatically on system startup. The small number of "leaked" packets may occasionally be observed in monitoring or logs from external systems such as firewalls.

bugs.title: Error message IDs for image-agent do not match those documented in the error catalog
bugs.symptoms: Some of the message ids logged by the image-agent service in platform log do not match the error message id in the catalog.
bugs.conditions: Looking up image-agent logs by ID in the error message catalog.
bugs.impact: This discrepancy makes it difficult to correlate system logs with documentation for troubleshooting and support.
bugs.fix: Updated the error catalog message IDs correctly.

bugs.title: Interface 8.0 on r2000 and r4000-series F5OS appliances does not join LACP LAG or transmit LLDP BPDUs after upgrade to F5OS-A 1.8.3
bugs.symptoms: - Interface 8.0 has an operational status of UP - Interface 8.0 does not join a LACP LAG. - Interface 8.0 does not transmit any LLDP packets. - Log messages similar to the following in the platform.log: nic-manager[8]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x720c000000000003 msg="Error NULL interface descriptor".
bugs.conditions: - Running an affected version of F5OS-A. - An r2000-series or r4000-series appliance. This issue does not affect r5000-, r10000-, or r12000-series appliances. - Interface 8.0 is in a LACP LAG.
bugs.impact: Interface 8.0 is not able to negotiate and join a LACP LAG
bugs.workaround: This issue is fixed in F5OS-A 1.8.3 EHF-1, which is available for download on MyF5: https://my.f5.com/manage/s/downloads?productFamily=F5OS&productLine=F5OS+Appliance+Software&version=1.8.3&container=1.8.3-EHF

bugs.title: After upgrading, system health shows "disk encryption" as unhealthy even when UEFI communication is successful
bugs.symptoms: When upgrading from a version before 1.8.2 to version 1.8.2 or later, the system may incorrectly show "Disk Encryption" as unhealthy.
bugs.conditions: Occurs when upgrading from a version earlier than 1.8.2 to version 1.8.2 or later.
bugs.impact: System hardware health is incorrectly shown as unhealthy.
bugs.workaround: Reset the component attributes by calling below API as below: docker exec -it diag-agent psf run POST:components/reset component=appliance/hardware/drives/disk-encryption
bugs.fix: Component attributes have been updated to correctly reflect the actual system state.

bugs.title: Support for AFM DOS packet drops in TMSTAT in F5OS
bugs.symptoms: There are no visible hardware stats in F5OS tmstats for when AFM DoS packets are dropped.
bugs.conditions: -- Viewing hardware stats -- AFM DoS packets are getting dropped
bugs.impact: Affects understanding where packet drops have occurred.
bugs.workaround: Raise TCP ACK (TS) vector thresholds per K000139860 Disable the vector if not needed
bugs.fix: AFM DOS packet drops are visible in tmstat in F5OS.

bugs.title: Observing FCS Errors on system controller Peer HG Links
bugs.symptoms: The symptom of this issue is FCS error counters incrementing on control plane system controller peer HG links.
bugs.conditions: Run a system with 1.8.1+ that has the 6.5.26 version of the broadcom SDK.
bugs.impact: Error counters increment, no system impact is observed aside from the counters incrementing.
bugs.fix: Had to modify SDK at init time to properly set advertisements to disable FEC on the peer links when running 6.5.26 SDK.

bugs.conditions: -- LLDP in use. -- ConfD restarts or reconnects.
bugs.impact: No functional impact.
bugs.workaround: NA
bugs.fix: Thread processing has been improved to enable smoother restarts and reconnections.

bugs.title: Open Telemetry - system.disk.usage is always reported 0 on rSeries and VELOS
bugs.symptoms: Open Telemetry - system.disk.usage is always reported 0 on rSeries and VELOS
bugs.conditions: In all cases when a telemetry exporter is configured
bugs.impact: In all cases when a telemetry exporter is configured, the system.disk.usage is always reported 0
bugs.fix: When an exporter is configured, the value for system.disk.usage is always 0. This is because of mapping the metric to a wrong tmstat table. As a part of fix, mapped this correctly to report the correct value of stats.

bugs.conditions: Multi-bladed chassis is rebooted after an upgrade to 1.8.2.
bugs.impact: The impact will be related to inter-blade traffic. If imm_enabled is 0 for an affected destination blade, ingress traffic entering the chassis on one blade destined to the tenant deployed on the affected blade will not reach the tenant.
bugs.workaround: Reboot affected blade, on partition issue: cluster nodes node blade-X reboot X being the number of the affected blade.

bugs.title: Serial console access behavior
bugs.symptoms: Console access may be temporarily unavailable.
bugs.conditions: NA
bugs.impact: Could affect maintenance operations.
bugs.workaround: Follow standard recovery procedures.
bugs.fix: Fixed

bugs.title: Multicast traffic can be dropped by Host DLF rate-limiter
bugs.symptoms: Multicast traffic from a tenant can be dropped by the host DLF rate-limiter, causing traffic loss.
bugs.conditions: Egress multicast traffic exceeding 2500 packets per second.
bugs.impact: Loss of multicast traffic.
bugs.workaround: Create a static FDB entry for the multicast MAC address.
bugs.fix: We changed the behavior of the FPGA code to remove multicast packets that miss the L2 table from being classified as DLF.

bugs.title: System health warning for a PCI Express "Completion Timeout" error may appear after the system starts
bugs.symptoms: After the system starts, users may see a system health warning for "RAS AER 'Completion Timeout' uncorrectable error" (rasdaemon:aer:uncorrectable:completion-timeout). The system log may also contain PCI Express (PCIe) "Completion Timeout" messages for the field-programmable gate array (FPGA) devices. Correctable PCIe errors may also be logged. The cause of the error has not been determined.
bugs.conditions: The error can occur while the system is starting, while the FPGA devices are being loaded and connected. The error is intermittent and has been seen on platforms that contain FPGA devices.
bugs.impact: No functional impact is known. The warning clears on its own after the hourly health check finds no errors in the past hour. In earlier releases, this error could leave a blade stuck in startup with its interfaces shown as NOT_PRESENT. That no longer happens.
bugs.workaround: No action is required. The warning clears automatically.

bugs.title: On r5xxx, multicast packets are replicated to unused ports causing invalid packet drops.
bugs.symptoms: On r5xxx systems, multicast packets are forwarded to unused ports of the crossbar switch, resulting in packet drops on those ports. Because the ports are unused, the drop counters are meaningless.
bugs.conditions: Multicast packets received on a front-panel interface.
bugs.impact: None, this is purely cosmetic.
bugs.fix: Don't include unused ports in multicast duplication.

bugs.title: Logs in /var/confd/log are not rotated on system controllers
bugs.symptoms: Log files in /var/confd/log are not rotated on system controllers. Upgrades may fail due to a timeout.
bugs.conditions: -- A chassis-based system.
bugs.impact: If the files get too large, there can be disk space issues. It can also cause upgrades to fail due to a timeout.
bugs.workaround: If these files get too large, they can be pared down using the Linux "truncate" command. Note that this will remove log messages from these files.

bugs.title: Prompt-statusd process occasionally cores
bugs.symptoms: Occasionally the prompt-statusd daemon will core.
bugs.conditions: This can occur in prompt-statusd during normal operation.
bugs.impact: After core, service will restart the operation

bugs.title: TACACS External Authentication Failure after a software upgrade
bugs.symptoms: TACACS users are not able to login to the device.
bugs.conditions: TACACS+ server sends back an authorization reply with an auth status of 'PASS_REPL' (pass + *replace all attributes*) instead of 'PASS_ADD' (pass + *add* to attributes)
bugs.impact: TACACS users will be unable to log in when the server is configured under the specified conditions.
bugs.workaround: Avoid using PASS_REPL on Tacacs server.
bugs.fix: After upgrading device to latest EHF build, the issue is not reproduced.

bugs.title: BX110 ports configured for 40G can fail to link with OPT-036 optics
bugs.symptoms: BX110 front panel interface configured for 40G with OPT-0036 optic fails to achieve link.
bugs.conditions: BX110 front panel interface configured for 40G and using an OPT-0036 optic.
bugs.impact: Front panel interface remains DOWN, preventing traffic from flowing.
bugs.fix: Implement a software workaround that first writes a reset bit to '0' before writing it to a '1'.

bugs.title: The "system aaa tls config passphrase" command does not validate whether or not the new passphrase correctly decrypts the current key file
bugs.symptoms: If the GUI is configured to use a custom key and certificate ("system aaa tls config certificate" and "system aaa tls config key") and use an encrypted key file protected by a passphrase ("system aaa tls config passphrase"), the system fails to perform validation for subsequent changes to the passphrase (and the system is not decrypting and re-encrypting the key file).
bugs.conditions: -- System is configured to use a custom key and certificate for GUI access. -- They key is encrypted with a passphrase, and "system aaa tls config passphrase" is used to set this passphrase in F5OS. -- "system aaa tls config passphrase" is later used to change the passphrase, but the underlying key is not changed.
bugs.impact: -- Key migration fails -- HTTP GUI and API are rendered unusable
bugs.workaround: Using the CLI: -- Manually re-encrypt the key to use the new passphrase. OR -- Change the passphrase ("system aaa tls config passphrase") back to the one that matches they key.

bugs.title: The port of Allowed IP Addresses is shown as "Select" on GUI instead of port number.
bugs.symptoms: While editing Allow List Entry under System Settings -> System Security -> Allowed IP Addresses in the "Port" field you see "Select" instead of port number e.g. "22".
bugs.conditions: You configured Allowed IP Address Entry for port other than SNMP (161).
bugs.impact: The word "select" is incorrectly displayed, but it otherwise has no effect.

bugs.title: VELOS controller unhealthy if it is rebooted after clean install while platform-services-deployment still starting
bugs.symptoms: A newly-installed controller running the correct software version is inaccessible from the network or peer controller, even though it is booted into F5OS. Log messages in /var/log/messages or "journalctl -u platform-services-deployment" indicating that it failed to pull docker images, and the initial registries were set as a mirror of themselves: platform-deployment: Initial registry (port 2000) setup as mirror of port 2000 registry complete platform-deployment: Initial registry (port 2500) setup as mirror of port 2500 registry complete [...] platform-deployment: Pulling repository localhost:2500/vcc-partition-software-manager platform-deployment: Error: image vcc-partition-software-manager:7.2.7-f5os-c-1-8-1-candidate.2025-02-11-05-55-35.S383ff41b not found platform-deployment: Unexpected error encountered while starting platform services via docker-compose. platform-deployment: Nov 12 11:57:57 controller-2.chassis.local platform-deployment[3342]: Error: image vcc-partition-software-manager:7.2.7-f5os-c-1-8-1-candidate.2025-02-11-05-55-35.S383ff41b not found platform-deployment: Platform services done
bugs.conditions: A fresh install of software on a VELOS system controller (an RMA replacement system controller, or a clean install via PXE or USB). During the initial boot into F5OS, the new system controller is rebooted while platform-services-deployment is still running in the background.
bugs.impact: The VELOS system controller remains inoperative.
bugs.workaround: Perform a clean install of the VELOS system controller software again, and do not reboot the controller while platform-services-deployment is still running.

bugs.title: Disabled ports or port mode mismatchs can cause bad register reads.
bugs.symptoms: When a Front panel port is disabled or the port mode is mismatched, it can cause incorrect register reads. This may manifest as port interface flapping on other unrelated ports.
bugs.conditions: Front Panel Port is disabled or a port mode mismatch, such as a 100GE optic installed when the port is configured for 40GE operating mode.
bugs.impact: The status on other interfaces may incorrectly show ‘down’ when the interface is ‘up’ or other unexpected behavior.
bugs.workaround: Enable all Front Panel ports, even those not in use, and ensure there are no port mode mismatches.
bugs.fix: Updated FPGA firmware is required for the fix.

bugs.title: Disabled ports or port mode mismatches can cause bad register reads.
bugs.symptoms: When a Front panel port is disabled or the port mode is mismatched, it can cause incorrect register reads. This may manifest as port interface flapping on other unrelated ports.
bugs.conditions: Front Panel Port is disabled or a port mode mismatch, such as a 100GE optic installed when the port is configured for 40GE operating mode.
bugs.impact: The status on other interfaces may incorrectly show ‘down’ when the interface is ‘up’ or other unexpected behavior.
bugs.workaround: Enable all Front Panel ports, even those not in use, and ensure there are no port mode mismatches.
bugs.fix: Updated FPGA firmware is required for the fix.

bugs.title: Application level DOS via improper configuration of the look aside memory allocator.
During live-upgrade, "show cluster cluster-status" shows "K3s IMAGE update has failed, will retry"
bugs.symptoms: If the prompt status is stuck in either of these 2 stages after F5OS-A live upgrade: 'Cluster update in-progress/Waiting for cluster service', checkout the cluster state by running following command: 'show cluster cluster-status' If the cluster state shows some output like this where K3s Image update has failed, and confirm that this same issue is hit. INDEX STATUS --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ... . . . ... 6 2024-07-25 15:51:23.567837+00:00 - K3s IMAGE update has failed, will retry. ... . . . ...
bugs.conditions: This can occur while performing a live upgrade of F5OS-A or power on the device.
bugs.impact: The prompt status is stuck in 'Cluster update in-progress/Waiting for cluster service' error.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the system. The upgrade or boot up process will resume and complete.

bugs.title: Tenant Disk can be removed as a result of misinterpreting system state.
bugs.symptoms: A tenant disk will be removed from compute nodes when the tenant appears to be running from partition ConfD CLI. As a result, the VM pods cannot be started because the disk is gone. The orchestration software will notice this and recreate the tenant with a new disk, but all configuration and other data associated with the original tenant will be lost.
bugs.conditions: - Power Cycle is performed on the a controller, forcing the partition go to the one staying up if it was not already there - Cause a fault in the system that is up (like unplug mgmt interface cable). This is to cause the controller that was power cycled to take over as soon as it is able to. - When the node that was down takes over (because the one that became active is at fault after unplugging cable) the tenants in the partition could end up getting wiped. This is intermittent since it is cause by a race condition at failover time. When the failover occurs, the other partition instance is running on controller node that will take a number of seconds to become active on the controller side and take over the kubernetes layer.
bugs.impact: The orchestration software that takes over because the other node is at fault could end up running the reconciliation logic to add and remove tenants with no data because the DB read is not done and/or the kubernetes layer is not ready for queries. If the reconciliation tenant list is empty, orchestration software end up misinterpreting it as if there were no tenants, causing tenants to be removed. But the DB does have the tenants. Subsequent iterations will detect there is a tenant that needs to be created, but at this point the disk is gone and a new disk gets created.
bugs.workaround: Because this is a race condition that occurs when a double fault happens (powercycle on one controller node and not having the mgmt interface up on the other controller node), the only way to try avoid it is to be ahead of the faults reported by the system.
bugs.fix: Orchestration software that was meant to reconcile what was missed should not take any action if the information is not available.

bugs.title: Rsync.log files on blades are not rotated
bugs.symptoms: The rsync.log files on VELOS blades are not rotated.
bugs.conditions: -- Chassis-based system. -- Large (several GB) rsync.log file on at least one blade.
bugs.impact: This can cause disk space issues on blades, which can cause various issues, including the failure to run tenants.
bugs.workaround: Manually truncate the rsync.log file. 1. From the active controller, ssh to the blade with the large log file, e.g.: ssh blade-1 2. Truncate the rsync.log file: truncate -s0 /var/F5/partitionN/log/rsync.log ... where N is the ID of the partition with the large rsync.log file. NOTE: This will remove all the contents of the rsync.log file. If you wish to keep this data, back it up before performing this operation.

bugs.title: After a controller upgrade, out-of-sync etcd processes can lead to unhealthy cluster
bugs.symptoms: After a controller upgrade, it is possible that the controller etcd processes can be out of sync causing the cluster to go into an unhealthy state.
bugs.conditions: The etcd processes require a quorum of three and the third etcd process is not being launched which leaves the etcds on both controllers in an inconsistent state.
bugs.impact: The cluster will remain in an unhealthy state.
bugs.workaround: On the active controller, manually launch the third etcd instance, by running this command at the root shell /etc/etcd/launch_etcd.sh Then issue a controller failover.

bugs.title: Tenant outage caused by deletion of VLAN in the tenant and unassignment of the VLAN from F5OS
bugs.symptoms: When a VLAN inside the tenant is deleted and the VLAN is un-assigned from F5OS, a service for the tenant could be deleted. Deletion of service will cause an outage on the tenant. Here are the two log messages on F5OS datapath-cp-proxy[11]: priority="Info" msgid=0x5901000000000045 msg="Confd Event Update:" EVENT="DELETE_SERVICE_ID" FROM="CONFD" TENANTNAME="" ATSE=0 SUBMODULE=0. datapath-cp-proxy[11]: priority="Info" msgid=0x5901000000000034 msg="Service Instance Update Success." TENANTNAME="tenant-1" DOSGRP="[2]" SVCGRP="[7]" SVCID=22.
bugs.conditions: -- Deletion of the VLAN inside the tenant. -- Un-assignment of the same VLAN from the F5OS.
bugs.impact: Because the service is removed, all VLANs on that service will be inaccessible for the tenant and cause an outage in the tenant.
bugs.workaround: If a VLAN is going to be deleted from the tenant, first un-assign the VLAN inside the tenant from F5OS. Then after a 2 second delay, delete the VLAN inside the tenant.

bugs.title: K3s install fails if a weak SSH MAC algorithm is configured
bugs.symptoms: If a weak SSH MAC algorithm is configured (via "system security services service sshd"), K3s will fail to install.
bugs.conditions: -- Appliance. -- Weak SSH MAC algorithm configured.
bugs.impact: This can prevent upgrades or K3s reinstallations.
bugs.workaround: Configure a strong SSH MAC algorithm, e.g. hmac-sha2-256. In the CLI: config system security services service sshd config macs [ hmac-sha2-256 ] commit It is possible to configure multiple MAC algorithms, in which case the administrator should keep the stronger algorithms enabled as well.

bugs.title: DmaTenantTcpCopOperHdlr, couldn't find stats for tenant
bugs.symptoms: An error is found in platform.log platform-stats-bridge[10]: nodename=controller-1(p3) priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x4305000000000008 msg="" msg="DmaTenantTcpCopOperHdlr, couldn't find stats for tenant".
bugs.conditions: -- Tenant is in configured or not deployed completely -- tcp-cop stats are queried when there are not yet any stats. (show tenants tenant tcp-cop tcp-cop)
bugs.impact: No functional impact. The log message is logged at the error level and should be logged at the warning level.
bugs.fix: The Err log is changed to Warning log in the latest versions (from 2.0+ and C-1.8.3)

bugs.title: The Virtual Server is not receiving traffic due to an incorrect VLAN update from F5OS platform
bugs.symptoms: When a specific native VLAN is configured for a port in virtual-wire, the incoming packets still arrive with VLAN ID 4094, while the Virtual Server expects traffic with the configured VLAN ID.
bugs.conditions: Configuring a specific native vlan on a port and then configuring it in virtual-wire.
bugs.impact: When enabling/disabling virtual-wire mode on a port with a configured native VLAN, the port default VLAN was being set with values (4094 for vwire enable, 4095 for vwire disable), ignoring any existing native VLAN configuration.
bugs.workaround: Once the virtual-wire is configured on the port, if the remove and re-add the native vlans to the interfaces, the hardware should get programmed correctly.
bugs.fix: Added a fix such that ensure native VLAN configuration is respected and preserved throughout the virtual-wire lifecycle.

bugs.title: F5OS does not validate the LDAP TLS CA certificate
bugs.symptoms: F5OS does not validate that LDAP CA cert config (system aaa authentication ldap tls_cacert) is a valid CA certificate. An error similar to the following will be logged: authd[7]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x3901000000000101 msg="LDAP API error during : -" oper="SASL bind" code=-1 msg="Can't contact LDAP server".
bugs.conditions: -- F5OS system configured to use remote authentication via LDAP. -- Invalid ldap tls_cacert configured.
bugs.impact: Remote LDAP authentication does not work.

bugs.title: Switchd may process blade slot operational data updates that are not intended to trigger any action
bugs.symptoms: On software upgrade v1.7.x to v1.8.x and later releases following with a firmware upgrade, it is observed that the power field in the slot operdata may fluctuate. This behavior can cause switchd to incorrectly detect that the slot's dataplane ports require reconfiguration, resulting in a link flap on the affected blade dataplane port(s) This will show up in the blade fpga manager as VOQ watchdog timeouts.
bugs.conditions: Upgrade from v1.7.x to v1.8.x and later that also involve a firmware update.
bugs.impact: Degraded dataplane performance and TMM HA failovers.
bugs.workaround: Reboot system controllers and / or impacted blades.
bugs.fix: Switchd configures the dataplane ports of a slot only in response to changes in slot presence or blade type

bugs.title: Tenant disk can get removed when there is a double fault scenario
bugs.symptoms: Tenant disk will be recreated from scratch, prompting for changing the password from the default one.
