bugs.conditions: When a controller is booting and is required to become the active role (including all partition active instances) due to the other controller being unavailable, a race condition may occur. This can result in the orchestration daemon removing tenant disks, as it has not have acquired the latest system state.
bugs.impact: Tenant disk is lost. No way to recover it.
bugs.workaround: Whenever possible, perform a power cycle on the controllers following a partition failover to the active controllers. Additionally, verify that there are no faults in the controller hosting the active partitions. This approach helps mitigate race conditions that may occur when the standby controller, during startup, is required to take over due to an unhealthy active controller.
bugs.fix: Removed the race condition that could cause prematurely removing tenant disks.

bugs.title: Vqf bitstream failed to load on blade
bugs.symptoms: When there is a power outage/down without power backup then sometime a blade's usb drive will be disconnected. That will cause the vqf bitstream to fail to load.
bugs.conditions: Install the 1.8.2-C build on the system and perform power cycle. (This is highly intermittent issue)
bugs.impact: Blade will be in an inoperative state.
bugs.workaround: Power cycle will bring the system back
bugs.fix: NA

bugs.title: LLDP core found while upgrading chassis
bugs.symptoms: LLDPD process terminated unexpectedly(core file) during database connection establishment due to an unhandled exception.
bugs.conditions: -- ConfD Connection Timeout. -- ConfD not running when LLDPD started.
bugs.impact: LLDP crashes and restarts. No functionality impact.

bugs.title: Observed ctrlplane0x interface missing & ixgbe load errors after Active System Controller power cycle test
bugs.symptoms: After performing a power cycle of active system controller, an error of loading ixgbe diver is observed which results in ctrlplane0x port missing in team0. Errors: [ 5.611594] ixgbe: probe of 0000:06:00.0 failed with error -5
bugs.conditions: Install v1.8.X-C/v1.7.C-X build on the system and perform active system controller power cycle. (This is intermittent issue) On the failure case, dmesg logs will point: [ 5.611594] ixgbe: probe of 0000:06:00.0 failed with error -5
bugs.impact: A malformed trunk between the control plane switch and controller host can lead to unpredictably unreliable traffic flows between the controller host and control plane switch.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the controller.
bugs.fix: The failed PCI device has been reinitialised.

bugs.title: Error Catalog not generating Hex Values in msgid
bugs.symptoms: Error catalog messages were not generated past 9. Hex values A-F were skipped if they were in the msgid.
bugs.conditions: When there is a log message that has msgid that go past 9.
bugs.impact: Previously generated log messages did not have Hex msgid values past 9. Clouddocs error catalog page will not show the HEX msgid entries.
bugs.fix: Allow msgid's to represented as hex values.

bugs.title: FDB entries may expire when multiple entries hash to the same FPGA table index and traffic is intermittent
bugs.symptoms: L2/FDB entries may expire even when traffic is arriving at the FPGA of the Appliance or VELOS Blade.
bugs.conditions: L2 entries which internally hash to the same table index inside the FPGA can lead to the expiration of the entry when traffic is arriving on intervals of more than 30 seconds from that MAC address. On each interval, an age refresh message might be lost, leading to decrement the age of the entry on 30 seconds. When the entry reaches the last period it will expire, and then it will be re-learnt again.
bugs.impact: The expiration of the FDB entry can lead to Destination Lookup Failures that are rate-limited, i.e. traffic loss. Depending on the scenario this could lead to intermittent potential outages between the entry expires, and it is learnt again.
bugs.workaround: Create a static FDB entry for the MAC address that suffers expiration issues. See K000152328. Ensure that traffic from the MAC address expiring arrives continuously under 30 seconds intervals. Open a Support case and request an EHF.

bugs.title: Controller upgrade struck in in-progress after upgrading the chassis from 1.7.1 EHF1 to 1.8.2 EHF3
bugs.symptoms: When performing a rolling System controller upgrade from 1.7.1 to 1.8.x it is possible on of the upgrading System Controllers does not complete its upgrade and show system image displays "in-progress" for that system controllers upgrade status indefinitely.
bugs.conditions: Problem is known to occur on a fully loaded CX1610 chassis.
bugs.impact: Dataplane should continue to function at a reduced rate. However, the System Controllers will not form a ConfD HA pair until both System Controllers are running the same System Controller version and management communication may be lost with the upgrading controller.
bugs.workaround: Perform a manual switch of both service and os versions to match the peer System Controller. Example: echo "switch cc_os <iso-version> " | nc -U /var/sw-mgmt.unix echo "switch cc_serv <iso-version> no_restart" | nc -U /var/sw-mgmt.unix where <iso-version> is the version the peer System Controller is currently running. Then reboot the system reboot the system controller
bugs.fix: Ugrades from 1.7.1 to releases 1.8.x and later are no longer subject to becoming stuck in the "in-progress" state.

bugs.title: No logs observed when mgmt interface state changes
bugs.symptoms: When mgmt interface state changes, there are no logs observed in platform.log.
bugs.conditions: Mgmt interface state change.
bugs.impact: There is no functional impact. interface state changes can be still read from Confd.
bugs.fix: NA

bugs.title: Chassis partition go-standby command does not work correctly after Active/Active resolution
bugs.symptoms: If an internal chassis network partition causes the chassis partition HA pair to go active/active, the HA pair will resolve to the current preferred controller when the network partition is fixed. But future attempts to manually fail over to the other controller using the 'go-standby' command will immediately fail back to the original controller.
bugs.conditions: If an internal controller network partition causes partition HA pair to go active/active the internal failover state is left inconsistent.
bugs.impact: The go-standby command will not work.
bugs.workaround: Proper operation can be restored by restarting the partition HA on the non-preferred controller (controller-2 if in 'auto' mode): syscon-1-active(config)# system diagnostics os-utils docker restart node controller-2 service partition1_ha Restarting container affects configuration and data path. Do you want to proceed? [yes/no] yes result partition1_ha restarted successfully syscon-1-active(config)#
bugs.fix: The go-standby command works correctly after active/active resolution.

bugs.title: After Power Cycle testing on 1.8.2 EHF-3, observed partition mgmt interface stuck DOWN
bugs.symptoms: Access to partition management can be permanently lost if the System Controller is power cycled.
bugs.conditions: Power cycle the system controller on which the active instance of a partition is running.
bugs.impact: Management access to partition CLI / webUI lost.
bugs.workaround: Delete and recreate the partition management interface from the System Controller ConfD partition configuration. config# no partitions partition <name> config mgmt-ip config# commit config# partitions partition <name> config mgmt-ip <ipv4 | ipv6> address <ip address> prefix-length <length> gateway <gateway address>
bugs.fix: Reconnection to partition CLI/webUI through the management IP can be reliably reestablished after power cycling the system controller hosting the active partition instance.

bugs.title: FPGA firmware health status reported as unhealthy/error
bugs.symptoms: Shortly after a VELOS BX520 blade boots up, the health status of the blade shows an error for one of the FPGAs, it never clears, and the blade still successfully runs traffic. There are also verification errors in velos.log. For example, in confd: "blade/firmware/fpga/atse1 firmware:update-status unhealthy error error" In velos.log, entries such as: "FWU response error." ... "PCI slot ca:00.0 width is 4; expected 8." FWU atse2 Verification failed, retrying (also appears in the blade PEL) FWU atse2 Verification failed (also appears in the blade PEL)
bugs.conditions: Booting up a VELOS BX520 blade.
bugs.impact: One or more of the FPGA-to-CPU (PCIe) links may be running in a degraded state and could affect the bandwidth of traffic between the blade's FPGA and CPU.
bugs.workaround: The blade can be rebooted to retry the FPGA load process, which will retrain all the FPGA PCIe links.
bugs.fix: Retries were increased for the FPGA load process to make it more reliable.

bugs.title: The file /var/omd/CLUSTER_REINSTALL on Standby causes openshift reinstall after failover
bugs.symptoms: If /var/omd/CLUSTER_REINSTALL exists on Standby, when there is a controller failover, an openshift reinstall triggers.
bugs.conditions: - /var/omd/CLUSTER_REINSTALL exists on the Standby controller. - A failover to that controller occurs.
bugs.impact: Service outage of Chassis
bugs.workaround: The file /var/omd/CLUSTER_REINSTALL is created by the user in order to trigger an openshift reinstall. It should not normally exist. Proactively check that /var/omd/CLUSTER_REINSTALL does not exist on the Standby controller. For example, from Active blade console: [root@controller-A(VELOS):Active ~]# ssh controller-B ls -la /var/omd/CLUSTER_REINSTALL ls: cannot access /var/omd/CLUSTER_REINSTALL: No such file or directory Where "controller-B" is the other controller, for example "controller-2".

bugs.title: Tenant image upload failure when there is still sufficient space available
bugs.symptoms: Tenant image upload failure when there is still sufficient space available. You may see below error from logs "Disk usage exceeded threshold."
bugs.conditions: When there is sufficient space available, tenant image upload fails.
bugs.impact: Unable to upload tenant image
bugs.fix: Fixed in 2.0

bugs.title: Stale cache info can cause inaccurate tenant orchestration operations
bugs.symptoms: - A tenant is showing as deployed, has no running pods. - A tenant that is supposed to be running is not running while a deleted tenant is trying to come up (in terms of pods in the system).
bugs.conditions: Sequence of failover operations on the partition when tenant configuration changes were being processed
bugs.impact: Tenants may not reflect the latest committed configuration state.
bugs.workaround: Failover the partition or recreate the tenant.
bugs.fix: Updated standby cache regularly and cleared the stale info before orchestration daemon becomes the active one.

bugs.title: Invalid or unresponsive rsyslog remote servers for log forwarding can exhaust system memory.
bugs.symptoms: System memory usage will increase over time without boundaries.
bugs.conditions: Remote-syslog servers configured with TCP protocol that cannot establish a connection (or has a unreliable connectivity).
bugs.impact: The rsyslog daemon will retry, and memory will continue to increase. This could potentially exhaust system memory.
bugs.workaround: Fix the connection, remove the invalid or flaky servers from config, OR use the UDP protocol.
bugs.fix: The new syntax used for rsyslogd remote-servers forwarding configuration requires specifying for each forwarding action a linked list queue type. This will implicitly use the default queue size of 1000 messages (or lower for earlier versions of rsyslogd).

bugs.title: F5OS web UI fails to load upon refreshing the page
bugs.symptoms: After performing a live upgrade of F5OS, refreshing the browser while on the appliance/partition/controller web UI returns a "404 Not Found — The requested URL was not found on this server" error. The web UI does not recover until the browser navigates back to the root URL manually.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs on F5OS-based platforms (chassis and appliances) when a user refreshes the browser page.
bugs.impact: Access to the webUI may be lost when the browser is refreshed.
bugs.fix: Added a client-side fallback in the F5OS http-server to redirect stale deep-link requests back to the application root on page reload.

bugs.title: F5OS Backplane connectivity issues: 'TMM Not Ready', VoQ EMMs disabled for Blades due to VQF-CC link failures
bugs.symptoms: Dataplane switch interfaces corresponding to the even slot of a BX520 blade may be incorrectly disabled, causing a link outage to the Dataplane port of the even slot BX520 blade.
bugs.conditions: The Platform HAL sends a chassis platform response to the Chassis Manager indicating lop_ok is 0 for the even slot of a BX520 blade. Consequently, the Chassis Manager registers the blade as 'not present' (present = 0), prompting switchd to disable the port associated with the even-numbered slot.
bugs.impact: VQF IMM watchdog timeouts appear in the FPGA manager log.
bugs.workaround: Reboot both CCs. Can be performed in service if standby is rebooted first, followed by lsystem redundancy go-standby and then rebooting the new standby.
bugs.fix: The Chassis Manager will not publish a loss of presence specifically for the even slot of BX520 blades, ensuring that the corresponding dataplane port is not inadvertently disabled by switchd.

bugs.title: WebUI Connection may be refused After Upgrading to version F5OS-A 1.8.3
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading from version 1.5.3 to 1.8.3, access to the WebUI is no longer available. All connection attempts result in a "connection refused" error.
bugs.conditions: Occurs when upgrading from v1.5.3 to v1.8.3
bugs.impact: WebUI becomes inaccessible.

bugs.title: Intermittent webUI startup failure after F5OS v1.8.x upgrade caused by SSL certificate generation issue
bugs.symptoms: In rare cases after upgrading to F5OS v1.8.x, the Web GUI (httpd) may fail to start. System logs may show a missing ServerName directive, and the /etc/auth-config/default/f5os.cert file may be missing or zero bytes.
bugs.conditions: This issue can occur in certain scenarios where the upgrade process fails to properly generate or retain the f5os.cert certificate file, and the authentication-manager does not recover from the missing or empty certificate, resulting in an invalid httpd configuration.
bugs.impact: The webUI is completely unavailable. CLI and API access remain functional.
bugs.workaround: Restart the authentication-mgr and http-server services using the following CLI command: system diagnostics os-utils docker restart node platform service authentication-mgr system diagnostics os-utils docker restart node platform service http-server

bugs.title: Removing the active controller does not trigger an immediate tenant failover
bugs.symptoms: On a VELOS chassis setup where the BIG-IP tenant is active for a traffic group and the HA score includes a weighted value for F5OS_INTERNAL_TRUNK. Removing the active controller does not result in an immediate failover.
bugs.conditions: The tenant is active for a traffic group and is running on the controller that is currently active for the partition hosting the tenant. The active system controller is removed or powered off using AOM.
bugs.impact: Tenant failover is delayed upto 4min when an active controller of the active tenant is pulled out .
bugs.fix: Reduce the polling interval for lost VQF-link confD events to shorten the event detection time.

bugs.title: LACP LAG interface stops forwarding packets when interface is disabled and re-enabled
bugs.symptoms: When an interface that is part of a LACP LAG is disabled and then re-enabled, the interface stops forwarding packets.
bugs.conditions: LACP LAG interface disabled and re-enabled.
bugs.impact: LACP LAG down since BPDU packets are not being captured.
bugs.workaround: A reboot re-enables packet forwarding on the interface.
bugs.fix: Restarting the appliance allows BPDU packet capture which fixes LACP.

bugs.title: Snmpwalk misses LAG interface stats intermittently
bugs.symptoms: Though the LAG interface is configured in system, some stats for the LAG interface will be missed in snmpwalk output intermittently.
bugs.conditions: Issue is rarely observed when running snmpwalk in a loop continuously.
bugs.impact: Snmpwalk may not display all statistics for the LAG interfaces.
bugs.workaround: Run snmpwalk after a 20 second delay.
bugs.fix: Ensured all LAG interface statistics are properly reported in SNMP walk output.

bugs.title: Long BIG-IP tenant names will prevent virtual console access
bugs.symptoms: Creating a BIG-IP tenant in the GUI with a name longer than 32 characters will prevent virtual console access to the tenant.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP tenant name is longer than 32 characters.
bugs.impact: The creation of the tenant-console user fails, preventing access to the virtual console for that tenant.
bugs.workaround: Use tenant names that don't exceed 32 characters in length.

bugs.title: TLS client authentication for LDAP servers not working
bugs.symptoms: F5OS does not authenticate to LDAP servers.
bugs.conditions: - LDAP authentication in F5OS configured to use a client certificate and key ("system aaa authentication ldap tls_cert" and "system aaa authentication ldap tls_key"). - Either or both of the following: -- An LDAP group mapping is configured (ldap-group specified for a role) -- Active Directory enabled and Unix Attributes disabled
bugs.impact: F5OS is unable to connect to the LDAP server

bugs.title: System is not booting after trying password recovery steps on rocky OS
bugs.symptoms: When tried to use password recovery steps as mentioned in the KB article https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000134739, system is unable to boot to OS.
bugs.conditions: When tried to use password recovery steps as mentioned in the KB article https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000134739, system is unable to boot to OS.
bugs.impact: System is unable to boot to OS.
bugs.workaround: In the recovery steps, if we use reboot instead of the 2nd exit, the containers/services are getting up as expected.
bugs.fix: KB article must be updated with proper steps mentioning that reboot must used, instead of the second exit.

bugs.title: Enable login-attribute to work with UPN based authentication in F5OS
bugs.symptoms: Authentication using userPrincipalName is not enabled by default in F5OS.
bugs.conditions: In F5OS, When configured active_directory to true and trying to authenticate the user with userPrincipalName instead of sAMAccountName will fail.
bugs.impact: Authentication using userPrincipalName will fail in F5OS for active directory based remote authentications.
bugs.workaround: 1. Configure login-attrribute to userPrincipalName from ConfD CLI as below: system aaa authentication ldap login-attrribute userPrincipalName 2. For client based UPN authentication - a. Client Certificates should have been generated using UPN name b. Configure in which field we need to fetch username in confd via "system aaa authentication clientcert config client-cert-name-field" c. Configure login-attribute as userPrincipalName in confd via "system aaa authentication ldap login-attrribute userPrincipalName" Note: We can configure login-attribute via confd cli or restconf api. In this release there is no support to configure login-attribute from GUI.
bugs.fix: Added configurable parameter in confd to enable "userPrincipalName" based authentication.

bugs.title: F5 rSeries Port Down, Optic Unplugged, or other frequent unexpected events.
bugs.symptoms: A small number of r5000/r10000 appliances have been found with a hardware defect on the internal PCIe links. This defect can result in erroneous internal register reads, causing the system to falsely detect conditions such as link down or optic unplugged. Other alarms or indications of system instability are possible.
bugs.conditions: There are no special conditions. This issue occurs frequently on affected systems.
bugs.impact: The system is unstable and unusable.
bugs.workaround: There is no specific log entry to detect the issue. Provide a QKVIEW for assessment by F5. If the issue is found in the QKVIEW, the unit must be returned and replaced.
bugs.fix: The manufacturing test has been updated to screen these defects in production. Existing units confirmed to have the issue must be returned and replaced.

bugs.title: Controller can incorrectly be removed from the OpenShift cluster during rolling upgrade
bugs.symptoms: After a rolling upgrade of the controller software, one of the controllers may incorrectly be removed from the OpenShift cluster. This leaves the OpenShift cluster in a state where there is only one leader node in the cluster.
bugs.conditions: This can happen during a rolling upgrade due to a race condition on checking the status of the standby controller.
bugs.impact: If this occurs the affected controller will no longer be in the OpenShift cluster, so HA availability of the OpenShift cluster between the controllers will be compromised.
bugs.workaround: To protect against a controller being removed from the cluster during the rolling upgrade while the active controller is still running the older software, it is recommended to do a "touch /tmp/omd/pause" on the active controller before starting the rolling upgrade. This will keep the down rev controller from removing the newly upgraded controller if the bug is hit. The pause file be automatically removed when the controller is upgraded after the newly upgraded controller becomes active. The workaround to recover once the controller has been removed from the cluster is to manually retrigger the addition of the removed controller to the Openshift cluster. If controller-1 was removed, on controller 2 the user would do a touch /var/omd/CONTROLLER1_REINSTALL If controller-2 was removed, on controller 1 the user would do a touch /var/omd/CONTROLLER2_REINSTALL
bugs.fix: The race condition that led to the controller being incorrectly removed from the cluster has been fixed, so that a controller will no longer be removed from the cluster during rolling upgrade once the controllers have been upgraded.

bugs.title: Tenant management IP may be inaccessible until ARP entries timeout after controller failover
bugs.symptoms: After a controller failover, or reboot of the active CC mode, Stale ARP entries may cause the tenant management IPs to not be accessible. GARP packets are sent, but there was a race between the management port on the new CC becoming active and the tenant orchestration layer sending the GARPs
bugs.conditions: This can happen after reboot/power cycle of the active controller, or manual failover the system controllers.
bugs.impact: The tenant management IP will become inaccessible until the ARP entries in the upstream switch times out, or the tenant generates outbound traffic on the management port that causes an update of the ARP table.
bugs.fix: GARPs are now sent for a longer time after the controller failover to make sure they reach the upstream network device.

bugs.title: No guradrail for downgrade from 2.0.0 to lower version when common criteria mode enabled.
bugs.symptoms: The common criteria compliance_cfg file is persistent with status enabled when downgrading from 2.0.0 to a lower version.
bugs.conditions: No guardrail for downgrade from 2.0.0 to lower version when common criteria mode is enabled.
bugs.impact: The common criteria compliance_cfg file will have incorrect information about the common criteria mode.
bugs.workaround: Implement guardrail while downgrading from 2.0.0 when common criteria mode is enabled.
bugs.fix: Once Common criteria mode is enabled, the user will not be able to downgrade to a version that does not support Common Criteria mode. To perform a downgrade, the user must first disable Common Criteria mode.

bugs.title: Controller boot up in rare conditions can impact blade management network after failover
bugs.symptoms: A rare race condition in the vcc-lacpd process can prevent a system controller failover correctly setting the LACP status for LACP based link aggregations. This condition is easily identifiable if the log msgid=0x6602000000000003 originating from vcc-lacpd process is seen since the last controller reboot.
bugs.conditions: Controller reboot. It is more likely though still extremely rare to occur if vcc-lacpd process restarts independently of a controller reboot.
bugs.impact: Blade management network can be impacted which can cause a variety of issues, including blade reboot loops on partition upgrade. If a management aggregation on the controller front panel management ports is configured for LACP, this aggregation may also be impacted.
bugs.workaround: Restart the affected vcc-lacpd process via docker restart cc-lacpd.
bugs.fix: While you may still see msgid=0x6602000000000003, the log no longer indicates a problem as the vcc-lacpd process will appropriately recover.

bugs.title: Enhance logging for clear-all alert cases.
bugs.symptoms: When a Power Supply Unit (PSU) is removed or a hardware component is cleared, there is no corresponding trace or log entry in velos.log or platform.log confirming that the associated alarms were cleared. The system clears the alarms, but it does so silently.
bugs.conditions: Observed the behaviour when triggers a "clear-all" operation for component specific alerts.
bugs.impact: No functional impact. Administrators and support cannot verify via system logs whether an automatic clear-all alert operation was successfully triggered or executed, making it difficult to diagnose edge cases where alarms might fail to clear properly.
bugs.workaround: No
bugs.fix: Logging has been enhanced. The system now explicitly logs informational messages whenever a clear-all request type is received and processed.

bugs.title: Empty File path in upload api leads to core
bugs.symptoms: The utils-agent service crashes
bugs.conditions: Provide an empty file path to the upload api
bugs.impact: Utils-agent crashes and generates a core.
bugs.fix: Empty/Null check added for file path field in upload api to make sure no crash in utils-agent service.

bugs.title: F5OS image import fails with 'Signature verification failed' error
bugs.symptoms: When F5OS ISO certificates were rotated for the first time in October 2025, certificate validity was set to 6 months. Consequently, importing affected images fails after expiration. This issue is limited to image import.
bugs.conditions: Occurs when attempting to import an F5OS ISO image published on or before October 2025.
bugs.impact: F5OS ISO images published on or before October 2025 cannot be imported.
bugs.workaround: Use F5OS ISO images published after October 2025 for import.
bugs.fix: F5OS ISO certificate expiration period has been extended to 39 months.

bugs.title: L2 table become inconsistent after reseating VELOS blades
bugs.symptoms: After reseating blades, L2 tables become inconsistent and traffic is sent to wrong interfaces despite static FIB entries being present.
bugs.conditions: Occurs when multiple VELOS blades are removed and reinserted. L2-agent fails to connect to confd during blade initialization, preventing proper interface/portgroup configuration updates.
bugs.impact: Traffic misdirection, inconsistent L2 tables, SNMP and CLI interface commands may fail.
bugs.workaround: Perform partition failover, disable/re-enable partition, or reseat affected blades.

bugs.title: TCP Packet loss after upgrade with AFM provisioned
bugs.symptoms: After an upgrade, disabled hardware DOS vectors may use old values.
bugs.conditions: -- F5OS tenant -- Upgrade -- AFM provisioned
bugs.impact: DOS thresholds may be incorrectly set or set too low resulting in packet loss that causes poor throughput.
bugs.workaround: Disable and re-enable the disabled DOS vectors. Log into the BIG-IP GUI and navigate to Security ›› DoS Protection : Device Protection Filter attack vectors: tcp click the "Network" text Enable all the disabled vectors by clicking on the vector name and changing state from "disabled" to "mitigate". Then disable the vectors by clicking on the vector name and changing state from "mitigate" to "disabled".

bugs.title: PSU alarms getting cleared during controller failover
bugs.symptoms: PSU fault alarms were not triggered during controller failover.
bugs.conditions: When PSU alarms are present in the system and are followed by a controller failover.
bugs.impact: When PSU health status is displayed as faulty, the corresponding alarm notification does not appear.
bugs.fix: Updated diag-agent service so that any psu alarms won't be cleared by standby controller boot up.

bugs.title: Corrected Typo "tenanat" to "tenant" in Logging
bugs.symptoms: When searching log archives or examining journalctl outputs, the word "tenant" is misspelled as "tenanat" in log messages generated. This prevents support engineers and diagnostic tools from finding relevant log entries when searching or grepping logs for the keyword "tenant".
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs on all supported platforms (including version A-1.8.3) when log entries are written by network-manager or appliance-network-manager.
bugs.impact: Although the spelling error is minor, it directly hinders supportability. Standard diagnostic tools, automated scripts, search queries, or grep commands targeting the word "tenant" will fail to locate these logging records. This can lead to frustration and extended troubleshooting times for support teams.
bugs.workaround: To locate these logs prior to applying the fix, search or grep for the misspelled term tenanat instead of tenant.
bugs.fix: The spelling of "tenant" has been corrected.

bugs.title: PSU alarm disappears intermittently when PSU issues exist
bugs.symptoms: The PSU alarm gets stuck when PSU hardware is faulty and frequent controller switchovers (or power cycle followed by switchovers) that can generate more LOP events and trigger the issue.
bugs.conditions: Faulty PSU hardware and frequent controllers switchover.
bugs.impact: No functional impact but PSU alarm gets stuck in ConfD.
bugs.workaround: Need to replace faulty PSU hardware. For more information on Platform maintenance, refer to Platform Guide: VELOS CX Series. For further assistance, contact F5 Support.

bugs.title: Partition VLAN traffic may dropped for a noticeable period of time during standby initialization
bugs.symptoms: LACP PDUs will be exchanged between the system controller and blade before switchd processes ConfD lagg membership and partition configuration (needed to setup partition vlans). As a result, LACP negotiation between blade and system controller completes before the lagg is actually ready for traffic. The delay between these events is typically ~10 seconds but may be up to 30 seconds.
bugs.conditions: Standby initialization after a reboot or power cycle.
bugs.impact: Services depending on partition connectivity between blade and System Controller are delayed until the System Controller switch daemon configures hardware trunks and partition vlans on the BCM control plane switch.
bugs.workaround: None. Partition traffic between blade and system controller requires successfull LACPD negotiation and trunk/vlan configuration of the control plane switch.

bugs.title: VELOS BX520 ATSE Datapath lockup causes blade to report unhealthy and stop passing traffic
bugs.symptoms: This failure looks like an RQM lockup. An RQM lockup can show up as a DMA receive failure or a DMA transmit failure. Receive failure because the receive queue will not accept HBM memory writes. Transmit failure because loopback health check packets will back up and flow control the transmit data-path.
bugs.conditions: No known conditions. This typically happens on initialization, but has been seen at runtime.
bugs.impact: This causes a data-path lock-up and traffic will not be passed by the affected blade.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the system.
bugs.fix: HBM calibration has been fixed.

bugs.title: 'Show NTP' Command Displays Incorrect Server IP Information
bugs.symptoms: The 'show ntp' command does not indicate an error when a server DNS name cannot be resolved. Additionally, if multiple NTP servers are configured, sometimes it displays the IP address of the synchronized time source as the IP address of all configured servers.
bugs.conditions: Configure multiple NTP servers, possibly with some with unresolvable domain names.
bugs.impact: NTP server information is inaccurate.
bugs.fix: NTP server status display has been corrected.

bugs.title: AOM and fan alarms persist on rSeries appliance persist after hardware replacement and cannot be cleared
bugs.symptoms: After replacing a faulty fan tray via RMA, critical fan and AOM fault alarms remain visible in show system alarms even though replacement hardware is operating normally and show system health reports all components as healthy. Standard docker alert-service clear commands fail to remove the stale alarms.
bugs.conditions: Fan tray hardware replaced via RMA Replacement fans operating correctly (>15K RPM, health status: ok)
bugs.impact: Persistent false-positive critical alarms create operational confusion and monitoring noise.
bugs.workaround: Log into the system as root and run: docker exec alert-service /confd/test/sendAlert -n "<message>" -s <Resource> -r clear -se error -i <ID> -d "<Text>" If above does not clear it. 1. docker restart alert-service 2.docker exec alert-service /confd/test/sendAlert -n "<message>" -s <Resource> -r clear -se error -i <ID> -d "<Text>"

bugs.title: F5OS tpm-integrity-status is Unavailable on certain versions released since October 2025
bugs.symptoms: When you run show components component state tpm-integrity-status, the TPM integrity status reports "Unavailable" # show components component state tpm-integrity-status TPM INTEGRITY NAME STATUS ----------------------- platform Unavailable
bugs.conditions: -- Running the tpm-integrity-status command from F5OS-A or F5OS-C on rSeries or VELOS: - VELOS systems running F5OS-C versions 1.8.2, 1.8.2-EHF, or 1.6.4 - rSeries systems running F5OS-A versions 1.8.3, 1.8.3-EHF, or 1.5.4 - EHFs built after October 15, 2025, including EHFs posted to MyF5 downloads in October such as: - F5OS-A-1.8.3-23493.R5R10.EHF-1 - F5OS-C-1.8.2-28324.CONTROLLER.EHF-1 - F5OS-C-1.8.2-28324.PARTITION.EHF-1 -- The calendar date is on or after April 4, 2026
bugs.impact: The tpm-integrity-status output reads Unavailable after April 4th, 2026.
bugs.workaround: If it is before April 4, 2026, you can run 'show components component state tpm-integrity-status' to get the TPM status.

bugs.title: Possible that cluster status output in controller CLI may not represent actual status
bugs.symptoms: There is a rare possibility that the cluster status output in the controller CLI may not display the actual cluster status in the chassis.
bugs.conditions: There is a timing case where stale values for the cluster status are written to the confd database on startup and are not refreshed when actual values are available.
bugs.impact: User will see an incorrect cluster state.
bugs.workaround: User can issue a controller failover and that will update to the correct cluster status within confd

bugs.title: The dbus-daemon SIGSEGV causes NetworkManager communication failures leading to Vcc-host-config issues
bugs.symptoms: The dbus-daemon SIGSEGV causes NetworkManager communication failures leading to Vcc-host-config issues.
bugs.conditions: The dbus daemon should crashed or restarted.
bugs.impact: Communication failures leading to Vcc-host-config issues.
bugs.workaround: Restart NetworkManager.service.
bugs.fix: Issue has been fixed.

bugs.title: Tenant image upload silently fails
bugs.symptoms: In some scenarios extra disk space is required for a tenant image. If there is enough space to upload the image, but not enough extra space, the operation will silently fail.
bugs.conditions: Enough disk space available to upload a tenant image, but not enough to copy it.
bugs.impact: Silent failure when uploading a tenant image.
bugs.workaround: Clear disk space by removing old tenant images, or resize the images volume.

bugs.title: Tenant image uploads are failing without error notifications, despite sufficient available storage.
bugs.symptoms: In some scenarios extra disk space is required for a tenant image. If there is enough space to upload the image, but not enough extra space, the operation will silently fail.
bugs.conditions: There is sufficient disk space to upload the tenant image; however, there is not enough space to copy it.
bugs.impact: Silent failure when uploading a tenant image.
bugs.workaround: Clear disk space by removing old tenant images, or resize the images volume.

bugs.title: Stale USB drive entry remains in show components after USB removal on VELOS
bugs.symptoms: After a USB drive is removed, show components may still display the removed USB disk entry (for example sda DataTraveler) even though lsusb, lsblk, and platform-hal GET:drives no longer show it.
bugs.conditions: On VELOS systems, a USB drive was previously attached to a controller and then removed; stale drive data may remain shown in show components.
bugs.impact: Show components can report stale storage information, which may mislead operators about currently attached USB devices.

bugs.title: PlatformStatsBridge crash on VELOS due to malformed SNMP requests
bugs.symptoms: Multiple PlatformStatsBridge core dumps observed on VELOS controller and partition.
bugs.conditions: Occurs when the system receives malformed or out-of-range SNMP queries, such as those generated by misconfigured monitoring scripts (e.g., Zabbix integration).
bugs.impact: PlatformStatsBridge process crashes, generating core files. No impact to production traffic or overall VELOS system health reported.
bugs.workaround: Ensure SNMP monitoring tools send only valid and supported OIDs. Review and correct any custom SNMP scripts or templates to avoid malformed queries. No further action required if scripts are compliant; issue does not affect production service.

bugs.title: Ports 7100 and 7200 Exposed, Allowing Remote Console Access via Management Network
bugs.symptoms: Ports 7100 and 7200, used for internal console access between controllers, are remotely accessible over the management network. This can lead to potential unauthorized access to the controllers.
bugs.impact: Unauthorized access to the controller's console using exposed ports.
bugs.fix: Ports 7100 and 7200 are included in the controller allowlist, which allows adding allowed-IP rules for these ports.

bugs.title: Memory leak in confd-key-migrationd when frequently retrieving primary key data
bugs.symptoms: The confd-key-migrationd process experiences a slow memory leak.
bugs.conditions: - primary-key state is frequently retrieved via 'show system aaa' or 'show system aaa primary-key state'. - Equivalent API endpoints such as '/restconf/data/openconfig-system:system/aaa' can also trigger the leak.
bugs.impact: The resident size of the confd-key-migrationd process increases slowly over time, and may eventually exhaust system memory, resulting in OOM killer and system instability (typically after months of uptime).
bugs.workaround: Observe the resident size (RSS) of the confd-key-migrationd process with the following command: ps -o pid,vsz,rss,cmd -p $(pidof confd-key-migrationd) It is typically no more than ~20MB on a healthy system. Reboot the system or restart the confd-key-migration-mgr docker container to free up the memory, if needed: docker container restart confd-key-migration-mgr

bugs.title: Blades Reappear Under Default Partition After Downgrade When Default Partition Is Deleted
bugs.symptoms: After moving blades to the 'none' partition and deleting the default partition, blades unexpectedly reappear under the default partition after a downgrade from a 2.0.0 build to 1.8.2. Additionally, the system may show blades associated with the default partition even when the partition was previously removed.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when: -- Blades are moved to the 'none' partition -- The default partition is deleted -- The system is downgraded from a 2.0.0 build to 1.8.2 -- The fips-service restarts and detects only the 'none' partition
bugs.impact: Blades are incorrectly reassigned to the default partition, leading to an inconsistent system state and unexpected partition behavior. This may affect partition management workflows and system configuration integrity.
bugs.workaround: There is no direct workaround. Avoid deleting the default partition before downgrade, or ensure partition configuration is validated after downgrade.

bugs.title: [Windows AD] Secure LDAP / Basic LDAP is not working post toggling the active_directory flag True/False
bugs.symptoms: With Basic LDAP or Secure LDAP (LDAPS) integrated with Windows Active Directory, toggling the active_directory and unix_attributes flags causes LDAP authentication to stop working. Specifically: 1. The Windows AD Domain SID is not recreated after the toggle. 2. LDAP-authenticated users receive a 403 Forbidden error when accessing the REST API.
bugs.conditions: 1. F5OS-A/C is configured with Windows AD LDAP or Secure LDAP (LDAPS) authentication. 2. LDAP roles are mapped to AD groups using system aaa authentication roles. The active_directory flag is toggled from true -> false (and unix_attributes from false -> true), then toggled back.
bugs.impact: All remote LDAP users cannot authenticate via LDAP, and LDAP-authenticated users lose access to the management CLI and REST API.
bugs.fix: The issue is fixed on F5OS-2.0.0 and F5OS-A-1.8.4

bugs.title: Packet loss on a F5OS tenant when vlan-groups are in use
bugs.symptoms: On an F5OS tenant, there may be packet loss when vlan-groups are in use. This occurs due to high churn inside the FDB table due to MAC addresses being learned between different host ports resulting in temporary DLF drops while the MAC is learned on the new port.
bugs.conditions: - BX520 blade - VLAN groups - A large amount of unique MAC addresses in the FDB table
bugs.impact: Packet loss. Failing monitor probes.
bugs.workaround: Monitor probe issues may be alleviated by creating a static FDB entry for the local admin bit flipped MAC address that TMM is egressing packets from.
bugs.fix: Enable service-DAG when learning host generated MAC addresses to eliminate port-motion events between host ports.

bugs.title: Console Shows Kernel Warning Messages While Copying Image to USB Drive
bugs.symptoms: When using the "F5 rSeries Systems: Installation and Upgrade" guide, https://techdocs.f5.com/en-us/f5os-a-1-5-3/f5-rseries-systems-installation-upgrade/title-install-upgrade-software.html, and following the instructions to "Create a bootable USB flash drive", warning messages from the Linux kernel may appear on the console output. Messages may be similar to the following: - INFO: task smartctl:1090100 blocked for more than 120 seconds. - Tainted: G OE -------- - - 4.18.0-553.109.1.f5.1.1.10.el8_10.x86_64 #1 These messages are benign, and the file copy will still complete successfully.
bugs.conditions: Running F5OS v2.0.0 and creating a bootable USB drive.
bugs.impact: Kernel warning messages may appear.
bugs.workaround: Add the following to the end of the dd command: "oflag=direct"

bugs.title: “Error: application communication failure” after aborting system image check-version-fips / set-version-fips
bugs.symptoms: When running system image check-version-fips iso-version <version> (and in some cases system image set-version-fips), the CLI may return: Error: application communication failure
bugs.conditions: Occurs when system image check-version-fips (or set-version-fips) is aborted or times out and the command is re-run immediately (within ~10–20 seconds), especially when the check takes several minutes to complete.
bugs.impact: Image compatibility verification may fail with Error: application communication failure.
bugs.workaround: Avoid aborting system image check-version-fips once started; allow it to complete. If the command is aborted or you see Error: application communication failure, wait 10–20 seconds before re-issuing check-version-fips / set-version-fips.

bugs.title: Unexpected Controller Switchover Observed While Copying Image to USB Drive Using dd Command
bugs.symptoms: On the active controller, copying the image to the USB controller triggers the controller switchover to standby.
bugs.conditions: -- Install the latest 2.0 iso on the chassis. -- On active controller, perform iso copy on USB using the dd command. example: dd if=<file.iso> of=/dev/sda bs=1M -- Active controller will switch to standby mode.
bugs.impact: The system will be unresponsive for some time (~200 sec). ConfD will be switched over to the standby controller.
bugs.workaround: Use oflag=direct flag with dd command: example: dd if=<file.iso> oflag=direct of=/dev/sda bs=1M

bugs.title: Port mismatch between images imported on both common controllers
bugs.symptoms: The service registry port assignment for the imported image is different in both common controllers.
bugs.conditions: The port assigned to a services registry for an imported image is different on both common controllers
bugs.impact: Will impact bringing up of cluster service pods.
bugs.workaround: Trigger a switch over of CC mode, this would sync the port assignments of imported images among common controllers.

bugs.title: Kernel Panic Occurs While Accessing page_private Data During Writeback
bugs.symptoms: System crashes with kernel panic during filesystem writeback
bugs.conditions: Occurs when hardware or drivers (e.g., RDMA/DMA) write directly to file-backed pages pinned with get_user_pages() (GUP), bypassing normal filesystem write paths, so the filesystem is unaware of the changes
bugs.impact: Kernel panic/system crash
bugs.fix: Kernel upgraded

bugs.title: The module-communication-error not clearing post-recovery
bugs.symptoms: A shared commError flag in the VPC and VFC health monitoring tasks caused a race condition when tracking communication errors across controllers.
bugs.conditions: A shared commError flag caused a race condition where a communication error in one PSU controller could be incorrectly cleared by another PSU controller, leaving the original controller's error uncleared even after recovery.
bugs.impact: This led to scenarios where a module communication error status was not cleared even after recovery.
bugs.workaround: Restart diag-agent using the below command docker restart diag-agent
bugs.fix: Fixed Communication Error not clearing for recovered modules

bugs.title: Platform-diag-agent process consuming more memory
bugs.symptoms: The diag-agent service running on the service seems to consuming more memory over the time due to runtime memory leaks leading OOM on system.
bugs.conditions: The diag-agent services receiving a burst of events at a time, leading to its queues being filled up with too many entries and raising the memory.
bugs.impact: Over the long time, if diag-agent receives event bursts again and again the service would end up consuming more memory from DUT.
bugs.workaround: If diag-agent service memory raised too much, restarting the diag-agent service before any OOM would free up the memory of device.
bugs.fix: Provided fix for few identified leaks in diag-agent event queue.

bugs.title: TX_Enable Not Set for Lanes 2-4 After Hot-Swapping 400G Optic on BX520 Front Panel Port in 4x100G Bifurcated Mode
bugs.symptoms: Upon optic re-insertion in 4x100G mode on BX520 blades, there is an issue in MAC enable for lanes 2 to 4. For example, if port 3/2 is in 4x100G mode and the optic is hot-swapped, then the MAC will be enabled only for the first link 3/2.1 and not for 3/2.2-2.4.
bugs.conditions: On a BX520 blade, the front panel port is in bifurcated mode (4x100G), and the optic is hot-swapped (removed and re-inserted).
bugs.impact: The issue in MAC enable for lanes 2 to 4 will cause an issue when sending out the egress packets on lanes 2 to 4 of the port.
bugs.workaround: Admin bounce of ALL interfaces will help facilitate a clean link-up. Administratively disable the 4x100G interfaces before removing the optic. Then remove and re-insert the optic. Then re-enable the interfaces.

bugs.title: Device Reboot Delayed During Port-Profile Changes
bugs.symptoms: On the R2R4 device, the system undergoes a reboot when port profiles are being changed. With new NAC FW support added in 2.0.0, system reboot will be delayed by 2-3 mins as changing the port-profiles needs more time.
bugs.conditions: When port-profiles are changed on R2R4 device.
bugs.impact: Device reboot will be delayed for 2-3 mins.
bugs.workaround: NA

bugs.title: Orchestration Manager crash when partition configured with mgmt-vlans
bugs.symptoms: The Orchestration Manager (OMD) process crashes and restarts when a partition is configured with mgmt-vlans.
bugs.conditions: - Partition configured with mgmt-vlans, e.g. "mgmt-vlans untagged". - The mgmt-vlans added to an existing partition.
bugs.impact: - The Orchestration Manager process crashes and restarts. - Cluster data is unavailable during the restart.
bugs.workaround: Create partition without "mgmt-vlans", or remove from existing partition: conf no partitions partition <partition> config mgmt-vlans commit

bugs.title: Cluster Health Degradation and Tenant Offline Due to High Disk Usage
bugs.symptoms: When file system usage exceeds 95%, k3s initiates pod eviction and internal garbage collection in an attempt to free disk space by removing unused pods. This action can cause all pods—including the tenant—to enter a non-functional or failed state, resulting in the tenant going offline. Recovery of file storage alone does not automatically restore cluster or tenant health; automated recovery is not triggered upon clearing disk space.
bugs.conditions: File system (disk) usage increases to 95% or above.
bugs.impact: Tenant and potentially all pods within the cluster become unavailable/offline. Restoration of disk space does not automatically recover affected cluster and tenant components.
bugs.workaround: Manual intervention is required for full recovery. As the root user, trigger cluster re-installation by running: -- touch /var/omd/CLUSTER_REINSTALL

bugs.title: [R2K/4K] - TMM restarts are observed on the tenant startup as part of VF initialisations
bugs.symptoms: TMM restarts with following errors in /var/log/tmm localhost.localdomain notice xnet[12:00.0]: Error: Unable to attach to xnet dev localhost.localdomain notice xnet(1.8)[12:00.0]: Error: Unable to initialize device
bugs.conditions: During tenant launch or startup on the latest F5OS 2.0 builds.
bugs.impact: TMM restarts are seen only during it's startup. This might cause a little tenant readiness delay. There are no runtime or traffic impacts.
bugs.workaround: NA

bugs.title: Kubelet log flood: "orphaned pod ... failed to remove volume ... directory not empty" for Tenant ConfigMap Volumes After Reboot
bugs.symptoms: On F5OS-A systems, kubelet may continuously log errors similar to the following every ~2 seconds: orphaned pod "<pod-uuid>" found, but failed to remove volume at path /var/lib/kubelet/pods/<pod-uuid>/volumes/kubernetes.io~configmap/<tenant>-configmap: remove ...: directory not empty This log flood occurs when the kubelet is unable to clean up the configmap volume directory for an orphaned tenant pod
bugs.conditions: -- F5OS-A version 1.5.x or 1.8.x (including 1.8.3) on rSeries platforms -- The tenant pod is orphaned after a reboot (old pod replaced by a new pod for the same tenant) -- The configmap volume directory for the old pod retains its standard Kubernetes content (timestamped data subdirectory, ..data symlink, and key symlinks)
bugs.impact: -- Continuous error log messages in /var/log/messages (approximately one every two seconds) -- No functional impact to running tenants; the issue is cosmetic/operational (log noise) -- Manual intervention may be required to clean up the stale directory
bugs.workaround: Manually delete the stale configmap directory for the orphaned pod using standard Linux file removal commands (e.g., rm -rf) Note: Ensure the directory is not in use by any active pod before removal
bugs.fix: This issue is fixed in F5OS 2.0 and later, which incorporate improved cleanup logic from upstream Kubernetes. For F5OS-A 1.8.x and 1.5.x, a dedicated fix is being tracked under this bug.

bugs.title: [R2R4] Misleading Estimated Reboot Count Displayed in ConfD During Upgrade to Version 2.0.0
bugs.symptoms: When Live upgrade is triggered, confd shows the estimated reboots required as 2 reboots. Since the R2R4 device undergoes an NAC FW upgrade in F5OS v2.0.0 (which requires 2 reboots to complete the FW upgrade), the total number of reboots required is 3
bugs.conditions: When the Live upgrade is triggered to 2.0.0
bugs.impact: No Functionality impact

bugs.title: No console log reports confirming the completion of the firmware upgrade.
bugs.symptoms: No logs reported on console notifying that the firmware upgrade has been completed. The status can still be tracked via "show components component properties".
bugs.conditions: After the firmware upgrade, the console does not log any Firmware upgrade completion.
bugs.impact: No alert on the console to notify about firmware upgrade completion.
bugs.workaround: Upgrade status can be checked via confd, checking for "show components component properties"

bugs.title: Supported optic reports UNKNOWN state after upgrade
bugs.symptoms: After a system upgrade, a supported optic may report its state as UNKNOWN even though the system supports it.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when optics are inserted in the system before a live upgrade.
bugs.impact: For any optics that require specific tuning values, they will not be applied and may result in unexpected or inconsistent behavior.
bugs.workaround: Remove and reinsert the affected optic, or reboot the device.
bugs.fix: The optics-mgr process was timing out before it could retrieve optic data. The timeout period has been extended to allow the system to complete the data request.

bugs.title: Upgrade Failure due to OStree rebase to version failure
bugs.symptoms: "show system image" upgrade status as failed.
bugs.conditions: ostree fsck --repo=/var/export/chassis/ostree/controller/repo show report error.
bugs.impact: Upgrade failed , system will be down.
bugs.workaround: 1) Delete the imported ISO ref from remote repo. ostree refs --delete 1.8.3-31494 --repo=/var/export/chassis/ostree/controller/repo 2) Verify the ref has been removed: [root@controller-1:Waiting for ConfD ~]# ostree refs --repo=/var/export/chassis/ostree/controller/repo 2.0.0-22818 3)prune the deleted objects: ostree prune --repo=/var/export/chassis/ostree/controller/repo --refs-only Total objects: 130015 Deleted 49731 objects, 2.5 GB freed 4) reboot the controller. reboot 5) after boot check the ostree health : ostree fsck --repo=/var/export/chassis/ostree/controller/repo 6) abort the current upgrade: In confd config : [root@controller-2:Active ~]# su - admin Last login: Wed May 20 10:25:10 UTC 2026 on ttyS0 Welcome to the F5OS System Controller Management CLI admin connected from 127.0.0.1 using console on syscon-2-active syscon-2-active# config Entering configuration mode terminal syscon-2-active(config)# system image install-abort 7) wait for system image status to become aborted.

bugs.title: The 'show system health' API fails due to a communication failure
bugs.symptoms: The confd endpoint's 'show system health' API invocation fails as the callpointer is not registered by the respective service.
bugs.conditions: The diag-agent service is stuck in an infinite loop while registering the callpoint (either show system health or any other API) due to some race condition hit leading to the respective confd endpoint failing.
bugs.impact: The specific confd endpoint for which registration is stuck would fail. In this case, the "show system health components component" fails and the respective health info is missing for the GUI too.
bugs.workaround: Restart the diag-agent service to perform the registration again, and the confd endpoint invocation succeeds.

bugs.title: Tenant configuration is reset during F5OS v2.0 baremetal to 1.x downgrade
bugs.symptoms: After performing a live downgrade from a bare-metal (PXE/USB) installed F5OS-A 2.0.0 system to F5OS-A 1.x, deployed tenants appear factory-reset.
bugs.conditions: The system was initially installed via PXE or USB with F5OS-A v2.0 A live (OSTree-based) downgrade is performed to F5OS-A 1.x One or more tenants were deployed and configured prior to the downgrade
bugs.impact: Tenant disk storage is mounted on the wrong volume group instead of the dedicated partition_tenant volume (293 GB). This results in tenant configuration loss and significantly reduced tenant storage capacity.
bugs.workaround: Before triggering the downgrade from F5OS-A v2.0 to 1.x, run the following command on the appliance to manually add the fstab entry: grep -q '/var/F5/system/cbip-disks' /etc/fstab || echo "/dev/partition_tenant/root /var/F5/system/cbip-disks ext4 defaults,nofail 0 0" >> /etc/fstab

bugs.title: Kernel panic reboot observed on r2000 and r4000-series appliances while upgrading
bugs.symptoms: An intermittent issue seen when NAC Firmware upgrade is in progress after Live upgrading r2000 and r4000-series appliances to 2.0 versions. A kernel core dump from ice driver is observed which results in intermittent reboot of the system and prompt Status or GUI status is stuck in "Firmware upgrade in-progress".
bugs.conditions: - F5 r2000- or r4000-series appliance - Upgrading from F5OS 1.x to F5OS 2.0 for the first time.
bugs.impact: prompt Status or webUI status gets stuck in "Firmware upgrade in-progress" after upgrading to 2.0 Version from 1.X version
bugs.workaround: If "Firmware upgrade in-progress" prompt status is seen for longer duration and no upgrades are in progress in backgroup, follow the below steps to recover the device 1) Do system reboot. 2) After the device is up and running, check if all the services are up and stable ( still "Firmware upgrade in-progress" is observed), restart diag-agent container. Command : "system diagnostics os-utils docker restart node platform service diag-agent"
bugs.fix: Issue Fixed.

bugs.title: Installation failure at anaconda shell during bare metal
bugs.symptoms: During bare metal installation via USB, the process errors in anaconda shell at RAID creation with an issue in RAID partition.
bugs.conditions: System with dual SSDs and installation perfomed via USB.
bugs.impact: Image installation failure.
bugs.workaround: Run a disk cleanup using F5 Disk Erase utility at the start of installation during boot up. Please follow below steps -> Reboot the System: Type 'reboot' in serial console. -> Launch Utility: During boot, press 'e' when prompted to launch the F5 Disk Erase Utility. -> Confirm Operation: Select 'Continue' when warned about permanent data loss. -> Select Drives: Choose the drives to erase from the menu. -> Confirm Erase: Select 'Erase-All-Data' to confirm. -> Complete Operation: After erasure, choose to erase another drive or select Exit to reboot.

bugs.title: Remote logging with TLS based authentication will not be supported on IP based host.
bugs.symptoms: With the rsyslog-ossl package, the IP-based permittedpeer authentication method is not supported for IP address verification using the CN and SAN fields.
bugs.conditions: When remote logging server is configured with the IP address with TLS auth enabled instead of hostname or FQDN of server.
bugs.impact: Remote logging feature will not work.
bugs.workaround: Use hostname based cert and server for remote logging. Hostname should be configured on server and in certificate as CN and in SAN as Domain name.

bugs.title: Memory leak in user_manager when remote LDAP authentication binds fail
bugs.symptoms: When remote LDAP authentication is configured and LDAP bind attempts fail, user_manager leaks memory handles on each failed attempt. Symptoms include: - Host platform memory steadily depletes over time. - Repeated error messages in system logs (authentication-mgr / var/log/messages): Trying SASL bind with bindDN <DN> SASL bind error: -1 'Can't contact LDAP server' - Eventually, host memory becomes fully exhausted, triggering the Linux kernel Out-Of-Memory (OOM) killer. - Host management interfaces (SSH, WebUI, and serial console) become inaccessible, and running tenant instances become unresponsive or freeze.
bugs.conditions: - Remote LDAP authentication is configured (system aaa authentication config authentication-method includes LDAP_ALL). - The configured LDAP server is unreachable, rejects bind credentials, or encounters a protocol/port misconfiguration (e.g., global "ssl on" configured against plaintext port 389). - Background polling (AAA_Poller) repeatedly attempts to bind to the LDAP server to synchronize role mappings.
bugs.impact: Available host platform memory is exhausted over time, leading to kernel Out-Of-Memory (OOM) conditions, total loss of host management access, tenant disruption, and requiring a hard power cycle/reboot of the appliance.
bugs.workaround: To halt the memory leak, eliminate the failed bind attempts using either of the following methods: 1. Correct the LDAP configuration or network reachability so binds succeed: - Ensure the server is reachable and credentials are valid. - Resolve any protocol conflicts (e.g., if using SSL, use port 636 with "ssl on"; if using port 389, configure "ssl start_tls" or "ssl off"). - Remove any duplicate or conflicting server-groups: config no system aaa server-groups server-group <duplicate_group> commit 2. Temporarily switch authentication back to local accounts until LDAP service is restored: config system aaa authentication config authentication-method [ LOCAL ] commit

bugs.title: Downgrade from F5OS v2.0 release to older releases(1.8.x) is blocked, when RADIUS/TACACS Server Group Secret Keys Are Configured
bugs.symptoms: Attempting to downgrade from F5OS v2.0 to any older versions of F5OS-A or F5OS-C will fails with the following error: "Cannot downgrade to a version that does not support AES-encrypted RADIUS or TACACS server group secret keys. Please remove all RADIUS and TACACS server group secret keys and retry."
bugs.conditions: 1. RADIUS or TACACS+ server-group secret keys are configured in versions less than F5OS v2.0. 2. Upgrade to F5OS v2.0 (all build numbers) on F5 rSeries and VELOS Chassis. 3. Attempting to downgrade to any older versions of F5OS-A or F5OS-C.
bugs.impact: Downgrade is blocked until all RADIUS and TACACS server-group secret keys are manually removed.
bugs.workaround: Before downgrading, manually remove all RADIUS and TACACS+ server group configurations. After the downgrade is complete, reconfigure these settings as needed. Please note that once the RADIUS and TACACS+ server group configurations are removed, remote authentication will be unavailable. Administrators must use local accounts during and after the downgrade to restore RADIUS and TACACS+ server groups and secrets. Step-by-step instructions for efficient restoration of RADIUS and TACACS+ server group configurations: 1. Perform a configuration backup before upgrading to the F5OS v2.0. 2. Upgrade to F5OS v2.0 version. 3. Before downgrading, remove the RADIUS and TACACS+ server group configurations, then proceed with the downgrade. 4. After successful downgrade, restore the configuration. 5. Reboot the system.
bugs.fix: NA

bugs.title: RR-DAG issue when L4 source port = destination port
bugs.symptoms: RRDAG uses a protocol CAM to identify packet metadata to "hash" in Round Robin mode. A new RR-DAG feature added the capability for the packet metadata hash to match on L4 DPort in the Protocol CAM. There is an issue in the FPGA feature implementation of both sDAG and eDAG where the L4 DPort presented to the Protocol CAM is forced to zero if the packet had DPort=SPort. Because of the bug, packets would use the wrong disaggregation hash when the DPort=SPort since it wouldn't match the CAM entry.
bugs.conditions: Running RR-DAG and L4 source port == destination port.
bugs.impact: Packets sent to the wrong CPU service destination. RR-DAG packet distribution is unbalanced.
bugs.workaround: This issue an FPGA feature implementation defect. Fix requires a SW update with new FPGA bitfiles.
bugs.fix: The fix requires FPGA bitfile updates targeted at F5OS v2.0.1.

bugs.title: K3s cluster installation fails on one controller after live upgrade from 1.8.x to 2.1.0
bugs.symptoms: After a live upgrade from F5OS-C 1.8.x to 2.0.0, one controller fails to join the cluster. Blades may also fails to join the cluster. One of the Controller and blades remain in "Not In Cluster" state.
bugs.conditions: Live upgrade from F5OS-C 1.8.x to 2.0.0, where a controller fail to join the cluster.
bugs.impact: Cluster services are degraded. Only one controller participates in the cluster, and all blades(nodes) fail to join the cluster. Tenants cannot be deployed until the cluster is fully operational.
bugs.workaround: Trigger a cluster reinstall from the active controller. "touch /var/omd/CLUSTER_REINSTALL"

bugs.title: DMA-Agent crashes while trying to disable a Service Endpoint (SEP) that is already disabled
bugs.symptoms: The DMA-Agent process crashes with an assertion failure ("Assertion Failed: FALSE"), causing ATSE data movers to stop unexpectedly. Affected tenants may become unresponsive or experience a service interruption. The crash occurs after an SEP (Service Endpoint) has been successfully enabled and a subsequent disable operation is issued against a SEP that is already in a disabled state.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs on F5OS v2.1.0 across all supported platforms. The condition is triggered when the DMA-Agent receives a request to disable an SEP that has already been disabled. For example, during tenant lifecycle operations or automated service recovery sequences where redundant disable commands may be issued against the same SEP.
bugs.impact: When this issue is triggered, the DMA-Agent crashes and all associated ATSE data movers are stopped, resulting in a loss of tenant data-plane traffic processing. This is a critical-severity issue that can cause an unplanned tenant outage requiring manual intervention or a service restart to restore normal operation.
bugs.workaround: No workaround available. If the crash occurs, restart the DMA-Agent and affected tenants to restore service. Avoid initiating rapid or repeated tenant disable operations in close succession to reduce the likelihood of encountering this issue.

bugs.title: F5 rSeries ASW firmware v71.6.5.00
bugs.symptoms: F5 rSeries ASW firmware v71.6.5.00
bugs.conditions: F5 rSeries system
bugs.impact: Not applicable.
bugs.workaround: Fixes issues with RRDAG. See ID2337865 for more information.

bugs.title: F5 rSeries ASW firmware v71.6.5.11
bugs.symptoms: F5 rSeries ASW firmware v71.6.5.11
bugs.conditions: F5 rSeries system

bugs.title: Users unable to authenticate via the F5OS GUI/API when using LDAP
bugs.symptoms: - External users are unable to authenticate via the F5OS GUI/API. - The external-authenticator process crashes and generates a core file: Core-helper.Appliance: priority="Err" msgid="0x6501000000000001" msg="Core dumped on Appliance" process="external-authen" location="/var/shared/core/container/core.system_manager.external-authenticator.1468325.1783541684.core.gz"
bugs.conditions: - An Active Directory LDAP environment that broadly does not have unix attributes allocated. - Users are in many non-F5OS security groups that don't have a gidNumber associated with them.
bugs.impact: Unable to authenticate via the F5OS GUI/API
bugs.workaround: Setting an ldap-group on relevant roles, and then setting "unix attributes" to false.

bugs.title: Tenant image or F5OS ISO upload fails with "Copy failed" error in the GUI
bugs.symptoms: When uploading a tenant image or F5OS ISO via the GUI file utility, the upload fails with a "Copy Failed" error message. Logs for utils-agent show: msg="file upload error" error="Failed to move file to destination path" msg="File change path failed, so deleting the uploaded file."
bugs.conditions: User attempts to upload tenant image or F5OS ISO using the GUI file utility feature
bugs.impact: Admin cannot upload tenant images or F5OS ISO files via the GUI. Uploaded file is automatically deleted by the system after the failed move operation.
bugs.workaround: You may select one of the following options below: 1. Use GUI Import instead of Upload — In the F5OS GUI, use the Import function (import via URL from an accessible repository) rather than Upload. 2. Use SCP to push the file directly to the F5OS system.
bugs.fix: Tenant or F5OS ISO images successfully upload.

bugs.title: The k3s service may crash with a nil pointer dereference in flannel VXLAN during prolonged host stalls or heavy I/O
bugs.symptoms: panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference [signal SIGSEGV: segmentation violation code=0x1 addr=0x... pc=0x...] goroutine ... [running]: github.com/flannel-io/flannel/pkg/backend/vxlan.(*network).watchVXLANDevice(...) .../pkg/backend/vxlan/vxlan_network.go:...
bugs.conditions: While running F5OS-A 2.0.x on an rSeries appliance, the host experiences significant resource exhaustion, severe disk I/O latency, or temporary system stalls. During the stall, Netlink event delivery is delayed or disrupted while flannel's watchVXLANDevice() routine processes VXLAN network interface state changes.
bugs.impact: The k3s process terminates abruptly and is restarted by systemd.
bugs.workaround: There is no proactive workaround to prevent the crash under severe host stalls. The k3s daemon automatically restarts via systemd and recovers the VXLAN overlay.

bugs.title: cloud-init chpasswd passwords are not masked when using hyphenated arrays
bugs.symptoms: Passwords available in the chpasswd.list could appear unmasked in the cloud-init processed-data output when the username/password entries used the hyphenated array format.
bugs.conditions: The user-data includes chpasswd.list as a YAML sequence, for example: chpasswd: list: - user1:abcd - user2:abcd expire: False
bugs.impact: Passwords could be exposed in the confd state data(using show cloud-inits) and cloud-init API output. The cloud-init password configuration itself continued to work.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: Fixed the issue.

bugs.title: FPGA datapath issue allows packets to be sent from host to network out of order
bugs.symptoms: Packets from the host to network are received out of order on BX520 blade.
bugs.conditions: This typically happens in higher congestion or burst traffic conditions. The min/max packet size mix shows this issue most often, but packets out of order do happen with other random packet size mixes.
bugs.impact: Specific impact to UDP packet flows. UDP packets out of order can cause quality of service issues in audio and video streams.
bugs.workaround: Workaround requires a software update that contains an FPGA bitfile update to fix the issue.
bugs.fix: The issue is in the Transmit Routing Engine (TRE) in the FPGA transmit datapath from host to network. Part of the TRE architecture splits the transmit datapath into 2 100G packet paths, each directed at a 100G MAC interface. The issue is in how the packet paths were split. The datapath architecture uses a tuple hash to ensure that all packets from a specific packet flow are directed down the same packet path. In this case, the hash was not applied correctly which allowed packets from a specific flow to run down both 100G datapaths, which creates a race condition. In lower congestion applications, the packets hold their order. In higher congestion or bursty applications with varying packet sizes, the packets can be received out of order.

bugs.title: EDR license entitlement may briefly display "Missing" in logs following a controller reboot
bugs.symptoms: After a controller reboots, the EDR Enablement License entitlement status logged by the system may briefly report "Missing," even though a valid EDR add-on license is installed and active. The log self-corrects to the proper entitlement state (Active or Expired) within sometime, with no further recurrence.
bugs.conditions: This is an intermittent, timing-related issue that can occur only on controller reboot when: 1.An EDR add-on license is installed on the system. 2.A supported third-party EDR sensor (e.g., CrowdStrike Falcon) is installed and running.
bugs.impact: This is a logging/display issue only — there is no functional or security impact. The EDR sensor continues running undisturbed throughout, and no license, entitlement, or sensor data is actually lost or altered. The only effect is a transient, inaccurate "Missing" entry in the logs immediately after reboot, which could momentarily mislead an administrator reviewing logs right after a reboot into thinking the EDR license isn't applied.
bugs.workaround: No action is required. The correct entitlement status (Active/Expired) is automatically logged in subsequent logs after reboot. If immediate confirmation is needed, check the current entitlement using the system's licensing display (show system licensing) rather than relying on the log entry generated during the reboot window.
bugs.fix: The entitlement status check has been updated to wait until the system has finished reading and processing the installed license at startup before logging the EDR entitlement state, ensuring only the accurate status is logged - eliminating the transient incorrect "Missing" entry on reboot.

bugs.title: Standby controller may not log the EDR entitlement "Active" status after a chassis power cycle
bugs.symptoms: After a full chassis power cycle, the standby controller may not produce an edr entitlement log entry at all — leaving no EDR entitlement status recorded for the standby controller.
bugs.conditions: Occurs intermittently following a full chassis-level power cycle on a system with: 1.A valid EDR add-on license installed. 2.CrowdStrike Falcon sensor installed and running on both controllers.
bugs.impact: Visibility/logging only — the EDR add-on license entitlement itself is unaffected and remains correctly active on both controllers; the sensor continues running normally. The only effect is that the standby controller's log does not show a confirming "EDR Enablement License Active" entry
bugs.workaround: Confirm the entitlement status directly via the system's licensing display (show system licensing) on the standby controller, which reflects the correct state independent of this logging gap. If the log entry is specifically needed, restart the Falcon sensor service on the affected standby (systemctl restart falcon-sensor.service) controller to trigger the correct entitlement log to be generated.
